records.title: Fallback experiment matrix + cost penalty catalog (working notes)
records.text:
Fallback experiment matrix + cost penalty catalog (working notes)

Context / what changed since the Confluence version
-----------------------------------------------
This is a working doc intended to supersede the older Confluence page for day-to-day ops.

Key updates vs. Confluence (note to reviewers):
- We standardized on p95 + error-rate for decision gates; p99 is still tracked but no longer the primary gate except for cross-region routing tests.
- Cross-region routing cost model updated: egress is now tracked per "GiB" from the provider bill and attributed back to request traces by sampled bytes (we can’t reliably infer from tokens alone).
- CLI note: "redwoodctl" commands are still mostly correct, but platform tooling is being migrated to "rfctl". Keep both until Q2.
- Added explicit "customer harm" metrics: support ticket rate + HTTP 429/5xx annotations for throttling experiments.

Overview
========

This document captures a reproducible experiment matrix for operator-driven fallback strategies and an associated cost-penalty catalog used to evaluate trade-offs between SLO preservation and unit economics across regional surges. Intended audience: platform operators, SREs, runtime engineers, and product engineers running controlled degradation experiments or designing automatic fallback policies.

Why this exists
---------------
- Fallbacks preserve SLOs during capacity scarcity or model regressions, but they can change cost, quality, and customer experience.
- Operators need a concise experiment plan with metrics, dashboard queries, and a cost penalty model to compare candidate strategies.
- We want a single template for telemetry, rollout/rollback steps, and decision criteria for productionizing fallbacks.

Goals and scope
---------------
- Goal: Repeatable experiment matrix yielding quantitative comparisons of: latency SLO retention, token-cost delta, quality regressions (evals), and operator intervention effort.
- Scope: Multiregion inference surface (hosted + dedicated), model variant fallbacks (quantized, smaller model families), routing degradations (regional drain, tenant throttling).
- Out of scope: Model training/data pipelines, legal/customer contract negotiation.

Definitions and abbreviations
----------------------------
- Fallback variant: Any alternative response path (e.g., primary model -> smaller model, cached response) used when the primary path is unavailable or overloaded.
- Cost penalty: Unit cost increase or revenue impact metric associated with using a fallback (e.g., tokens * $/token diff, egress, incremental infra).
- SLO preservation: Fraction of requests meeting the p95 latency target and error-rate SLO (tracked per region and tenant priority).

Experiment matrix (canonical)
-----------------------------
Columns: experiment_id | description | fallback_type | trigger | primary-metric | cost-metric | quality-metric | run-length | owner

Example rows (templates)
1) EXP-001 | Model-variant degrade (Llama-70B -> Llama-13B-int8) | model_variant | queue-depth > 120 OR p95 latency > 650ms | p95 latency, error-rate | token-cost-delta-per-hour | eval-regression@30 prompts | 2h | operator-team
2) EXP-002 | Regional drain to peer region (eu-west -> us-east) | regional-routing | region capacity throttle 85% | p99 tail latency cross-region | egress-cost-delta | user-visible-quality (latency jump) | 4h | platform-network
3) EXP-003 | Prefetch cache fallback (serve from prefix cache) | cache_prefetch | cold-start rate > 25 req/min | mean latency | compute-cost-savings | correctness mismatch ratio | 3h | runtime-team
4) EXP-004 | Token-budgeted throttling for low-priority tenants | quota_throttle | burst credits exhausted | p95 latency of high-priority | revenue-at-risk + support-load | customer-error-annotations | 6h | platform-ops

New rows being piloted (add if you run them)
5) EXP-005 | Partial streaming disable (force non-streaming responses) | response-mode | event-loop lag > 150ms | p95 latency, disconnect-rate | infra-cost-delta | CSAT proxy (thumbs down rate) | 2h | api-runtime
6) EXP-006 | Retrieval reduced context window (RAG: 12 chunks -> 6 chunks) | retrieval-degrade | vector DB p95 > 200ms | end-to-end p95 | token-savings | answer completeness rating | 4h | rag-platform

Telemetry and dashboarding recipe
--------------------------------
Create a dedicated experimental dashboard with the following panels per experiment run:
- SLO heatmap: p50/p95/p99 latency over time (per region, per tenant priority).
  - latency_p95{experiment_id="EXP-001"}
  - request_duration_seconds_bucket (histograms)
- Cost delta stream:
  - token_cost_rate{fallback_variant!=""}
  - egress_gib_rate{experiment_id="EXP-002"} (new; sourced from network collector + sampled trace attribution)
- Quality regression signal:
  - evaluation pass-rate across a held promptset (30–60 prompts) run every 15 minutes.
  - eval_pass_rate{promptset="fallback-30"}
- Operator interventions:
  - operator_rollbacks_total{experiment_id="EXP-001"}
  - operator_override_seconds_total{experiment_id="EXP-001"}
- Customer harm / UX signals (especially for throttles):
  - http_responses_total{code=~"429|5..",experiment_id="EXP-004"}
  - support_ticket_rate{tag="fallback"}
- Composite KPI panel: cost-penalty vs. SLO-preservation scatter plot for each variant.

Minimum instrumentation checklist
--------------------------------
1) Annotate requests with experiment_id and fallback_variant in trace metadata.
2) Emit fallback_reason counter in request pipeline.
3) Record per-request token accounting and model_version label.
4) Attach prompt-set id for synthetic eval traffic.
5) Ensure operator actions log into the incident system with experiment_id tag.
6) (New) For cross-region tests: emit egress bytes by src_region->dst_region at 1m resolution.

Cost penalty catalog (examples + notes)
--------------------------------------
Catalog rows: fallback_variant | per-token-diff | expected-throughput | hourly-cost-delta | rollback-cost-estimate | notes

Example entries (update these numbers when finance-eng confirms billing rates):
- L70B -> L13B-int8 | -$0.0018 / token (lower cost) | ~2k tokens/s | -$12.96 / hour per 1000 rps (rough) | negligible | quality drop on long-form + tool use
- L70B -> L34B | -$0.0007 / token | ~1.2k tokens/s | -$5.04 / hour per 1000 rps (rough) | negligible | smaller regression than int8 in our last eval
- cross-region-eu->us | egress: +$0.085 / GiB (bill) | N/A | +$160–$260 / hour at 1000 rps (depends on payload/streaming) | potential SLA credits | must watch p99 + disconnect-rate
- cached_prefix_response | -$0.001 / token (savings) | N/A | -$3.6 / hour per 1000 rps | risk of stale content | requires invalidation policy + allowlist
- quota-throttle-low | revenue-at-risk estimate (see calc) | depends on tenant mix | - | revenue-impact = avg_MRR_per_req * blocked_reqs + support_cost | requires customer comms plan

Notes to self / open questions on cost
- Token price basis: some teams want $/1M tokens instead of $/token. Leave formulas in token-native form; dashboard can show both.
- For streaming, payload size can dominate egress more than tokens. Need to keep measuring bytes/request, not guess.

Cost calculations (short formulas)
---------------------------------
- token_cost_delta_hourly = sum_over_requests(token_count * (cost_primary - cost_fallback)) per hour
- egress_delta_hourly = egress_gib * egress_rate_per_gib
- revenue_at_risk = blocked_requests * avg_revenue_per_request
- support_cost_proxy = (new_tickets * avg_handle_time_minutes * cost_per_minute)

Include these calculations in the dashboard as derived timeseries.

Experiment run playbook (step-by-step)
--------------------------------------
1) Planning (2–4 days)
   a) Define hypotheses (example): "model-variant fallback preserves p95 latency with <=5% quality regression and cost delta within $250/hr"
   b) Pick held promptset (30–60 prompts) and synthetic traffic profile matching customer mix.
   c) Create experiment_id, add telemetry tags and dashboard.
2) Preflight (1 day)
   a) Run synthetic traffic against fallback in staging and collect baseline metrics.
   b) Validate eval pass-rate and trace annotation.
   c) Pre-commit rollback playbook and test it in canary.
3) Execution (2–6 hours normally; up to 24 hours if capturing diurnal traffic)
   a) Apply experiment on small cohort (1% of traffic or single region).
   b) Monitor SLO panels and operator intervention panel.
   c) Escalate to oncall if p95 > target * 2 or error-rate increases > 2x baseline.
4) Ramp or rollback (decision gates)
   a) If cost-savings or SLO-preservation meet hypothesis -> ramp to 10% then 50% using pre-defined step intervals.
   b) If quality regression > threshold OR operator rollbacks > 1 -> rollback immediately, file incident.
5) Post-run analysis (within 48 hours)
   a) Populate experiment report template (see artifacts).
   b) Archive synthetic trace samples and evaluation results.

Rollback quick commands (examples)
---------------------------------
Keep both tool variants until migration completes.

- Immediate global rollback:
  - redwoodctl rollout cancel --experiment EXP-001 --force
  - rfctl rollout cancel --experiment EXP-001 --force

- Regional undo (eu-west):
  - redwoodctl routing set-region-weight --region eu-west --weight 1.0 --experiment EXP-001
  - rfctl routing set-region-weight --region eu-west --weight 1.0 --experiment EXP-001

- Re-enable primary model:
  - redwoodctl model set-default --model redwood/llama-70b --variant baseline --experiment EXP-001
  - rfctl model set-default --model redwood/llama-70b --variant baseline --experiment EXP-001

Operator note: verify RBAC scopes before running rollback under incident stress.

Decision criteria matrix (accept/ramp/abandon)
----------------------------------------------
These are the current suggested gates (not absolute; document deviations in the report):
- Accept: p95 latency within 10% of baseline AND eval regression <= 3% AND hourly cost delta within budgeted threshold AND no sustained increase in 429/5xx.
- Ramp: p95 within 15% and eval regression <= 6% with operator + product approval.
- Abandon: p95 > 20% degradation OR eval regression > 10% OR customer harm signals spike (tickets/429s) OR unexpected safety regressions.

Artifacts to capture and store
------------------------------
- Experiment report (.md): hypothesis, traffic profile, duration, metrics before/after, cost calcs, operator notes.
- Trace bundle (S3 link) and synthetic eval outputs (json).
- Dashboard snapshot and Prometheus queries used.
- Postmortem if rollback occurred.

Operational responsibilities and ownership
-----------------------------------------
- Owner: platform-ops (primary contact: oncall@platform) for run coordination.
- Instrumentation: runtime-team for trace + metric changes.
- Cost modeling: finance-eng liaison for hourly cost validation.
- Security review: security-team if any customer data is used in synthetic prompts.

Safety and customer communication
--------------------------------
- For tenant-facing throttles/degradations that materially impact SLAs, coordinate with Customer Success for banner messaging and QBR notes.
- For enterprise Dedicated/Private deployments, require explicit sign-off per customer SLAs before ramping.

Retrospective template (post-experiment)
---------------------------------------
1) Summary: one-paragraph outcome
2) Metrics: baseline vs experiment (latency, error-rate, cost, eval pass-rate, customer harm)
3) What went well
4) What failed / surprises
5) Action items (owner + due date)
6) Decision: accept/ramp/abandon

Appendix A: sample PromQL snippets
---------------------------------
- p95 latency:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference",experiment_id=~"EXP-.*"}[5m])) by (le, region))
- fallback rate:
  sum(rate(fallback_reason_total[1m])) by (fallback_variant)
- 429/5xx rate:
  sum(rate(http_responses_total{code=~"429|5..",experiment_id=~"EXP-.*"}[5m])) by (code, region)

Appendix B: experiment ticket checklist (copy/paste)
---------------------------------------------------
- Experiment ID:
- Owner:
- Hypothesis:
- Synthetic promptset id:
- Baseline run links:
- Dashboard link:
- Rollback commands verified (redwoodctl/rfctl): Y/N
- Customer communication required: Y/N
- Egress attribution required (cross-region only): Y/N

Appendix C: change log (working doc)
------------------------------------
- 2026-01-22: Copied core content from Confluence page; started working notes version (Aisha).
- 2026-02-11: Updated triggers (queue-depth/p95), added customer harm metrics + rfctl migration note (Miguel).
- 2026-02-27: Updated egress cost modeling to GiB-based billing + trace sampling attribution (Dana).
- 2026-03-08: Added EXP-005/EXP-006 pilots and tightened decision gates (Aisha + Priya).

Where to ask questions
----------------------
- #platform-ops for run coordination
- #runtime-inference for instrumentation changes
- Finance-eng office hours for cost rate confirmation

records.text:
Private Release Gating & Change Management Policy

## Purpose
This policy defines the **minimum required gates** and **change-management workflow** for shipping Redwood Private releases (VPC and on-prem/air-gapped). The goal is to make upgrades **safe by default**, reduce upgrade-related incidents, and ensure we produce **auditable artifacts** (plan, prechecks, backup/restore status, approvals, and communications).

This page is normative. Teams may add stricter checks; exceptions require formal approval (see “Exceptions”).

## Scope
Applies to:
- Redwood Private control plane + data plane releases shipped via:
  - `redwood-private-installer` upgrade workflows
  - Helm chart updates (`redwood-helm-charts`)
  - Terraform module updates (`redwood-terraform`) impacting version pinning or artifact sources
  - Platform version compatibility/policy updates in `redwood`

Does not apply to:
- Redwood hosted API releases
- Pure documentation-only releases

## Definitions
- **Private release**: A versioned set of artifacts (installer, charts, images, migrations, compatibility policy) intended for customer-managed environments.
- **Upgrade plan**: A generated, persisted, auditable plan describing staged steps, required artifacts, dependencies, and rollback entry points.
- **N-1 → N**: Supported default upgrade path for initial GA. (Multi-hop may be supported case-by-case.)
- **Blocking precheck**: Must pass to proceed. Failure requires remediation or approved exception.
- **Warning precheck**: Does not block, but must be acknowledged in the change record.
- **Change record**: Single source of truth for a planned customer upgrade (internal ticket + attached artifacts).

## Policy summary (required gates)
A Private release or customer change event may proceed only if all of the following are satisfied:
1) **Supported upgrade path** is enforced by compatibility policy (default: N-1 → N).
2) **Upgrade plan** is generated and stored (no “imperative-only” upgrades).
3) **Blocking prechecks** pass.
4) **Backup** completes successfully (or an approved alternative is documented).
5) **Approval gates** are completed (Release Engineering + SRE; Security as required by risk score).
6) **Customer communications** are sent per risk score and timeline.
7) **Rollback readiness** is verified (rollback command available, rollback hooks present, post-rollback checks defined).
8) **Auditability** requirements are met (installer logs + audit events retained, support bundle includes upgrade traces).

## Roles and responsibilities
### Required approvers
- **Release Engineering (required)**: validates release artifact integrity, CI evidence, and packaging.
  - Default: Connor O’Brien (delegate: Devon Price)
- **SRE (required)**: validates operational safety, monitoring/alerting, rollback readiness.
  - Default: Sean Gallagher (delegate: Rafael Mendes)

### Conditional reviewers (by risk score)
- **Security/Compliance (conditional)**: required for regulated environments, backup/restore changes, audit event schema changes, or any change involving secrets/KMS.
  - Default: Naomi Feldman / Marcus Lin
- **Infrastructure (conditional)**: required for changes impacting storage backends, networking, or cluster requirements.
  - Default: Irene Choi / Victor Alvarez

## Risk scoring (customer environment)
Use the following rubric to determine communication timelines, approvals, and additional safeguards.

### Risk score = Impact (1–3) + Complexity (1–3) + Environment sensitivity (1–3)
- **Impact**
  - 1: Control-plane-only minor patch, no migrations, no Helm ordering changes
  - 2: Rolling restart of data plane or minor migration, expected <5 min disruption to management operations
  - 3: Schema migrations, control-plane/data-plane sequencing changes, or any change with potential inference impact
- **Complexity**
  - 1: Single component update, no dependency changes
  - 2: Multiple components, Helm hooks/order changes, or new prechecks
  - 3: New backup mechanism, rollback semantics change, or artifact source/mirror changes
- **Environment sensitivity**
  - 1: Non-regulated VPC; standard connectivity
  - 2: Regulated VPC (audit/SIEM requirements) or customer has strict maintenance windows
  - 3: On-prem/air-gapped, or customer has hard change-control gates (e.g., CAB), or evidence retention requirements

### Risk tiers
- **Low (3–4)**: Standard gates
- **Medium (5–6)**: Standard + enhanced comms + rollback drill (tabletop)
- **High (7–9)**: Standard + Security review + pre-upgrade readiness meeting + explicit rollback rehearsal plan

Record the score and tier in the change record.

## Release readiness requirements (pre-cut)
Before a Private release is marked “eligible for customer upgrades”, Release Engineering must attach evidence of:
- **CI evidence**: private installer integration test matrix coverage (minimum baseline below)
- **Compatibility policy update**: supported upgrade paths explicitly enumerated
- **Changelog**: customer-facing highlights + known issues + upgrade notes
- **Rollback contract**: unchanged or explicitly documented (if changed, requires SRE + Security review)

### Minimum CI baseline (must pass)
- Kubernetes versions: current supported set (see test matrix page)
- Scenarios:
  - N-1 → N happy path upgrade
  - Precheck failure injection (at least one blocking check)
  - Migration lock timeout simulation (ensures safe defaults / bounded timeouts)
  - Rollback invocation after a simulated mid-upgrade failure

## Per-customer change workflow (required)
### 1) Open the change record
Create a change record (internal ticket) and attach/link:
- Target environment identifiers (customer, region/site, VPC vs on-prem)
- Target versions (current → desired)
- Risk score + tier
- Proposed maintenance window
- On-call coverage plan

### 2) Generate and review the upgrade plan (required)
- Generate plan:
  - `redwood-private upgrade plan --from <current> --to <target> --output plan.json`
- Review plan for:
  - Artifact list completeness (images/charts/migrations)
  - Stage ordering: control plane completes before data plane rollouts
  - Defined rollback entry points and post-rollback verification steps
- Store artifacts:
  - Attach `plan.json` and human-readable summary to the change record

### 3) Run prechecks (required)
- Execute:
  - `redwood-private upgrade precheck --plan plan.json --output precheck-report.json`
- Attach the report to the change record.

#### Blocking prechecks (must pass)
(See full spec for details; below is the policy baseline.)
- **Kubernetes health**: all nodes Ready; no critical system pods CrashLoopBackOff; API server reachable
- **Control-plane connectivity**: installer can reach control-plane endpoints (or local on-prem endpoints)
- **RBAC/auth**: service accounts and cluster roles present; OIDC/SSO reachability validated when configured
- **Storage headroom**:
  - Persistent volumes used by databases/stateful components have ≥20% free space AND ≥10 GiB free (whichever is larger)
  - Snapshot target has sufficient space (backend-specific)
- **DB connectivity + privileges**: migration user can acquire required locks; bounded lock timeout configured
- **Version compatibility**: policy evaluation confirms supported path (default: N-1 → N)
- **Artifact availability**:
  - Online: registry/chart repo reachable
  - Offline: bundle present and checksum/signature verified
- **TLS/DNS**: certificates not expiring within 14 days; required SANs present; DNS resolution passes for internal endpoints

#### Warning prechecks (must be acknowledged)
- Non-critical capacity warnings (e.g., <30% cluster headroom)
- Optional integrations temporarily unreachable (e.g., SIEM forwarder, non-blocking webhooks)
- Non-default configuration drift detected (requires “acknowledge + document”)

### 4) Backup and restore readiness (required)
- Backup must complete successfully **before** executing any irreversible step (e.g., non-backward-compatible migration).
- Execute via installer:
  - `redwood-private backup run --plan plan.json --output backup-report.json`
- Backup requirements:
  - Encryption enabled (KMS/HSM where applicable)
  - Restore procedure documented and available to operators
  - Retention: minimum 7 days for standard; 30 days for regulated unless customer policy requires longer
- Attach `backup-report.json` and backup location metadata to the change record.

### 5) Approval gates (required)
Approvals required before “apply” begins:
- **Release Engineering approval** (required):
  - Confirms artifacts match release manifest
  - Confirms CI baseline met
  - Confirms offline/air-gapped bundle verification (if applicable)
- **SRE approval** (required):
  - Confirms prechecks are clean (or acceptable warnings are acknowledged)
  - Confirms monitoring/alerts in place for the window
  - Confirms rollback path is viable and documented
- **Security/Compliance approval** (conditional):
  - Required for High risk tier
  - Required for changes to audit events, backup handling, encryption defaults, or secret material

Approval must be recorded in the change record with approver name + timestamp.

### 6) Communications (required)
Communications requirements depend on risk tier.

#### Internal comms (all tiers)
- Post to `#eng-releases` and `#eng-oncall` at least:
  - T-24h for Medium/High
  - T-2h for Low
- Include: customer/site, window, versions, on-call lead, rollback trigger criteria, links to change record.

#### Customer comms
- **Low**: notify customer contact at least **48 hours** prior (or per contract), confirm window.
- **Medium**: notify **5 business days** prior; include expected operator actions and verification checklist.
- **High**: notify **10 business days** prior; schedule readiness call; confirm evidence expectations (audit logs, backup proof, rollback plan).

##### Customer email template (copy/paste)
Subject: Redwood Private maintenance window: upgrade to <VERSION>

Hello <Customer Team>,

We are planning a maintenance window to upgrade your Redwood Private deployment from <CURRENT_VERSION> to <TARGET_VERSION>.

- Proposed window: <DATE/TIME> (<TIMEZONE>)
- Expected impact: <e.g., control plane restart; inference data plane unaffected / short rolling restarts>
- Preconditions: We will run preflight checks (cluster health, storage capacity, connectivity) and take a backup prior to any migration.
- Rollback: If we detect upgrade failure conditions (see below), we will initiate a rollback to <CURRENT_VERSION> and validate service health.

Success criteria:
- Control plane healthy and responding
- Data plane readiness checks passing
- Upgrade audit events present for compliance logging (if applicable)

Rollback trigger criteria (examples):
- Persistent elevated error rate in control plane beyond <THRESHOLD> for > <DURATION>
- Migration step exceeds safe timeout or fails idempotency checks
- Readiness gates fail for > <DURATION>

Please reply with confirmation of the window and any change-control requirements we should align to.

Thank you,
<Redwood Contact>

### 7) Execute upgrade (during window)
- Start upgrade:
  - `redwood-private upgrade apply --plan plan.json --state-dir <path> --output upgrade-report.json`
- Requirements during execution:
  - Operator follows plan ordering; no manual step skipping without SRE approval
  - Health checks after each stage (control plane, then data plane)
  - If any blocking invariant fails, pause and escalate (see “Stop conditions”)

### 8) Stop conditions and escalation
Stop and escalate to SRE + Release Engineering if any occur:
- Control plane unavailable >10 minutes without clear forward progress
- Migration step exceeds declared plan timeout or reports lock contention beyond thresholds
- Repeated crash loops for upgrade jobs/hooks
- Artifact mismatch detected (digest differs from manifest)
- Unexpected data plane impact (elevated inference errors) during upgrade window

Escalation:
- Page SRE on-call (Private)
- Notify Release Engineering in `#eng-releases`
- Update customer status if Medium/High tier

### 9) Rollback policy (when invoked)
Rollback must be treated as an operational procedure with equivalent rigor.
- Invoke rollback only using supported tooling:
  - `redwood-private upgrade rollback --state-dir <path> --output rollback-report.json`
- Rollback requirements:
  - Uses stored upgrade state to ensure deterministic step reversal
  - Executes rollback hooks in defined order
  - Verifies post-rollback health checks (control plane + data plane)
- Attach rollback report and final status to the change record.

## Auditability and evidence retention
For every customer upgrade event, the following must be retained and attachable for support/compliance:
- Upgrade plan (`plan.json`) + human summary
- Precheck report (`precheck-report.json`)
- Backup report (`backup-report.json`) + backup identifiers
- Upgrade execution report (`upgrade-report.json`) and/or state machine logs
- Rollback report if used (`rollback-report.json`)
- Installer logs (sanitized) and referenced artifact manifests
- Audit log events for: upgrade started, prechecks pass/fail, backup completed, upgrade completed/failed, rollback invoked/completed

Retention guidance:
- Default: 30 days internal retention for upgrade artifacts
- Regulated customers: align to contract; if unspecified, 90 days recommended

## Post-change requirements
Within 2 business days of completion:
- Update change record with final status, duration, and any deviations
- If any incident occurred (customer-visible impact or rollback), file an incident and link it
- Record “lessons learned” and precheck gaps for backlog triage

## Exceptions
Exceptions are allowed only when documented and approved.
- Who can approve exceptions:
  - Release Engineering lead + SRE lead (both required)
  - Security/Compliance additionally required for regulated/high-tier customers
- Valid exception examples:
  - Emergency security patch where full comms timeline is not possible
  - Customer-mandated window with reduced lead time
  - Temporary CI gap with compensating controls (e.g., dedicated staging rehearsal)

Exception request must include:
- Which gate is being bypassed
- Why it is safe to proceed
- Compensating controls
- Rollback plan and stop conditions

## Appendix A: Change record checklist (operator-facing)
- [ ] Risk score + tier recorded
- [ ] Upgrade plan generated and attached
- [ ] Blocking prechecks passed; warnings acknowledged
- [ ] Backup completed; restore path documented
- [ ] Approvals captured (RelEng + SRE; Security if required)
- [ ] Customer notified per tier
- [ ] On-call coverage confirmed
- [ ] Upgrade executed with stage verification
- [ ] Rollback readiness confirmed; rollback executed if needed
- [ ] Artifacts retained; support bundle includes upgrade traces

## Appendix B: Internal Slack announcement template
Channel: #eng-releases (cc #eng-oncall)

Private upgrade scheduled
- Customer/site: <NAME> (<VPC/ON-PREM>)
- Window: <START–END> <TZ>
- Version: <CURRENT> → <TARGET>
- Risk tier: <LOW/MED/HIGH> (score: <n>)
- On-call lead: <NAME>
- Plan + prechecks: <LINK>
- Rollback trigger criteria: <BULLETS>

## Ownership
- Policy owner: Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien)
- Operational owner: SRE (Sean Gallagher)
- Next review date: 2025-09-30 (or sooner if we have a P0/P1 upgrade incident)

records.title: Planned Maintenance Communications SOP (Enterprise)
records.text:
Planned Maintenance Communications SOP (Enterprise)

## Purpose
This SOP defines required customer and internal communications for planned maintenance affecting production workloads, including Redwood Private upgrades.

## When to use
Use this SOP when a planned change has any of:
- Expected downtime
- Risk of degraded performance
- Customer-visible feature behavior changes
- Required customer participation (smoke tests, approvals, access)

## Required communications (minimum)
### 1) Pre-notice (T-5 business days recommended; minimum T-48h for enterprise)
Send a maintenance notice to the customer via the agreed channel (usually email + shared Slack Connect if available). Include:
- Date/time window in customers timezone
- Expected impact (downtime vs degraded; which routes/models)
- Rollback posture (we will rollback if KPIs exceed thresholds)
- Required customer participation (who needs to be present)
- Redwood escalation contact(s)

### 2) Internal heads-up (T-48h)
Post a short note in #eng-oncall and #customer-success with:
- Customer name
- Window time
- Change owner
- Link to change record
- Whether a security sign-off is required

### 3) Window start message (T=0)
Send a starting now message to the customer and internal channels. Confirm the backout plan exists and the next update time.

### 4) Progress updates
- Default cadence: every 30 minutes during the window
- Immediate updates for any rollback or risk escalation

### 5) All-clear (post-window)
Send an all-clear message when the verification window is complete. Include:
- Completed work summary
- Any follow-ups
- Post-change monitoring plan (e.g., 24h heightened watch)

## Status page guidance
- Hosted API: use public status page events when broad customer impact is possible.
- Private: do not post customer-specific maintenance on the public status page. Use direct customer comms unless contractually required otherwise.

## Templates
### Maintenance notice (customer)
Subject: Planned maintenance for your Redwood Private deployment
Body: We plan to perform maintenance on <DATE/TIME> for <DURATION>. Expected impact: <IMPACT>. Your participation needed: <WHO/WHAT>. Rollback criteria: <THRESHOLDS>.

### All-clear
Subject: Maintenance complete
Body: Maintenance completed at <TIME>. We verified <SMOKE TESTS>. Monitoring: <WHAT/WHO>.

## Approval
Customer Success must approve customer-facing maintenance notices for enterprise accounts.

records.title: Optimization Suggestions: estimated savings does not match billing/usage totals (Arkadia Finance)
records.text:
Optimization Suggestions: estimated savings does not match billing/usage totals (Arkadia Finance)

description:
Customer reports that the Console > Optimize > Suggestions view shows an estimated savings that does not reconcile with their billing totals for the same time period.

Customer impact:
- Confusion / loss of trust in "estimated $/day" shown in Suggestions drawer.
- Customer is using this as input for internal finance review; needs a defensible reconciliation.

Customer statement (from ticket intake):
- "The Suggestions panel says caching will save ~$1,250/day for /v1/chat on Llama-3 70B. Our usage/billing only moved by ~$300/day after we enabled caching. Where is the rest of the savings?"

Environment:
- Org: Arkadia Finance (enterprise)
- Region: us-east
- Routes: /v1/chat (primary), /v1/embeddings (secondary)
- Models observed in screenshots: rw-llama-3-70b-instruct, rw-qwen2.5-72b-instruct
- Suggestions feature flag: enabled (beta)
- Customer claims caching was enabled on 2026-02-19 ~17:00 ET

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Navigate to Console > Optimize > Suggestions
2) Filter to Project "prod-core" and Route "/v1/chat"
3) Open top caching suggestion (stable ID visible in drawer)
4) Note "Estimated savings ($/day)" and "Assumptions"
5) Compare to Billing > Invoices / Usage export for same days

Evidence / attachments (customer-provided):
- Screenshot 1: Suggestions list filtered to /v1/chat showing $/day estimate and risk badge
- Screenshot 2: Suggestion details drawer showing estimate range and stale_as_of
- Screenshot 3: Billing export excerpt with daily totals

Internal attachments (added by Support):
- Screenshot A: Console Usage Analytics "Inference cost (compute)" view (last 7 days)
- Screenshot B: Cost attribution query results for route/model (GPU-sec + tokens)

Notes:
- This is a beta feature; estimates are not contractual and use telemetry-derived assumptions.
- Need to confirm whether mismatch is due to time window, invoice vs compute cost basis, credits/discounts, partial rollout, or estimator bug.

comments:
2026-02-21 10:14 (Dev Patel): Created ticket from CS escalation. Tagging Miguel for customer comms and Nadia Rahman for cost attribution sanity check. Customer is specifically comparing Suggestions $/day to invoiced daily totals.
2026-02-21 11:02 (Miguel Santos): Reached out to Arkadia (email) requesting: (a) exact timeframe they’re comparing, (b) whether batching/caching was enabled for all projects/routes or just one, (c) billing export columns they’re using (gross vs net, credits, committed use).
2026-02-21 13:37 (Nadia Rahman): Quick check: Suggestions estimator uses compute-cost basis from cost-attribution aggregates (GPU-sec + token pricing) and excludes invoice-only items (platform fees, support add-ons, taxes) and can diverge from net invoiced totals due to credits/commit discounts. Also note estimator window defaults to trailing 7d with up to 24h ingestion lag; billing export Arkadia sent appears to be daily invoice accrual in local timezone.
2026-02-22 09:18 (Miguel Santos): Customer replied: comparing Feb 20–21 UTC days, using billing export "total_cost" column (net of credits). They enabled caching only for /v1/chat in project "prod-core" (not other projects). They did a phased rollout at 50% traffic for ~12 hours.
2026-02-22 10:41 (Mei Lin): Estimator for caching suggestion assumes full enablement on the route+model scope shown in the drawer and uses a baseline computed from last 7 days of traffic for that scope. It does not automatically account for partial rollout percentage unless telemetry indicates it as a separate "variant" (not currently wired in v0). If Arkadia enabled caching at 50% for 12 hours, observed savings will be ~25% of the headline daily number for those 24h windows.
2026-02-22 12:06 (Felix Schneider): UI currently labels this as "Estimated savings" but does not prominently call out that savings assume full adoption for the shown scope. Drawer has it in "Assumptions" section; might be too easy to miss. Also, the Suggestions list is sortable by $/day and people treat it as realized savings.
2026-02-23 08:52 (Miguel Santos): Did reconciliation attempt:
- Matched window to trailing 7d used by suggestion (drawer shows stale_as_of = 2026-02-21 00:00 UTC)
- Compared to Console Usage Analytics > "Inference cost (compute)" for same scope (project=prod-core, route=/v1/chat, model=rw-llama-3-70b-instruct)
Result: estimate implies ~18–22% compute cost reduction at full adoption. Customer observed ~6–8% reduction on Feb 20–21 which is consistent with 50% rollout + first-day cache warm-up effect.
Main deltas vs billing export: billing is net of credits/commit; estimate is on compute-cost basis and excludes non-inference line items. Billing is per-day UTC; customer initially compared to local-time days.
2026-02-23 09:30 (Jonas Weber): Cache warm-up effect is real: first 6–12 hours can show lower hit uplift depending on prefix repetitiveness. Estimator assumes steady-state uplift using median of last 7d prefix reuse distribution; it can overstate day-1 savings. Suggest we advise customers to evaluate over at least 48–72 hours after enabling and to look at cache hit metrics + compute cost, not invoice totals.
2026-02-24 14:12 (Miguel Santos): Sent customer guidance:
1) Use Console Usage Analytics "Inference cost (compute)" not invoice total to compare with Suggestions.
2) Align time window to UTC and to stale_as_of period.
3) If using partial rollout, scale the estimate by rollout percentage and allow 24–72h for cache warm-up.
4) If they need invoice reconciliation, we can help map compute-cost delta to net invoice (credits/commit discounts will compress visible delta).
Customer acknowledged and asked for a one-pager they can share internally. Looping in Elliot Price for docs link + suggested wording.
2026-02-25 10:27 (Elliot Price): Pointed Miguel to internal draft docs section explaining compute-cost vs billing totals and rollout scaling. We should also add a short inline callout in drawer: "Assumes 100% of traffic" + "Compute-cost estimate (not invoice total)".
2026-02-26 16:45 (Miguel Santos): Customer confirmed the discrepancy was primarily due to (a) comparing net billing totals (credits/commit) vs compute-cost estimate, and (b) partial rollout + warm-up. They can proceed with internal review using compute-cost deltas. Marking resolved. Follow-up: file copy/UX tweak request to make assumptions more prominent.

internal_analysis_notes:
Root cause classification: Not a billing bug; a reconciliation/expectation gap + missing clarity in UI.

Contributing factors:
- Suggestions $/day is based on compute-cost attribution aggregates (GPU-sec + token pricing) and does not equal net invoiced totals (credits/commit discounts, platform fees, taxes).
- Estimator assumes full adoption for the scope shown; does not incorporate rollout percentage for A/B/canary in v0.
- Cache warm-up can make first-day realized savings lower than steady-state estimate.
- Time window mismatch: suggestion uses trailing 7d baseline + stale_as_of; customer compared to two UTC days and initially used local time.

Recommendation to Support/CS:
- When customers compare to billing, redirect to Console Usage Analytics (compute-cost) for apples-to-apples.
- Ask for rollout percentage and whether change was applied across all routes/projects.
- Ensure they compare a 48–72h window post-enable to avoid warm-up noise.

Product follow-ups (non-blocking):
- Promote assumption text in UI (100% adoption, compute-cost basis, exclude discounts/credits).
- Consider adding an optional field in suggestion payload for "adoption_factor" or a UI control to scale savings by rollout percentage (future).
- Add docs section on reconciliation: compute-cost vs invoice total.

resolution:
Provided reconciliation guidance and validated that observed savings aligns with estimate after accounting for (1) compute-cost vs net billing totals, (2) partial rollout percentage, (3) cache warm-up and baseline window alignment. No platform defect identified; follow-up request logged to improve UI copy around assumptions and to clarify savings are compute-cost estimates.

records.text:
Planned Change: SLO / Error Budget Impact Review Requirements

## Purpose
This document defines the minimum SRE review steps for planned changes that may impact availability, latency, or throughput SLOs for any production environment (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).

## When this review is required
SRE review is required for any change that is classified Medium/High/Critical risk under the Production Change Management Policy, or any change that:
- Requires disabling alerts
- Requires a maintenance window
- Has a credible risk of increased 5xx, latency regression, or capacity shortfall

## Required checks (attach evidence/links)
### 1) Current SLO state
- Confirm current 30-day error budget remaining for impacted services/tenants.
- If error budget remaining is below 25%, attach an explicit risk acceptance from Engineering + SRE lead.

### 2) Capacity + saturation
- Confirm GPU and request capacity headroom for the expected window.
- Confirm no overlapping capacity events (region maintenance, fleet migrations, known shortages).

### 3) Monitoring coverage
- Identify the “watch list” metrics for the change window (at minimum: 5xx rate, P95 latency, saturation/queue depth, restarts/OOM, and synthetic checks).
- Confirm alerts are enabled and routed to an active on-call.

### 4) Rollback feasibility
- Validate that rollback can be executed within the defined “time-to-restore” target for the customer (or platform).
- Identify the decision point for rollback (e.g., after control-plane or after data-plane).

### 5) Change overlap
- Confirm no concurrent high-risk changes affecting the same customer/region.
- If overlap exists, record mitigation or reschedule.

## Go/No-Go criteria from an SRE perspective
SRE will recommend GO only if:
- Error budget is healthy or risk acceptance is documented
- Monitoring is ready and on-call coverage confirmed
- Rollback plan is concrete and feasible
- Customer comms plan exists when customer-visible

## Minimum evidence checklist (copy/paste into change record)
- [ ] Error budget screenshot/link
- [ ] Capacity headroom note (GPU + queue)
- [ ] Alert routing confirmation
- [ ] Rollback time estimate + decision point
- [ ] List of services/routes impacted

records.title: Production Change Management Policy
records.text:
Production Change Management Policy

## Overview
This policy defines the minimum process and approvals required for production changes at Redwood Inference. The objective is to reduce customer impact from planned changes and ensure we capture sufficient evidence, rollback planning, and communications.

This applies to: Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments (including customer-managed clusters).

## Definitions
- *Change record*: the system-of-record ticket for the change (Jira for support/operations changes, Linear for engineering work, with a Jira change record if customer production is affected).
- *Risk level*: Low/Medium/High/Critical based on blast radius and reversibility.
- *Go/No-Go gate*: explicit confirmation at start of window that prerequisites are met.

## Required elements for every production change
1. Change record with scope, owner, and timeline.
2. Rollback plan (time-to-rollback estimate required).
3. Monitoring plan (what signals are watched, by whom).
4. Customer communications plan if there is customer-visible impact or a maintenance window.
5. Evidence attached: preflight outputs, screenshots/links to dashboards, relevant test results, and approvals.

## Risk classification
### Low
Examples: documentation-only, internal tool changes without customer impact.

### Medium
Examples: changes behind a feature flag; reversible config changes; single-tenant changes with fast rollback.

### High
Examples: multi-component changes; schema migrations; upgrades to customer production Private clusters; changes to auth/RBAC; changes requiring coordinated downtime.

### Critical
Examples: irreversible changes; upgrades during peak traffic; changes during active incident; changes that affect multiple enterprise customers simultaneously.

## Approval matrix (minimum approvers)
### Low
- Engineering peer approval OR team lead approval.

### Medium
- Owning team lead
- On-call/SRE notified

### High
- Owning team lead
- SRE approver (named individual)
- Customer Success approver if customer-facing
- Security approver if security triggers are met

### Critical
- Director-level engineering approver
- SRE approver
- Security & Compliance approver
- Customer Success approver

## Security triggers (require Security & Compliance sign-off)
Security sign-off is required when the change affects any of the following for a customer production environment:
- Authentication, SSO, token validation, signing keys, or session handling
- RBAC policy defaults, permission boundaries, or privileged service accounts
- TLS configuration, certificate automation, or trust stores
- Audit logging pipeline, retention, or integrity controls
- Introduction of new third-party dependencies/images
- Network boundaries (ingress/egress controls)

## SRE triggers (require SRE review)
SRE review is required when the change:
- Alters scaling behavior, autoscaling policy, or load shedding
- Changes core request routing, fallback policies, or region-level capacity
- Modifies alerting/monitoring or disables alerts for a window
- Has any planned downtime or performance regression risk

## Communications requirements
If the change is customer-visible (maintenance window, risk of degraded service, or known downtime), the change record must include:
- Customer notification timing and channel
- Internal comms plan (who is on bridge, where to post updates)
- An all-clear message plan

## Go/No-Go gate requirement
For High/Critical changes, the Change Owner must explicitly record a GO/NO-GO decision at window start including:
- Confirmation approvals are complete
- Confirmation rollback is ready
- Confirmation monitoring is in place
- Confirmation customer comms are sent and acknowledged where applicable

## Exceptions
Exceptions (including change freeze overrides) require explicit approval and must be linked from the change record.

records.title: AWS Marketplace procurement + security FAQ (2026)
records.text:
AWS Marketplace procurement + security FAQ (2026)

## Overview
This page is the current internal FAQ for answering enterprise buyer questions about purchasing Redwood Inference through AWS Marketplace (public offer vs private offer), and the most common security/compliance questions (SOC 2, encryption/KMS, retention, audit logs, data residency, incident response, and SSO/RBAC).

This content is used by AEs/SEs for deals where the customer prefers AWS Marketplace so spend can count toward AWS commitments (e.g., EDP) and to streamline vendor onboarding.

---

## What customers typically ask for (quick list)
- Why buy via AWS Marketplace (EDP/committed spend, consolidated invoicing) and when to use a private offer.
- SKU fit: Hosted API now, Dedicated capacity later, and when Private (VPC) is required.
- Metering and billing: dimensions (tokens/requests), reporting cadence, and invoice visibility.
- Security questionnaire items: SOC 2 posture, encryption/KMS, retention controls, audit logs, data residency, incident response, and SSO/RBAC.
- Shared responsibility boundaries for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Onboarding flow: subscription → entitlement validation → org provisioning/linking → first API key → first call.
- Support and escalation expectations for marketplace customers.

---

## Marketplace procurement FAQ

### Q: Public offer or private offer?
**Recommended for enterprise: Private offer.** Private offers allow us to align term length, committed spend constructs, and any deal-specific exhibits (e.g., security addendum, DPA references) while still using Marketplace as the procurement channel.

**Public offer** (pay-as-you-go) is typically used for small pilots or when procurement does not require an order-form-like artifact.

### Q: Does Marketplace spend count toward AWS commitments (e.g., EDP)?
In most enterprise cases **yes**, but eligibility is determined by the customer’s AWS agreement and how the offer is accepted. When asked, we should state:
- We structure offers using standard AWS Marketplace constructs.
- The customer should confirm EDP crediting mechanics with their AWS account team.
- Redwood can loop in our AWS partner contact if needed to validate mechanics for the customer.

### Q: What information do we need to create a private offer?
Provide the customer the intake checklist and collect:
- Buyer AWS account ID(s) that will accept the offer
- Preferred AWS region(s) for processing (and any single-region requirement)
- Requested start date
- Term length (12 months is most common)
- Commercial structure (committed spend target, prepay vs monthly, overage expectations)
- Required legal/security exhibits (DPA, breach notification language, subprocessor references)
- Signatory / procurement contact

**Internal note:** The current intake path is the “AWS MP Private Offer Intake” Salesforce form (ask Deal Desk for the latest link).

### Q: What is the onboarding flow after subscription?
Typical flow:
1) Customer subscribes/accepts the offer in AWS Marketplace.
2) AWS sends an entitlement to Redwood.
3) Customer signs into the Redwood Console and links the Marketplace subscription.
4) Customer creates or links a Redwood org.
5) Customer generates an API key and makes a first test call.

**Entitlement timing (updated):** Most entitlements propagate in **5–20 minutes**. In rare cases it can take longer (up to a few hours) depending on AWS-side propagation.

**If entitlement is delayed:** Customer should contact Redwood support first. We can confirm whether we received the entitlement and can trigger a re-sync using the subscription/entitlement identifier.

---

## SKU + deployment model FAQ

### Q: What’s the difference between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private?
- **Hosted:** Fastest start. Shared infrastructure with tenant isolation controls. Usage-based metering via Marketplace. Best for pilots and many production workloads.
- **Dedicated:** Reserved capacity for predictable throughput and stronger isolation. Often adopted after a successful Hosted pilot.
- **Private (VPC):** Redwood runs in (or is tightly attached to) the customer’s network boundary. Best for strict network controls, VPC-only access, and certain key management/residency requirements.

### Q: Shared responsibility (what we own vs what the customer owns)
- **Hosted/Dedicated:** Redwood operates the service, core security controls, and platform availability. Customer configures org access (SSO/RBAC), API key practices, and application-layer security.
- **Private:** Customer owns more of the network boundary and can own more of the key management and logging pipeline depending on architecture. Redwood still owns application security and platform components we operate.

---

## Security & compliance FAQ (common questionnaire items)

### Q: Do you have SOC 2 Type II?
**Yes.** Redwood maintains a current SOC 2 Type II report.
- We provide access via our trust portal with controlled access.
- For Marketplace reviews, we also provide a security overview packet that maps major controls without distributing the full report broadly.

### Q: ISO 27001?
Redwood is aligned to ISO 27001 control areas and maintains a formal security program. If a customer specifically requires an ISO certificate, route the request to Security/Compliance to confirm the current status and appropriate response for the deal.

### Q: Encryption in transit and at rest (what TLS versions)?
- **In transit:** TLS **1.2+** (TLS 1.3 supported for modern clients where applicable). API and console require HTTPS.
- **At rest:** Encrypted storage layers.

### Q: Do you support customer-managed KMS keys (BYOK)?
**Updated guidance (2026):**
- **Hosted:** Customer-managed KMS is available for enterprise tenants in select regions as an add-on, using per-tenant key configuration (subject to feasibility review). If not available in the target region, the default is provider-managed keys.
- **Dedicated:** Customer-managed key options are available for many Dedicated configurations.
- **Private (VPC):** Customer-managed keys are supported and typically the recommended path when BYOK is a hard requirement.

If asked for a simple statement: “Hosted uses provider-managed keys by default; customer-managed keys are available for certain enterprise configurations; Private/VPC supports customer-managed keys.”

### Q: Do you store prompts and completions? Can retention be set to zero?
We should avoid vague language. Use these points:
- Redwood does **not** use customer prompts/outputs to train models.
- Redwood retains limited metadata required for service reliability, abuse prevention, billing reconciliation, and security investigations.
- **Content retention controls:** Enterprise configurations can disable content logging and minimize content persistence.

**Updated retention guidance (2026):**
- Default for enterprise Hosted is **content logging disabled** unless explicitly enabled for debugging.
- Minimal operational/billing metadata is retained per policy; the retention window is documented in the “Data Handling & Retention” attachment for Marketplace buyers.
- “Retention = 0” should be positioned as “no persistent storage of request/response content,” while acknowledging that transient in-memory processing is required to serve the request.

### Q: Audit logs (what events exist, can we export to Splunk)?
Redwood provides audit logging for admin actions and auth events, such as:
- User invites and role changes
- SSO configuration changes
- API key creation/revocation
- Model deployment/config changes (where applicable)
- Policy/config updates

**Export options (updated):**
- API-based export is supported.
- Standard integrations include export to customer SIEM pipelines (Splunk commonly) and/or customer-owned storage (e.g., S3) depending on deployment and plan.

**Immutability/WORM:** Redwood maintains integrity controls. If the customer requires WORM/immutable retention guarantees, the recommended approach is exporting logs to the customer’s immutable store where they enforce WORM retention.

### Q: Data residency / region restriction (e.g., US-only, us-east-1 only)
- Redwood can support regional processing commitments within the set of available regions for the customer’s SKU.
- If the customer requires strict single-region processing (e.g., **us-east-1 only**), confirm feasibility for the specific SKU and put the commitment in writing (private offer exhibits / order form language) referencing the data handling documentation.
- For Private (VPC), data residency aligns to the customer’s chosen region and architecture.

### Q: SSO / SAML / RBAC
- Enterprise orgs support SSO/SAML.
- Console access is governed by RBAC.
- API keys are scoped and can be managed per org/project practices.

### Q: Incident response and breach notification timelines
Redwood maintains an incident response program with defined severities and notification processes. Specific notification timelines are typically addressed contractually; route strict requirements to Legal + Security/Compliance.

### Q: Subprocessors
Redwood maintains a current subprocessor list and shares it through the security packet/trust portal. Scope varies by Hosted vs Private (Private can reduce reliance on some subprocessors depending on the customer architecture).

### Q: Private connectivity (VPC endpoints / PrivateLink)
- **Private (VPC):** Supported.
- **Hosted:** Generally accessed over public internet with TLS. If the customer has strict network controls requiring private connectivity, position **Private** as the intended solution.

---

## Metering, billing, and FinOps FAQ

### Q: What are the metering dimensions?
Metering is usage-based and expressed in AWS Marketplace dimensions (commonly token-based for generation and embeddings units depending on SKU). The exact dimension names are included in the offer and listing details.

### Q: How quickly does usage show up in AWS billing / Cost Explorer?
**Updated guidance (2026):** Marketplace metering is not real-time. Customers typically see updates within **hours to ~24 hours** depending on AWS billing pipelines.

### Q: Does Redwood provide usage reporting that matches the AWS invoice?
Yes. Redwood provides org-level usage reporting (e.g., by project/model/route) and supports reconciliation with Marketplace billing line items.

---

## Standard next steps for an enterprise Marketplace deal
1) Send the customer the Marketplace security packet and short-form security FAQ.
2) Provide trust portal access instructions for SOC 2 (as needed).
3) Collect buyer AWS account IDs, region constraints, term/start date, and commercial preferences.
4) Draft and route the private offer internally (Deal Desk) and then to the customer.
5) Book a technical deep dive if the customer requests detail on audit logs, retention controls, or entitlement troubleshooting.

---

## Internal escalation and ownership
- Security/compliance questionnaire, SOC 2 access, retention/residency commitments: **Security & Compliance (Naomi Feldman)**
- Marketplace entitlement/provisioning issues and onboarding flow: **Solutions Engineering (Markus Klein)**
- Private offer structure, term/commit mechanics, and procurement timelines: **Account Team / Deal Desk (primary AE: Stephanie Nguyen)**

---

## Change log
- 2026-03-12: Updated guidance on Hosted customer-managed KMS availability, entitlement timing, and AWS billing latency expectations.
- 2026-02-03: Initial publication for sales enablement.

records.title: Partial-result Checkpointing and Client Resume Contract
records.text:
Partial-result Checkpointing and Client Resume Contract

Summary
-------
This document defines a cross-service contract and operational playbook for partial-result checkpointing and client-driven resume for streaming inference calls. It provides a deterministic HTTP/WebSocket/HTTP/2 streaming contract that enables clients to tolerate transient connection failures, resume long-running generation requests, and reconcile partial outputs without risking duplicate side-effects or quality regressions. The contract balances developer ergonomics, predictable economics, and production safety for Redwood’s hosted and dedicated offerings.

Scope
-----
Applies to API surfaces that provide: text generation streaming, structured output streaming (tables/records), long-running embeddings/rerank jobs with incremental progress, and any route that supports server-sent partial outputs (examples: /v1/generate.stream, /v1/chat.stream, /v1/rerank.stream).

This specifically covers:
- Wire-level semantics for checkpoints and resume tokens.
- Idempotency requirements and server-side deduplication semantics.
- Storage, retention, and encryption requirements for checkpoint artifacts.
- Operational SLOs and alerting thresholds.
- Client and server rollout and compatibility strategy.

Motivation
----------
We observe that long-running streams (interactive assistants, long-form generation, batched rerank) are sensitive to transient network glitches and HTTP connection limits, which cause poor user experience or expensive restarts. Implementing a lightweight checkpoint/resume mechanism: reduces perceived latency, lowers token cost by avoiding full re-generation, and improves reliability for customers on poor networks or intermediate proxies.

Goals (non-exhaustive)
- Allow clients to resume a previously-started stream from the last acknowledged checkpoint.
- Guarantee exactly-once external side-effect semantics for requests that produce side-effects (webhooks, downstream writes) via server-side gating.
- Keep checkpoint storage small and short-lived by checkpointing only the minimal resume state (KV cache ID, consumed token count, model variant id, deterministic RNG seed if applicable).
- Make the contract backward-compatible with clients that do not implement resume.

Contract: Wire semantics and payloads
----------------------------------
1) Checkpoint messages
- Servers MUST emit a stable checkpoint envelope at configurable intervals (default every 512 tokens or 10s, whichever comes first).
- Checkpoint envelope fields (JSON):
  - type: "checkpoint"
  - checkpoint_id: string (UUIDv4)
  - request_id: string (Redwood request id)
  - model_variant: string
  - token_offset: integer (number of tokens produced so far)
  - kv_cache_ref: string (opaque id for server-side cache)
  - truncated_output_hash: string (SHA256 of last emitted chunk to enable client reconciliation)
  - expires_at: ISO8601 timestamp (checkpoint TTL)
  - signature: string (HMAC-SHA256 of envelope using per-tenant key)

Example checkpoint envelope (server -> client):
{
  "type": "checkpoint",
  "checkpoint_id": "b8f3d8f8-3d2f-4d5a-9f2b-6a7c12c4e9bb",
  "request_id": "r-2026-00012345",
  "model_variant": "redwood-large-v2-quant",
  "token_offset": 1536,
  "kv_cache_ref": "cache://tenant-42/shard-17/ckpt-42",
  "truncated_output_hash": "sha256:abcd...",
  "expires_at": "2026-03-12T18:42:00Z",
  "signature": "sig:..."
}

2) Resume requests
- Client may initiate a resume by sending a ResumeRequest to the same endpoint (prefer HTTP/2 or WebSocket), passing the checkpoint_id and an optional client_ack_hash to indicate the last received chunk.
- ResumeRequest fields (JSON):
  - type: "resume_request"
  - checkpoint_id: string
  - client_ack_hash: string (optional)
  - client_id: string
  - request_metadata: map (opaque string kvs)
  - desired_resume_window: integer (tokens; server may honor subset)

Example ResumeRequest (client -> server):
{
  "type": "resume_request",
  "checkpoint_id": "b8f3d8f8-3d2f-4d5a-9f2b-6a7c12c4e9bb",
  "client_ack_hash": "sha256:abcd...",
  "client_id": "web-6d2a",
  "request_metadata": {"ui_session":"sess-123"},
  "desired_resume_window": 1024
}

3) Server resume response
- Server verifies signature and TTL. If valid, server responds with either:
  - resume_accepted: provides a new stream that resumes generation from token_offset, or
  - resume_denied: provides reason (expired, checkpoint-not-found, variant-mismatch) and optional best-effort fallback (restart token and cost estimate).
- Servers must not resume across incompatible model variants; resume across quantization variants is allowed only if deterministic equivalence is guaranteed (see model-compatibility ledger).

4) Idempotency and side-effect handling
- For requests that may trigger external side-effects, servers MUST not replay side-effects on resume. Implement one of two modes chosen per-route:
  - server-gated side-effects: the first successful finalization of the request generates an immutable side-effect token; clients must present this token when invoking any follow-up action.
  - client-ack-guarded mode: side-effects are only emitted after explicit client acknowledgement of final chunk.

5) Failure modes and reconciliation
- If the client’s client_ack_hash does not match the server’s truncated_output_hash, server SHOULD emit a ‘divergence’ event containing the minimal suffix the client is missing and a suggested merge strategy.

Operational requirements and configuration table
------------------------------------------------
| Key | Default | Unit | Description | Owner |
|-----|---------|------|-------------|-------|
| checkpoint.interval_tokens | 512 | tokens | Default token cadence for emitting checkpoints | inference-runtime |
| checkpoint.interval_seconds | 10 | seconds | Time-based cadence upper bound | inference-runtime |
| checkpoint.ttl_seconds | 86400 | seconds | Default checkpoint retention (24h) | storage-team |
| checkpoint.max_size_bytes | 16384 | bytes | Max size of serialized checkpoint metadata | storage-team |
| resume.auth_window_seconds | 300 | seconds | Time window after checkpoint creation where resume is allowed without re-authorization | identity |
| resume.p95_restart_latency | 150 | ms | SLO for resuming and starting token emission after a resume request | eng-sre |
| resume.max_parallel_resumes_per_tenant | 5 | count | Rate-limit per tenant to prevent abuse | quota-service |

Storage and encryption
- Checkpoints are stored in the checkpoint-store service (S3-compatible). All checkpoint metadata must be encrypted at rest with customer KMS, and signed with a per-tenant resume key. Checkpoint payloads must avoid storing user PII or full prompts unless configured by customer (private deployments).

SLOs and alerts
---------------
- Resume success rate (per-tenant) >= 99.5% over 24h.
- Resume p95 latency <= resume.p95_restart_latency (150ms default).
- Checkpoint persistence latency (write to checkpoint-store) p99 < 200ms.
- Alert if > 1% of resumed streams require full restart due to divergence in a 24h window.
- Alert on checkpoint-store error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes.

Observability and telemetry
-------------------------
- Emit events with standardized tags: checkpoint.emitted, checkpoint.persisted, resume.requested, resume.accepted, resume.denied, resume.divergence.
- Each event must include: request_id, checkpoint_id, tenant_id, model_variant, route, token_offset, and p99 latency metric dimensions.
- Trace spans: stream-gateway -> checkpoint-service -> inference-runtime -> checkpoint-store must be stitched with the same trace id for end-to-end debugging.

Rollout and compatibility
-------------------------
1) Backwards compatibility
- If an older client does not implement resume, server continues to emit checkpoints but ignores resume requests. The server must support default behavior of restarting from scratch with a clear restart-cost estimate.
2) Canary rollout steps (recommended):
  a) Implement server-side checkpoint emission behind a runtime flag (flag: checkpointing.enabled).
  b) Enable for internal tenants only and run synthetic failover tests for 72h.
  c) Gradually enable for 5% of external tenants, monitor resume success metrics and downstream cost delta.
  d) Increase to 25% then 100% if thresholds met.
3) Rollback plan: TTL reduction + immediate disable of checkpointing flag. Documented incident playbook in eng-platform/runbooks.

Testing and validation checklist
-------------------------------
- Unit tests for checkpoint envelope creation and signature verification.
- Integration tests: simulate connection interruption at token boundaries and mid-chunk; validate client resume produces the same final payload within tolerance threshold for structured outputs.
- Chaos tests: drop TCP connections, simulate transparent proxies, and ensure resume success > 99.5%.
- Cost regression: ensure average token cost delta after enabling resume < 3% (positive or negative).

Security considerations
----------------------
- Ensure checkpoint signatures use per-tenant HMAC keys stored in KMS. Rotate keys with zero-downtime using dual-signature validation during rotation window.
- Checkpoints must not expose raw secret keys, or PII unless explicitly enabled by customer and documented in private deployment configs.

Appendix: example CLI flows and cURL
-----------------------------------
Emit stream (client):
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"Write a long analysis...","stream":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate.stream

Resume flow (client):
# client reads checkpoint_id from last message and issues resume
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"type":"resume_request","checkpoint_id":"b8f3d8f8-3d2f-4d5a-9f2b-6a7c12c4e9bb","client_id":"web-6d2a","client_ack_hash":"sha256:abcd..."}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate.resume

Operational owners and contact
----------------------------
- inference-runtime: @inference-runtime-team (primary implementer)
- checkpoint-store/storage-team: @storage-team (persistence, encryption)
- stream-gateway: @edge-team (protocol / rate-limiting)
- eng-sre: oncall for SLO violations and rollback.

Related reading
---------------
- Model variant compatibility ledger (model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026)
- Cost-aware streaming payload schema guideline
- Runbook: stream-resume-incident-playbook (eng-platform/runbooks/stream-resume-incident-playbook)

Revision history
----------------
- 2026-01-12: Initial draft by Maya Chen.
- 2026-02-05: Added SLO thresholds and storage encryption detail (reviewers: Rohit, Liam).
- 2026-03-05: Final edits and publication, clarified divergence reconciliation logic.
