records.title: eng-runtime
records.text:
eng-runtime

kai: Heads up — saw a spike of OOMs on staging after switching to the percentile-based workspace sizing. Started after yesterday's deploy. Anyone seen this pattern with long KV contexts?

devon: Which percentile change did we make? dynamic-reserve -> 99p global? any repro? :eyes:

kai: Swapped to 99th-percentile workspace sizing for FFN (to shave costs). It reduced avg footprint but when requests had long KV (seq_len 32 -> 2048) we hit OOMs. Attaching quick profiler excerpt below.

infra-bot: New alert created: PROD-STAGING OOM spike (alert#1930000123) — https://internal/alerts/1930000123 :rotating_light:

maria: Likely cause: heuristic assumed "workspace dominated", but KV cache growth wasn't modeled. So allocations for workspace + KV + cuBLAS temp can exceed slab reservation. Need to fold kv_bytes into the workspace estimator.

samir: Quick numbers from the trace: cuBLASLt GEMM temp ~1.2GB, FlashAttn temp ~600MB, KV cache ~3.5GB (int16), other reserves ~300MB -> total ~5.6GB. Our slab threshold for that worker was 5.0GB -> OOM.

devon: Repro snippet to compute peak estimate I used locally:```python
# pseudo estimate
batch=1
seq=2048
hidden=512
kv_bytes = batch*seq*hidden*2  # int16 KV
ffn_ws = ffn_workspace_est(hidden, batch, seq)
attn_ws = flash_attn_workspace_est(batch, seq, hidden)
total_est = kv_bytes + ffn_ws + attn_ws + static_reserve
print(total_est)
```

sofia: Two immediate mitigations: 1) Make chooser aware of kv_bytes and prefer kernel variants with lower transient scratch when kv_bytes is large. 2) Add a quick precommit probe (simulate allocations without touching CUDA) to predict whether the full set fits. If not, route to smaller kernel / reduce batch / return 429.

kai: The latency tail also regressed for long-context requests (p99 up ~15%). We could accept a small latency/cost bump if it eliminates OOMs, but want minimal impact on short contexts.

maria: Suggest multi-tier rules: 
- if seq <= 512: prefer FlashAttention (best perf)
- if 512 < seq <= 1024: try Triton path with medium scratch
- if seq > 1024 or kv_bytes > kv_threshold: prefer cuBLASLt matmul path (lower temp) or quantized kernels
Also adjust probereserve to add kv_bytes into the probe.

devon: Implementation idea: before kernel selection we run `predict_peak(request_meta)` which returns predicted_peak_bytes. Kernel chooser takes free_gpu_mem and predicted_peak and picks variant with smallest predicted_peak that meets perf/cost policy. If none fit, pick a safe fallback: smaller batch / block decode.

samir: Ran a canary patch locally that: a) accounts for kv_bytes in estimator b) downgrades to cuBLASLt when predicted_peak > 90% slab. Results: p99 latency for long-context down from 420ms -> 360ms, OOMs -> 0 on 500 runs, short-context median latency +3%.

sofia: nice. can we add metric tags for "chooser_reason" so we can slice which requests were routed to fallback? :+1:

kai: I'll open a small PR with the probe + metric tags. Planning a staging canary tonight. Link when ready. Also adding a dashboard to show predicted_peak vs actual peak.

devon: Also we should test with quantized KV (int8) scenarios — estimator needs model/quantization-aware computations.

maria: Agreed. I'll add a unit for the estimator: test cases for seq {32,128,512,1024,2048} x quant {fp16,int8} x batch {1,4}.

kai: Thanks all. Canary push scheduled 22:00 PST. Will monitor histograms and OOM alert. If anyone wants to watch: /run profiler --live staging --thread 1930000123

sofia: :thumbsup: great plan.

records.title: eng-ml
records.text:
eng-ml

hannah: quick thread to propose the 'synthetic_sentinel_v2' gate for v4q-longdoc onboarding. idea: one compact index that captures coherence + hallucination + tail-latency + infra warmup signals so we can do principled autofallbacks.

leo: nice. i like a single index rather than a bunch of ad-hoc rules. what signals?

hannah: signals: concordance_score_delta (higher is worse), ner_halluc_pct, latency_p99_ms (absolute + pct uplift), kv_warm_miss_per_1k (cache warmup), tokens_per_session_delta. normalize and weight. trigger when risk_index >= 0.78 sustained over window.

mina: add a small answer-coherence metric (BLEU-ish ngram overlap vs reference) for multi-turns. v4 shows subtle fluency that MRR misses.

hannah: good call. i'll add answer_coherence_delta as low-weight input. default weights: concordance:0.45, ner_halluc:0.2, latency:0.18, kv_warm_miss:0.1, tokens:0.05, coherence:0.02. seq_len adjustments: for >2500 tokens multiply latency weight x1.6 and reduce concordance weight x0.9.

raj: safety preconds? tiny cohorts are noisy. require either canary_traffic_pct >= 1.8% OR num_slices_firing >= 3 for auto-rollback. otherwise just alert to #eng-ml.

hannah: agreed. also two-tier thresholds: alert_score=0.65 (10m smoothing), soft-auto=0.9 (3m sustained) for first 4h, then auto threshold decays to 0.8 afterwards. ops prefer conservative autos early.

taylor: can you paste the compact policy blob so infra/orch can accept it directly? devex wants per-signal contribution exposed in Console for triage.

hannah: pasted below. it's the staging draft for the orchestration API.

```json
{
  "name": "synthetic_sentinel_v2",
  "inputs": ["concordance_delta","ner_halluc_pct","latency_p99_ms","latency_pct_uplift","kv_warm_miss_per_1k","tokens_delta_pct","answer_coherence_delta"],
  "weights": {"concordance_delta":0.45,"ner_halluc_pct":0.2,"latency_p99_ms":0.18,"kv_warm_miss_per_1k":0.1,"tokens_delta_pct":0.05,"answer_coherence_delta":0.02},
  "normalize":"robust_scale",
  "latency_rule": {"abs_p99_ms":420,"pct_uplift_threshold":0.22},
  "context_adjust": [{"if":"seq_len>2500","apply":{"latency_mul":1.6,"concordance_mul":0.9}}],
  "thresholds": {"alert_score":0.65,"soft_auto_score":0.9,"post_watch_auto_score":0.8,"alert_window_min":10,"soft_auto_window_min":3},
  "preconds": {"min_canary_pct":1.8,"min_slices_firing":3},
  "actions": {"on_alert":["notify:#eng-ml","attach:per_signal_series"],"on_soft_auto":["notify:#oncall","escalate_if_persistent"],"on_auto":["rollback","create_incident:severity=high"]}
}
```

leo: nit: absolute p99 420ms might be tight for some regions; we should have region-aware baselines (console can allow region overrides). also prefer evictions_per_1k naming (kv_warm_miss_per_1k is fine).

mina: synthetic eval set: include a 200-item halluc-prone entity set + 150 multi-turn longchat examples + a tiny shadow of customer long-docs (opt-in). that will surface signals faster.

ops-bot: deploy: canary start for model:v4q-longdoc at 2026-03-24T09:40:00Z cohort=0.5%. hooks: concordance_delta, ner_halluc_pct, latency_p99_ms, latency_pct_uplift, kv_warm_miss_per_1k, tokens_delta_pct, answer_coherence_delta.

raj: plan: push sentinel to staging with the two-tier thresholds, require safety preconds for auto, and wire Console to show stacked per-signal contribution + running risk_index. i will also add a debug opt-in to emit per-request signal vector for the canary cohort to S3 for triage.

hannah: pushing to staging now. will post the staging config link + 25m shadow snapshot when the synthetic run finishes. thanks all :thumbsup:

records.title: Orchestrate layered build profiles and stabilize language toolchains
records.text:
Orchestrate layered build profiles and stabilize language toolchains

description:
Reduce CI build flakiness and latency by introducing composable BuildKit profiles (fast/dev/stable), migrating language SDKs into isolated runtime images, and stabilizing pinned toolchains. This ticket covers discovery, prototype, rollout plan, and metrics instrumentation to validate reduced median build time and lower cache miss rates.

acceptance_criteria:
Define and document three BuildKit profile templates: dev-fast, ci-stable, and release-optimized
Create per-language runtime images for Node/Python/Go with deterministic toolchain installs and SBOMs
Implement layered cache hints and cache-priming job such that CI median build time decreases by >= 30% for common changesets
Add observability: per-job cache hit rate, build latency P50/P95, and CI cost per-merge to the CI dashboard
Roll out migration to 20% of repos as canary and demonstrate zero increase in test flakiness during canary window

progress_updates:
2025-11-04: Kickoff meeting with Infra, DX, and Runtime teams. Aligned on goals and metrics. Agreed to use BuildKit advanced features (cache mounts + export/import).
2025-11-18: Completed audit of top 40 slowest repos. Identified common cache-miss patterns: language install, yarn/pip resolution, docker-layer-churn from monorepo Dockerfiles.
2025-12-02: Prototype dev-fast and ci-stable BuildKit profiles in a small demo repo (redwood-sample). Observed P50 improvement ~28% and P95 ~15% on repeated runs.
2026-01-15: Built canonical Node/Python runtime images with pinned toolchain versions, reproducible installs, and SBOMs. Images published to internal registry with TTL 90 days and immutable tags.
2026-02-02: Implemented cache-priming pipeline scheduled nightly for frequently touched base layers (node-modules, pip-wheel-cache). Increased cache hit rate in demo repos from 42% to 71%.
2026-02-20: Security review requested for publishing runtime images (KMS encryption of credentials). Security Q/A completed; minor changes required to image build job.
2026-03-01: Draft rollout plan for canary (20% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on flakiness spike or build-time regression. Dashboard panels and alert rules created.
2026-03-10: Started canary on five medium-size services. Early telemetry: median build time -33%, cache hit rate +22 points. Observed one flaky test unrelated to build changes; triage opened ENG-90912.

risks:
Pinned toolchains may lag security updates if not on a regular rotation schedule
Cache priming increases cluster egress and storage costs if not bounded by retention policies
Monorepo Dockerfiles with non-deterministic ordering can still cause cache misses until refactored
Canary could expose hidden flakiness in tests that only manifest with faster builds (timing-sensitive tests)

comments:
Amelia Park (2025-11-05): Initial scope laid out; infra will own registry publishing and retention policy.
Lina Chen (2025-12-05): Reviewed prototype, suggested adding deterministic yarn.lock integrity check step to image builds.
Samir Patel (2026-01-28): Ops requested an opt-out label for particularly brittle repos during canary.
Product (Maya Singh) (2026-02-22): Approved rollout plan pending security sign-off and dashboard coverage.
Diego Morales (2026-03-10): Canary started for services: auth-service, gateway, ingestion-worker, analytics-collector, embeddings-proxy. Monitoring closely.
Security (Janet Wu) (2026-02-05): Image publish pipeline needs to rotate GPG keys every 90 days. Added to follow-up tasks.

Cascadia RFP: BYOK/HSM integration details and test plan

["From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Fiona Wu <fiona.wu@cascadia-fin.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Initial BYOK/HSM integration questions + proposed test plan

Hi Fiona —

Thanks for including Redwood in the Cascadia RFP. To keep the BYOK portion of the security questionnaire moving, here's a short summary of the implementation options we support and a list of the items we'd need from you to validate integration during the procurement phase. Attached: BYOK-Integration-Diagram.pdf

What Redwood supports (short):
- Customer-managed keys: support for KMIP-backed HSMs and PKCS#11 where customers expose a KMIP proxy.
- Wrapped-key model: Redwood can accept customer-wrapped DEKs (AES-GCM key wrap) with short-lived unwrapping via a customer-provided HSM or a split-wrapping flow.
- Live attestation: optional remote attestation for supported HSMs (CloudHSM, Thales, Utimaco).
- TLS: mTLS (TLS 1.3) for HSM control channel; server authentication + client cert pinning supported.

Items we need from Cascadia to proceed:
1) HSM vendor and model (make/model + firmware) and FIPS 140-2/3 cert (PDF).
2) KMIP endpoint(s) (host:port), or PKCS#11 details if applicable; if behind a proxy, doc on proxy config.
3) HSM serial numbers for test units and an expected concurrency/ops/sec number for unwrap/wrap calls.
4) Preferred BYOK workflow: a) full-wrap + send DEKs, b) remote unwrapping via peered HSM, or c) split key (Redwood partial key + customer partial key).
5) Windows for an integration test (recommended 3 half-day windows).

Proposed Redwood test plan (high level):
- Day 0: exchange certs and validate TLS/mTLS handshake.
- Day 1: basic KMIP/PKCS#11 smoke tests, prove key creation/list/attributes.
- Day 2: wrap/unwrap performance and load verification, verify metadata (key usage, exportability).
- Day 3: rotation & fallback test (rotate DEK, ensure continued decrypt for existing tokens during alias window).

Could you confirm which BYOK workflow you prefer and send over the HSM certs/endpoint details to the Drive link? Once we have that, we can lock a test week and produce an HSM interop checklist.

Thanks —
Sooj
Soojin Lee
Security Programs Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Hi Sooj —

Thanks for the clear summary. Cascadia will pursue the wrapped-key flow initially (option a) — our cryptographic operations must remain under our HSM. We can provide the following now:
- HSM vendor/model: Thales nShield Edge (firmware 5.2.1).
- FIPS 140-2 Level 2 certificate (attached).
- KMIP endpoint: kmip.cascadia-fin.local:5696 (we will provide NAT/routable address for the test window).
- Estimated unwrap throughput: 200 ops/sec sustained, peak ~500 ops/sec.
- Test unit serials: E-TH-98432 (test1), E-TH-98433 (test2).

Questions from our side:
1) For the wrapped-key model, do you require Redwood to validate HSM attestation or is the FIPS cert + serial sufficient for procurement?
2) Is the TLS requirement mutual TLS with client certs generated by Cascadia CA, or do you need per-host pinning?

I'll upload the packages (Cascadia-HSM-Certificates.zip) to the Drive link you provided by EOD. We can do July 13-17 for the integration window.

—Fiona
Fiona Wu
Senior Manager, IT Security
Cascadia Financial
fiona.wu@cascadia-fin.com

---
Attachment: Cascadia-HSM-Certificates.zip (contains FIPS cert PDF and vendor attestation)", "From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Fiona Wu <fiona.wu@cascadia-fin.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial BYOK/HSM integration questions + proposed test plan

Fiona —

Appreciate the details. Quick technical clarifications from the runtime/ops side:
- We can support the wrapped-key flow where Cascadia performs the unwrap inside its HSM and returns wrapped DEKs to Redwood, or Redwood can be configured to call your KMIP endpoint to perform unwrapping via KMIP import/wrap-key semantics. For the latter we will need a routable endpoint and a secure channel (mTLS) with mutual auth.
- Our preferred cipher/transport: TLS 1.3 (RFC8446), AEAD cipher suites (TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 or TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384). We also support TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 with per-host cert pinning.
- For KMIP: we use client cert + basic KMIP username/password fallback; we prefer PKCS#11 only when you can provide a bridge/proxy that exposes a KMIP API.

Operational asks for the test window:
1) Provide routable KMIP host and a VPN or peered VPC path for Redwood test instances (we prefer a private VPC peering for throughput tests).
2) Confirm whether the HSM will accept our client certs signed by your CA or whether Cascadia will issue per-host client certs for Redwood test machines.
3) Share expected key attributes (algorithm, key length, usage flags) for the DEKs we will be exchanging.

One note on attestation: if Cascadia can provide the FIPS cert + module serial + vendor statement, that meets procurement in most cases. For production we recommend remote attestation; if Cascadia has a ReadyAttest or similar capability, we can add that as an option.

I'll draft a short HSM interop checklist and circulate (will attach to the thread).

Thanks,
Marcus
Principal Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

records.title: SDK Patch Release Playbook and Compatibility Rules
records.text:
SDK Patch Release Playbook and Compatibility Rules

Overview:

This playbook describes the lightweight, repeatable process we use to ship SDK patch releases (hotfixes, security patches, backward-compatible minor fixes) and the compatibility rules that must be enforced by the devx team. The goal is to minimize user impact, ensure consistent docs/website updates, and provide a clear triage + rollback path for incidents tied to SDK releases.

When to use this playbook:
- Patches for regressions in Official Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) that affect runtime correctness or cause high-severity developer experience regressions (errors in auth, streaming breaking, incorrect typing).
- Security fixes in dependency tree that require immediate release.
- Minor quality-of-life fixes that need to go out in the next patch window (semver PATCH).

High-level constraints and rules:
1) Semver policy: follow semver strictly. Patches must be release-type PATCH and must not introduce public API changes. Any change that modifies signature/behavior requires MINOR and must go through the normal feature release cadence.
2) Compatibility matrix: maintainers must run the automated compat matrix against supported runtime targets before cutting a release. Supported targets: Python 3.9–3.11, Node 16/18, Go 1.19–1.21.
3) Documentation parity: every published patch must include a docs-site short changelog entry and, where relevant, updated API snippets and migration notes.
4) Telemetry & opt-in beta flags: if a fix touches telemetry or experimental features, include an explicit opt-in flag and a developer note in the changelog.

Release checklist (short-form):
- [ ] Confirm issue severity and categorize as PATCH-worthy (owner + eng oncall)
- [ ] Create release branch: release/sdk/<sdk>-patch-YYYYMMDD-<issue-id>
- [ ] Update changelog entry (docs short entry + repo CHANGELOG.md)
- [ ] Run unit + integration + compatibility matrix tests (see below)
- [ ] Run package signing and vulnerability scan (SNYK/OSV)
- [ ] Publish pre-release to internal package registry for Canary users (npm:@redwood/sdk-canary, pypi:internal/test)
- [ ] Monitor canary for 24 hours (or agreed observation window)
- [ ] Publish public patch, update docs-site, tag release, notify #devx-releases
- [ ] Update support KB and canonical fixes list

Step-by-step playbook: detailed procedure

Phase A — Triage and branch
1) Triage in issue tracker: assign severity, set target release date (ASAP or next daily patch window).
2) Label issue with "patch-candidate" and create a short patch RFC in PR description describing the fix and verifying non-breaking guarantee.
3) Create release branch from main: git checkout -b release/sdk/<sdk>-patch-YYYYMMDD-<issue-id>

Phase B — Development and testing
1) Code: keep changes scoped; avoid refactors. Ensure public API surface untouched (types, exported functions).
2) Local test matrix: run full unit suite + integration mocks. Commands:
- Python: tox -e py39,py310,py311
- Node: npm run test --all-targets (Node 16/18 via nvm use)
- Go: go test ./... -tags=integration
3) Compatibility matrix job (CI): must succeed before merge. Matrix includes:
- installing SDK into blank sample apps for each runtime version
- running a small prompt/streaming sample against the staging Redwood hosted endpoint
- verifying artifact sizes and ABI-compatible native deps

Phase C — Canary and verification
1) Publish to internal registry with canary tag. Example commands:
- npm publish --tag canary --registry https://npm.internal.redwood.local
- python -m pip wheel . && twine upload --repository-url https://pypi.internal.redwood.local --verbose dist/* --skip-existing --repository test
2) Notify canary users and DevX stakeholders with instructions to opt-in. Provide sample install snippets for each SDK.
3) Monitoring: watch these signals for 24 hours (or configured window):
- telemetry error rate (alert if > 2x baseline)
- support tickets referencing the new canary
- automated smoke test failures in downstream integrations

Phase D — Publish and post-release tasks
1) Tag release: git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "Patch: <short-desc>" && git push --tags origin release/...
2) Create release on GitHub/GitLab and attach artifacts (wheels, tarballs).
3) Update docs-site: add short changelog on /docs/sdk/changelog and update any affected API examples. Use docs-site cli: docsctl release-changelog --sdk <sdk> --version X.Y.Z --notes "<one-line>"
4) Post to #devx-releases with step-by-step summary and links to docs + artifact.
5) Mark issue resolved and link release artifacts in ticket.

Rollback and emergency mitigation:
- If a critical regression is detected post-release (error rate spike, data corruption, major functionality broken), follow emergency rollback:
  1) Revert tag and release on package registry: npm deprecate <pkg>@X.Y.Z "broken release"; publish X.Y.Z-rc2 if needed.
  2) Inform SRE and Eng Oncall and open incident (link to confluence incident template).
  3) Roll forward hotfix only if root cause understood; otherwise publish a tiny shim that restores previous behavior without wide feature changes.

Standards for API changes in patches (must be followed):
- No signature removal.
- No behavior inversion (e.g. change default of boolean).
- Only internal helpers may be added.
- If a necessary fix modifies behavior for correctness, include an automated compatibility test demonstrating prior behavior problem and new behavior expectation.

Canonical support triage mapping (common patch-related support issues and fixes):
1) Auth errors after SDK upgrade
   - Likely causes: dependency bump changed default header; user-perceived error: 401/403.
   - Quick fix: Verify token header key, roll back dependency to previous working version, publish immediate patch that restores header mapping.
2) Streaming stalls or truncated chunks
   - Cause: changed chunk framing or backpressure handling in streaming helper.
   - Fix: revert to previous chunking loop and add test that streams 10k tokens in CI sample app.
3) TypeScript types not matching runtime
   - Cause: .d.ts generation change.
   - Fix: pin types generation step in release pipeline; republish patch with correct types only.

Changelog and release notes templates (short):
- Title: SDK <sdk> vX.Y.Z (patch) — YYYY-MM-DD
- One-line summary: Fixes authentication header regression causing 401s in streaming scenarios.
- Backwards compatibility: fully compatible (semver PATCH).
- Impact: users on >= vX.Y.(Z-1) should upgrade; no migration steps required.
- Snippets: (include pre/post example if behavior changed in edge case)

Sample PR description snippet to copy into PR body:
"""
Patch PR: <one-line>
Related Issue: #<id>
Motivation: short explanation of why this is a patch (no public API changes)
Testing: unit + integration + compat matrix results (link to CI)
Canary plan: list of canary users / internal packages to test
Rollback plan: steps to revert should regression be observed
"""

Ops & docs-site considerations (must not be skipped):
- Docs update minimal: add one-line changelog entry and update code snippets if they were modified. Avoid changing example app flows for patches unless required.
- Docs deployment: staging -> smoke -> prod. Use docsctl preview and verify sample pages referencing the SDK examples.

Automation and CI jobs required for every patch:
- patch-compat-matrix (parallel matrix across runtimes)
- patch-canary-publish (internal registry publish)
- patch-vuln-scan (SNYK/OSV)
- patch-sign-artifacts (GPG/HSM signing)

Compatibility matrix example (ASCII table):
| SDK | Python 3.9 | Python 3.10 | Python 3.11 | Node 16 | Node 18 | Go 1.20 |
|-----|-----------:|-----------:|-----------:|--------:|--------:|-------:|
| python-sdk | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| node-sdk | n/a | n/a | n/a | ✅ | ✅ | n/a |
| go-sdk | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | ✅ |

Common QA tests (smoke):
- auth flow test (happy path + expired token)
- streaming smoke test (1 token, 1k tokens, intermittent network)
- embeddings encode/decode roundtrip (for embedding SDKs)
- example app integration test (install SDK and run sample end-to-end request)

Maintenance: periodic items
- Quarterly review of supported runtimes and update matrix (owner: devx-maintainers).
- Archive canary tags older than 30 days.
- Monthly run of 'compat drift' job that installs latest SDKs into sample apps and reports warnings for any runtime deprecations.

Appendix A — Example CLI snippets and release commands
- Create branch: git checkout -b release/sdk/python-patch-20260203-1234
- Bump version: poetry version patch && git commit -am "bump: patch X.Y.Z"
- Build wheel and sign: python -m build && gpg --detach-sign --armor dist/*
- Publish (internal): twine upload --repository-url https://pypi.internal.redwood.local dist/*

Appendix B — Example automated changelog entry (YAML snippet used by docsctl):
changelog_entry: |
  - sdk: python
    version: "X.Y.Z"
    date: "2026-02-03"
    summary: "Fix streaming header regression affecting auth for long-running streams."
    compatibility: "patch"

Contact and ownership:
- Primary owners: devx-releases@redwood.internal (team)
- Secondary: runtime-team@redwood.internal (for runtime-related regressions)

If you are uncertain whether a change qualifies as a patch, escalate to the devx oncall and include a short compatibility justification in the PR description.

records.title: eng-runtime
records.text:
eng-runtime

alex: quick follow-up on the stalled-prefetch backoff idea i posted earlier — sketched a small proposal for a cooldown+coalesce heuristic to avoid noisy prefetch storms when resident sets are tight.

maria: can you paste the config sketch? curious how you'd tune cooldown vs coalesce window.

alex: sure — basic idea: track per-tenant prefetch stalls (prefetch requested but page already queued or IO in-flight). increment a stall counter, trigger exponential cooldown on subsequent prefetches for that tenant until stall counter decays. also batch coalesce windows when cooldown active to reduce tiny IOs.

alex: code sketch:
```
# config for prefetch backoff/coalesce
prefetch_backoff:
  base_cooldown_ms: 50
  max_cooldown_ms: 2000
  stall_threshold: 3
  decay_half_life_s: 30
coalesce:
  base_window_ms: 5
  max_window_ms: 100
  expand_factor_on_cooldown: 4
```

tj: makes sense. sequence length / request concurrency will affect these numbers a lot. did you simulate on 1k qps with bursty tails?

alex: i ran a small local sim — workload with frequent KV cache misses + 10–20 request concurrency per tenant. result: p50 unchanged, p95 ~ +1–2ms, p99 improved by ~6% vs always-prefetch strategy (we avoid dozens of 1–2ms IOs at the tail).

sam: interesting. how does this interact with our KV cache and existing auto-batcher? if we coalesce in software we may duplicate work with hardware-level batching.

alex: good point. plan is to expose a hint to the runtime's batcher: when tenant is in cooldown, the prefetch hint becomes "defer" and the batcher treats it as low priority and tries to coalesce into the next batch window. if the hardware/GPU runtime already coalesces, the hint is a no-op.

maria: any concerns with fairness? a noisy tenant might get stuck in cooldown and starve others if their demotions are aggressive.

alex: fairness handled two ways: 1) cooldown is tenant-scoped only (we don't global-suppress prefetch for the whole host), 2) cooldown uses decay so a single recovery request quickly reduces stall counter. also we limit max cooldown to avoid indefinitely delaying critical inf requests.

natalie: what about fragmented pages — coalesce window may pull adjacent pages and increase fragmentation churn if we do lots of small compactions after.

alex: coalesce is read-side only (we're coalescing prefetch IOs). write-path compaction would be unchanged. but i added a guard: if host fragmentation metric (prometheus: host_fragmentation_ratio) > 0.6, reduce expand_factor_on_cooldown to 1 to avoid large fanouts.

sam: could we expose a per-tenant opt-out? some latency-sensitive customers may prefer always-prefetch.

alex: yes — expose policy: prefetch_policy = [always, cooldown-aware, disabled]. default cooldown-aware.

infra-bot: ci/build #5621 passed — diff includes prefetch backoff config + unit tests.

tj: test plan? need e2e with a mixed-tenant slow-storage case (simulate NVMe saturations) and a microbench for p99 change.

alex: test plan in PR: unit tests for stall counter decay + integration that replays a trace with bursts (script included). e2e: run small cluster with fio-backed slow tier and synthetic clients to measure tail.

maria: can you add a telemetry tag to the cooldown events? we want a counter and histogram of cooldown durations per-tenant so we can tune in prod.

alex: will add: metric pref.backoff.cooldown_count{tenant,reason}, and pref.backoff.duration_ms histogram. also a debug log at info when tenant crosses stall_threshold.

natalie: one last thing — make sure rollout plan includes a canary with dedicated pool so we can observe cross-tenant effects before global rollout.

alex: agreed. canary plan: 5% of traffic on dedicated pool, monitor p99, IO ops/sec, host_fragmentation_ratio, and pref.backoff.* metrics for 6h. rollback if p99 degrades >5% or fragmentation increases >10%.

sam: :thumbsup: if we keep the default conservative and have solid telemetry this seems low-risk.

alex: i'll open the PR with the config + tests + telemetry and tag you all. thanks for quick feedback.

maria: thanks — quick nit: call the config field prefetch_cooldown instead of prefetch_backoff to avoid confusion with network-level backoff.

alex: noted, will rename in PR.

infra-bot: deploy-preview created: https://ci.redwood/preview/5621

sam: cool — feel free to @me on the PR if you want pairing for the e2e script.

alex: will do.

records.title: Serialized window shard mismatch causing cross-service throttling and customer outages
records.text:
Serialized window shard mismatch causing cross-service throttling and customer outages

description:
Summary: On 2026-03-12 we observed a surge of opaque 429s across multiple tenants in Hosted and Dedicated. Investigation shows a mismatch in how rate-window state was serialized and sharded between the edge proxy layer and the quota orchestrator. The mismatch caused window epochs to diverge during a partial orchestrator upgrade, leading to large numbers of requests evaluated against an expired/sharded window and resulting in premature throttles. Several high-volume customers opened escalations reporting persistent throttling for 10–45 minutes. This ticket documents investigation, mitigations, root cause, and long-term remediation plan.

impact:
Multiple high-volume tenants experienced sustained request failures (429) for 10–45 minutes during peak traffic. A subset of Dedicated customers reported SLA violations and elevated support escalations. Estimated revenue impact: medium (customers on dedicated committed capacity were rate-limited unexpectedly). Operational overhead: pager rotations and manual rollbacks on two clusters.

reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy orchestrator with mixed version (old/new) while edge proxies have continuous per-tenant window serialization format A.
2) Send traffic with burst patterns (hundreds of QPS per tenant) and observe quota ledger entries created on both versions.
3) Trigger a reconciliation flow (orchestrator leader handoff) that forces partial replay/merge of shard state.
4) Observe divergence: proxies evaluate token bucket using epoch X while orchestrator believes epoch X+1 and rejects requests as exhausted.

observed_signals_and_logs:
- Spike in 429 rate across regions starting 2026-03-12T01:17Z.
- Orchestrator leader handoff logs show 'applied-epoch: 37412' and proxies report 'window-epoch: 37411' for same tenant.
- Quota ledger snapshots indicate missing epoch delta reconciliations for sharded keys.
- Support tickets and escalations: #TICKET-2345, #TICKET-2346 from major customers.
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123 (rollback performed).

root_cause_summary:
During a rolling upgrade to introduce compact serialization for window shards, we introduced a version negotiation bug: the orchestrator accepted compact shards and wrote a newer epoch semantics into the centralized ledger, but the edge proxy deserializer fell back to legacy interpretation for shards with a particular flag. This produced asymmetric epoch advancement across services. The reconciliation logic incorrectly assumed idempotence across formats and skipped epoch-gap correction when encountering the legacy flag, resulting in stale window state being evaluated as current and causing premature quota exhaustion.

mitigations_applied:
1) Emergency rollback of orchestrator change to previous serialization format in affected clusters (completed 2026-03-12T02:05Z).
2) Short-lived global bypass: edge proxies temporarily accepted both formats and bypassed strict epoch checks for 5 minutes during reconciliation window.
3) Replayed ledger snapshots to correct epoch counters for tenants that saw divergence.
4) Customer comms: sent incident bulletin to affected customers and opened dedicated support threads.
5) Added a temporary monitoring rule to alert on epoch drift > 0 for a tenant for more than 2 minutes.

long_term_fix:
1) Implement compatible forward/backward schema for window shards with explicit version headers and a robust negotiation handshake.
2) Harden reconciliation logic: do not skip epoch-gap correction when encountering unknown flags; instead, surface to orchestrator and perform deterministic merge.
3) Add end-to-end integration tests (proxy+orchestrator+reconciliation) that exercise mixed-format rolling upgrades.
4) Add unit tests around serialization/epoch semantics and fuzz tests for shard boundaries.
5) Plan phased rollout with feature gate and canary traffic at 1% with automated rollback on epoch-drift alerts.

testing_plan:
- Local integration matrix: proxy v1/v2 x orchestrator v1/v2 with simulated traffic patterns and leader handoffs.
- Staging canary: deploy changes to staging cluster, enable feature gate for a small set of tenants, run load generator mimicking customer burst profiles.
- Blue-green controlled rollouts in prod with traffic ramp and epoch-drift gating; require zero occurrences of drift > 1 minute before expanding.
- Post-deploy regression: run nightly chaos test that simulates leader failovers and sharded ledger merges.

rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Merge and run full integration tests (2 days).
Phase 1: Canary (1% tenants) with feature gate and automatic rollback on alert (3 days).
Phase 2: Progressive rollout to remaining clusters with monitoring escalations (5 days).
Contingency: Immediate rollback to legacy serialization in any cluster with drift or customer reports.

monitoring_and_kpis:
429 rate by tenant and region
epoch-drift per-tenant
leader-handoff latency
quota-correction events per hour
customer-reported throttles

timeline:
2026-03-12 01:10Z - first alerts; 01:22Z - identified orchestrator serialization change as suspect; 01:50Z - emergency rollback initiated; 02:05Z - rollback completed; 02:30Z - ledger replay and corrections finished; 03:00Z - alerts subsided. Postmortem drafting started same day.

decision_notes:
We elected to roll back rather than attempt in-place conversion because the rollback path had a lower risk envelope and allowed deterministic ledger correction. The long-term plan is to add explicit schema versions and reconcile on epoch gaps rather than skipping. Product concurs that this must be prioritized before the next runtime release.

next_steps:
Implement schema-version header and negotiation (owner: Marco Chen, estimate: 8 pts)
Add reconciliation failure telemetry and automatic correction scripts (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 5 pts)
Build mixed-version integration test harness and include in CI (owner: Diego Ramos, estimate: 3 pts)
Update runbook and incident playbook for epoch-drift events (owner: SRE team, estimate: 2 pts)
Customer outreach follow-up and SLA remediation proposals (owner: Customer Success, estimate: 2 pts)

comments:
2026-03-12 01:30 - Aisha Patel: Initial triage indicates serialization change correlated with incident window.
2026-03-12 01:55 - Marco Chen: Started rollback of orchestrator change; coordinating ledger replay.
2026-03-12 02:10 - Priya Nair: Applied temporary proxy tolerance for legacy shards; monitoring for side-effects.
2026-03-13 09:20 - Diego Ramos: Integration test harness prototype pushed to infra branch; needs review.
2026-03-14 11:00 - PM Lead Sofia Gonzales: Approved prioritization in next sprint; flagged for runtime-1.20 release gating.

records.title: Half-open socket flood after model-variant swap causing burst 5xx and streaming drops
records.text:
Half-open socket flood after model-variant swap causing burst 5xx and streaming drops

description:
Issue summary: Acme Health observed a sharp rise in 5xx responses and frequent streaming session drops beginning 2026-03-10 02:15 UTC following a customer-initiated model-variant switch. The spike was concentrated in eu-west and impacted active streaming chat sessions and large-embedding uploads.

Impact: ~18% elevated 5xx rate for the tenant over a 30-minute window, ~12% of active streaming sessions terminated early (socket resets). Customer reports production user-facing errors and increased latency.

Initial triage: Support escalated to SRE at 02:35 UTC after customer provided request IDs and trace samples. No scheduled platform deploys were shown in the tenant's control plane around the time of the spike; however an automated model-variant swap for the customer's pinned route completed at 02:12 UTC and triggered a tenant warmup burst.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer pins a route to a new model variant and triggers warmup/prefetch.
2) Warmup creates short-lived high-concurrency prefetch requests that flood connection pools.
3) Under sustained warmup plus concurrent customer traffic, the API gateway accept queue begins to backlog and many downstream proxies start returning 502/503.
4) Streaming sessions hit half-closed socket conditions and get reset when upstream runtime threads block on connection cleanup.

Note: We reproduced a similar failure in staging by running the customer's warmup script (prefetch=8x baseline for 30s) combined with ongoing streaming traffic at 60 concurrent streams.

logs:
Excerpt of correlated logs (masked):
[2026-03-10T02:12:09Z] route-manager: variant-swap completed route=/customers/acme-tenant route_id=rt-abc123
[2026-03-10T02:12:33Z] apigw: accept_queue_length=128/1024 conn_backlog=95 thread_pool_util=92% route=rt-abc123
[2026-03-10T02:13:05Z] proxy[ephemeral-17]: tcp_half_open_count=64 keepalive_reaped=0
[2026-03-10T02:13:17Z] runtime: kvcache_lock_wait_ms=2100 gpu_watchdog_reset=false pid=23456
[2026-03-10T02:14:41Z] apigw: outbound_error=502 upstream=proxy/ephemeral-17 details=\"connection_reset\"
[2026-03-10T02:16:02Z] sres-alarms: tenant_rt-abc123_5xx_rate=0.18 threshold=0.03

Stack traces and full logs uploaded to support bundle: s3://support-bundles/SUP-163845/2026-03-10/supp_bundle.tar.gz

timeline:
2026-03-10 02:12 UTC - Customer-initiated model-variant swap triggered automated prefetch/warmup.
2026-03-10 02:15 UTC - Customer reported elevated errors (first contact).
2026-03-10 02:20 UTC - Support collected traces and escalated to SRE.
2026-03-10 02:30 UTC - Reproduced in staging with synthetic warmup+stream load.
2026-03-10 03:05 UTC - Hotfix (apigw threadpool pruning fix + temporary accept_queue sizing) rolled out to eu-west.
2026-03-10 03:20 UTC - Customer traffic returned to baseline; streaming disconnects dropped to <1%.
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC - Post-incident review and runbook items created.

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: Sudden warmup prefetch created a burst of short-lived connections that exposed a latent bug in connection pool pruning logic in the API gateway. The bug left half-open sockets in the ephemeral proxy (keepalive not reclaimed), creating accept_queue pressure and causing downstream runtime threads to block on socket cleanup while kvcache locks contended.

What we checked:
- apigw thread pool and accept queue metrics (elevated during window).
- proxy half-open socket counts (spike concurrent with warmup).
- runtime kvcache lock wait and prefetch latencies (elevated).
- GPU watchdog and driver logs (no driver resets observed).

Staging reproduction: By replaying the customer's warmup script while streaming 60 concurrent session simulations we observed quick growth in tcp_half_open_count and an apigw thread_pool exhaustion that produced 502s and forced runtime request cancellations. This reproduced core symptoms (502/503, streaming resets).

Root cause: combination of aggressive prefetch/warmup traffic pattern for this tenant + a connection-pruning bug in apigw that failed to reclaim half-closed sockets rapidly enough, producing accept-queue saturation and upstream request cancellations.

workaround:
1) Applied a temporary tenant-level rate cap on warmup/prefetch to smooth ramp.
2) Increased apigw accept_queue sizing for eu-west domain and tuned keepalive reclaim interval to be more aggressive.
3) Customer temporarily reduced prefetch multiplier from 8x to 2x while we validated the fix.

resolution:
Deployed hotfix 2026-03-10 03:05 UTC: apigw PR merged (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428) which:
- fixes connection pool pruning bug that left half-open sockets unreclaimed,
- improves threadpool pruning heuristics to prevent starvation under warmup bursts,
- adds a short-term mitigation to backpressure new warmup requests when accept_queue occupancy exceeds threshold.
After rollout, accept_queue occupancy dropped and 5xx rates returned to baseline for the tenant. Customer verified recovery and we kept the temporary tenant prefetch cap for 24h as a precaution.

Post-incident: change merged and monitored for 48h; no regressions observed. Incident closed 2026-03-12 after postmortem review.

follow_up_actions:
- Add a runbook section for model-variant warmup patterns and recommended tenant prefetch limits.
- Implement an automated alarm that triggers when apigw accept_queue > 70% and tcp_half_open_count rises for >60s.
- Add an integration test simulating large warmup bursts with concurrent streaming to catch regressions.
- Coordinate with product to provide guidance to customers on safe prefetch multipliers for enterprise/private tiers.
- Schedule postmortem doc and share with SRE and Solutions Engineering teams.

root_cause:
Bug in API gateway connection-pruning logic combined with aggressive tenant warmup (prefetch) behavior leading to persistent half-open sockets, accept-queue saturation, and cascading upstream cancellations.

comments:
Priya Nair (Support) 2026-03-10T02:17Z: Customer reports 502s and streaming drops. Collected request IDs and asked for recent route edit history.
Liam Chen (SRE) 2026-03-10T02:40Z: Triage: seeing accept_queue and half-open socket spikes in eu-west. Spinning up staging repro now.
Elena Rodriguez (ProdEng) 2026-03-10T02:55Z: Found connection-pruning edge-case; sending PR for hotfix. Need quick canary rollout to eu-west only.
Acme Health (Customer) 2026-03-10T03:30Z: Confirmed traffic back to normal after your mitigation; thanks for rapid response. We'll keep warmup reduced until you confirm postmortem.
Liam Chen (SRE) 2026-03-12T09:58Z: Postmortem published and runbook updated: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Runbook+-+Ingress+Backpressure+Tuning

finance

elaine (Finance): Heads-up: Helios Bio flagged a big jump in their Nov invoice after they shifted some workloads to 'auto-scale nodes' in their private deployment. They say platform fees should apply to their committed GPU-hours (per MSA), not raw node-hours. Can ops + legal triage for a provisional true-up?

omar (AE): I got a note from Priya (customer billing). She attached the invoice and said they only changed orchestration type for staging clusters. They're worried churn if we don't respond quickly.

sasha (Solutions): Quick diagnostic: their cluster resource labels switched and our metering started emitting metric_key=node_compute_hours for that account. Our ETL treats node_compute_hours as billable usage by default.

billing-bot: Invoice 992201 created for HLS-321. Invoice total: $98,100. Line: Platform fee = $18,300.

sasha (Solutions): Ran a metering aggregate for Nov:

```
SELECT sum(node_hours) AS n FROM metering.events
WHERE account = 'HLS-321' AND ts BETWEEN '2024-11-01' AND '2024-11-30';
-- n = 9,720 node_hours
```

Using Helios commit mapping (commit = 3 x A100 equivalent) -> gpu-hour equivalent ~= 3,000 gpu_hours. Recomputed platform fee under committed basis comes to ~$7,700.

elaine (Finance): So delta ~ $10.6k? We can approve provisional credits < $15k without director sign-off. Please compute precise delta and open a credit request.

matt (CustSuccess): I'll tell Priya we'll acknowledge within 24 hours and issue a provisional memo while you audit. She appreciates quick fixes.

sasha (Solutions): Final numbers: node-based platform fee = $18,300; committed-equivalent platform fee = $7,700; delta = $10,600. I documented the conversion, linked internal mapping: /internal/billing/committed-mapping/helios-2024-11.md, and raised infra ticket to apply fallback mapping for accounts with active commits.

elaine (Finance): Opening provisional credit CR-2024-772 for $10,600, to be applied to Invoice 992201 as "platform fee reconciliation provisional credit". Will tag as reversible after audit.

zoe (Legal): I reviewed Helios_Bio_MSA_2023. Section 4.2 references 'Committed GPU capacity' and doesn't list node-hours. Good to provisionally credit while we confirm. I'll draft a one-paragraph confirmation to the customer noting provisional status and reversal conditions.

billing-bot: Credit request CR-2024-772 created. Status: pending_approval.

elaine (Finance): Please attach the customer's invoice PDF and any commit docs to the credit request. Also include reference CM-2024-301 for the provisional credit memo once approved.

omar (AE): Uploaded invoice_pdf and the customer's commit confirmation email. Customer agrees to provisional memo while they pull their infra logs.

sasha (Solutions): Action items: 1) PR to billing ETL to apply node->gpu conversion when account has commit flag (I will add test vectors); 2) add alert to detect metric_key changes for committed accounts; 3) finish internal audit within 3 business days.

matt (CustSuccess): Marking the account with a revenue risk flag until final reconciliation. I'll follow up with Priya after you issue the provisional memo.

billing-bot: Credit memo CM-2024-301 issued for $10,600 against Invoice 992201. Status: PROVISIONAL.

elaine (Finance): Approved provisional credit. We'll keep this thread updated with audit findings; if mapping is validated in our favor, we'll reverse the CM and bill the customer for the small differential. Thanks team.

zoe (Legal): Sent draft note to Priya and copied Omar.

omar (AE): Customer update planned for EOD today.

sasha (Solutions): PR and alert created: infra/PR#584, monitoring alert ID: METRIC_KEY_CHANGE_HLS-321.

elaine (Finance): Closing action for now; will re-open if audit changes the numbers.

records.title: POC traffic orchestration & token-mix scoping - LyricSoft
records.text:
POC traffic orchestration & token-mix scoping - LyricSoft

Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-18
Start time: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Jimenez (Redwood SE), Leah O'Connor (Redwood Solutions), Anika Bose (LyricSoft Head of ML), Tom Whittaker (Platform Engineer), Priya Rao (CTO), Jared Kim (SRE)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to align on workload shape, success criteria, benchmarks and timeline. Focus: QPS/concurrency targets, input/output token distributions, tail latency targets, and what data replay artifacts LyricSoft can provide. Agreed to run traffic replay using Redwood replay kit; SE to map baseline capacity and propose dedicated vs hosted tradeoff.

Topics covered:
- Current production traffic shape and variability
- Typical prompt/input sizes and output token distributions
- Target QPS and concurrency for POC (steady-state + burst)
- Success criteria: latency p95/p99, error rates, cost per 1k tokens
- Benchmark plan & timeline
- Security and data residency questions

Action items (recap):
- Maya: send benchmark template + instructions (replay tool)
- Tom: provide 48 hours of anonymized traffic (CSV) + sample prompts
- Carlos: prepare capacity mapping and SLA proposals for two scenarios (hosted + dedicated)
- Leah: include SOC2 docs and encryption/KMS notes

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick introductions? We have Maya and Carlos from Redwood, Leah here too.
[00:06] Anika: Hi, yes Anika from LyricSoft. We're excited — been looking at Redwood for inference cost and tail latency stuff.
[00:11] Tom: Tom here. I'll be owner for the traffic artifacts.
[00:15] Priya: Priya, CTO. I'll be on high-level success criteria. Jared's on for SRE questions.
[00:20] Maya: Great. The goal today is to scope a POC to run a traffic replay and measure tail latency and throughput, and to define success criteria. Can you tell us current QPS and typical concurrency?
[00:32] Anika: Sure. Peak user facing QPS is around 220 QPS during business hours, but the back of our pipeline hits spiky bursts up to 900 QPS for short periods, like 10 to 30 seconds. Average is more like 45 QPS. Concurrency per model instance is a hard number because we multiplex requests across microservices.
[00:50] Carlos: When you say "spiky bursts", are those sustained or short microbursts? 900 for 10 to 30 seconds suggests very bursty. That matters for auto-scale.
[00:58] Anika: Right, short microbursts. Also we have heavy tail tokens when users ask for summaries — output tokens can be 800 to 1,200 but median is 210. Input prompts are usually 60 to 120 tokens.
[01:12] Maya: Ok interesting. So token distribution is skewed — lots of short responses and a few very long responses. For the POC we usually ask for a 48 hour traffic sample, anonymized, with timestamps and token counts per request. That lets us build a QPS surface and a burst profile.
[01:28] Tom: We can do that. We'll need the exact CSV schema.
[01:31] Maya: I'll send the template after the call. It includes epoch ms timestamp, input_tokens, output_tokens, model_hint, and a sample prompt id.
[01:40] Jared: Quick security note — we need to be clear on what data leaves our VPC. LyricSoft prefers Private deployment for PII-sensitive prompts.
[01:50] Leah: We can run the replay from your VPC using a private deployment connector. But for initial benchmarking hosted mode is faster to iterate. There is a tradeoff.
[01:59] Priya: What's the difference in expected tail latency between hosted and dedicated? Some rough ballpark.
[02:04] Carlos: Ballpark: for a 256 token average response, hosted can be ~120–220ms p95 depending on model, whereas dedicated with pinned capacity and optimized batching can shave off 20–40% on throughput-sensitive workloads. But p99 tails depend a lot on burst handling and KV cache warmness.
[02:22] Anika: Our initial success bar is p95 < 300ms for 256-token outputs and p99 < 600ms for typical mixed workloads. Does that sound achievable?
[02:31] Carlos: It's reasonable as a target for the POC, we'll validate on the replay. We should also set an error budget for rejects/timeouts — e.g., <0.2% errors.
[02:39] Tom: Cost is another axis — can you estimate cost per 1k tokens for dedicated vs hosted?
[02:44] Maya: We'll share rough pricing tiers but a baseline POC cost estimate will depend on peak concurrency and how many hours you're running the replay. The replay usually runs at scaled QPS to simulate peaks for short windows.
[02:55] Anika: For the replay, we want two scenarios: steady-state day load (45 QPS) and burst scenario (simulate 900 QPS for 30s bursts repeated every 10 minutes).
[03:07] Carlos: Good. We'll design the benchmark harness to replay both patterns. We'll also instrument token-level latency so we can see where the tail tokens are coming from.
[03:16] Priya: On security: we need SSO, SAML, RBAC, and KMS integration. Any issues with bringing your control plane into our VPC?
[03:26] Leah: We have a Private deployment option that uses customer-managed control plane and supports KMS/HSM integrations and SSO. We'll send the architecture doc.
[03:33] Maya: For the POC success criteria let's record what we heard: p95 < 300ms for 256 tokens, p99 < 600ms for mixed, error rate < 0.2%, and cost below a threshold TBD. Anything to add?
[03:45] Priya: Add that model fidelity must match current outputs — no regressions on answer quality. We'll supply a small test set for quality baseline.
[03:51] Carlos: We'll run differential quality checks using your sample prompts. If we see regressions we'll flag them and iterate on quantization/config.
[03:58] Anika: About model variants — we currently use an open LLM stack. We might want to test a larger model for a subset of requests (long summaries) and a smaller fast model for chat. Can Redwood route by policy?
[04:09] Maya: Yes, smart routing is part of our platform. For the POC we can simulate routing by marking model_hint in the CSV so the replay uses different model families for different request classes.
[04:20] Tom: On telemetry, what traces/metrics do you provide during the replay? We want per-request token latency, queue depth, and host-level GPU utilization.
[04:28] Carlos: We surface token-level latency, batching stats, queue depth, GPU util, and KV cache hit rates. We'll give you a dashboard link for post-run analysis.
[04:36] Anika: Great. Any gotchas you've seen with traffic replays?
[04:40] Carlos: A few: timestamp skew, truncated prompts during anonymization, and missing model hints. Also if the replay is too synthetic it hides network variability; we prefer using real timestamps and simulating clocks.
[04:50] Maya: We'll provide the replay SDK and instructions. Tom, you mentioned S3 — we can accept the CSV in S3 or upload to our secure share.
[04:58] Tom: S3 works. We'll need a short checklist to ensure the data is anonymized.
[05:04] Leah: We'll add the checklist to the template. Also note on encryption: server-side encryption + customer KMS is supported.
[05:11] Priya: Timeline? We want this POC done before end of month if possible. That gives ~2 weeks. Is that realistic?
[05:16] Carlos: Two weeks is tight but doable for a basic run: 48 hour data ingestion and one benchmark run plus analysis. For a deeper dedicated scenario we'd need 3–4 weeks to provision and test.
[05:26] Maya: Proposed timeline: today: share template and security pack; by 9/24 customer provides CSV; week of 9/29 we run replay and initial benchmark; week of 10/6 we review detailed results and capacity planning.
[05:38] Anika: Works for us. One more question: for the POC do you allow us to pin model weights/version so we can compare exactly?
[05:46] Carlos: Yes you can pin model versions for reproducibility. We'll also snapshot runtime config used for the test.
[05:52] Tom: Are you able to simulate token caching / KV cache warm starts? Because our production has large prefix reuse.
[05:58] Carlos: We can simulate warm cache by seeding the KV cache or running a warmup phase before the measured run. We'll include that option.
[06:05] Maya: Any contractual stuff we need to flag? Priya?
[06:08] Priya: Nothing heavy for POC but legal will want an NDA and export controls reviewed.
[06:13] Leah: We'll send the standard POC agreement and SOC2 pack.
[06:17] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps...
[06:20] [recap] Maya: I'll send replay template, checklist, SOC2 docs; Carlos will draft capacity mapping; Tom will upload anonymized traffic; schedule run week of 9/29.
[06:30] Anika: Thanks all. Looking forward to the replay.
[06:33] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via the shared thread.

End of transcript.

Notes on artifacts to share: replay SDK link (will be in email), benchmark template CSV, SOC2 + security pack, initial rough pricing tiers, sample dashboard from previous similar POC (anonymized).

records.title: add pluggable init-probe support and k8s cert-rotation preflight hook
records.text:
add pluggable init-probe support and k8s cert-rotation preflight hook

description:
Motivation: Private installs need two things that have come up repeatedly in enterprise engagements: (1) the ability to run tenant- or environment-specific logic during init without forking charts, and (2) a safe, observable pre-upgrade certificate rotation path that can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. This PR introduces a small plugin surface for init probes and a Helm templated preflight cert-rotation hook with backoff and dry-run modes.

What this changes (summary): added a pluggable init-probe contract in values.schema, new ConfigMap+Job templates for probe bundles, a cert-rotation cronjob/hook template that can be toggled per-release, and docs + examples for Terraform module wiring. The change includes a lightweight Go helper container image reference (configurable) used by init jobs to execute probe bundles and emit structured status to /var/log/init-probes.json for the operator to surface.

Checklist: - [x] values.schema.json entries and validation - [x] Helm templates for init probe configmap, job, and hook - [x] Example values.yaml for airgap and non-airgap flows - [x] Terraform README showing integration points - [x] Unit tests for template rendering and CI smoke pipeline

Commits: See commits summary below for granular changes.

Files touched (high level): templates/init-probe-configmap.yaml, templates/init-probe-job.yaml, templates/preflight-cert-rotation-hook.yaml, values.schema.json, charts/redwood-private/Chart.yaml (chart version bump), examples/helm/values-cert-rotation.yaml, docs/operational/cert-rotation.md, third_party/terraform/modules/cert-rotation/README.md, README.md (installer docs).

Behavior notes: - The init probe system is opt-in: users enable probes via values.private.init.probes.enabled and provide a list of probe artifacts (configmap or OCI image refs). When enabled, the installer creates an init ConfigMap and a short-lived Job that runs before the main tenant bootstrap. Probe Job behavior is guarded by a probeTimeout and probeRetries field. - The cert-rotation hook supports `mode: dry-run|apply`, a rotation window (cron-style) and an explicit `kmsProvider` field so customers can point it at their key manager. The hook emits Prometheus metrics (probe_success, rotation_attempt) and logs structured JSON to stdout. - Pre-upgrade flow: the chart adds a Hook annotation for pre-upgrade with weight and a canary label so operators can opt to run rotation only on a subset of namespaces first.

Testing and CI: Helm template rendering tests (helm unittest) were added to validate values combinations. CI runs lint, unit render tests, and an integration smoke where the preflight job is rendered but not executed. All CI checks passed on the final revision.

Review highlights / conversation (abridged): - Sasha: asked for clearer failure semantics for probe Jobs (should not block install forever). I added probeRetries + backoff and documented it. - Diego: requested the KMS provider shape be extensible for HSM; I added a generic provider map and an example for HashiCorp Vault + HSM. - Lin: asked for metrics naming and unit. Updated templates to emit prometheus annotations and added a short metrics doc. - QA: requested an airgap-friendly example; included an examples/helm/values-cert-rotation-airgap.yaml and notes for image pre-pull.

Merge outcome: squash-merged into main after approvals from Sasha and Diego and green CI.

release_notes:
Add pluggable init probe extension points and a configurable cert-rotation preflight hook used during upgrades/imports. No breaking changes to existing values; new fields are opt-in.

Noah (PM): dropping frames for a new first-run surface: sample gallery (grid of cards) vs compact launch chip. fig: https://www.figma.com/file/xyZA1234/first-run-samples
Noah (PM): goal: increase sample starts without annoying repeat users. want copy variants, a11y check, and quick qual plan.

Asha (Design): gallery shows intent thumbnails + short purpose lines, good for discovery. chip is subtle and can expand to a tray. gallery = higher visual cost.

Diego (Frontend): gallery needs lazy loads and keyboardable cards; chip needs expand/contract animation and persisted per-workspace state. both need clear DOM order for keyboard flow.

June (A11y): quick accessibility notes:
- small caption text on cards fails contrast in dark mode; use semantic tokens
- ensure each card has descriptive aria-label (title + purpose + "~5 minutes")
- tray expand must use aria-expanded and announce content via aria-live=polite
- when tray/dialog opens, focus should move to the panel and return on close
- close buttons: visible label for screen readers (avoid only icons)

Clara (DevEx): analytics/events: sample_surface_shown (gallery|chip), sample_opened, sample_skipped, sample_dismissed_reason. add experiment_id and cohort. gate display on telemetry_consent true.

Ravi (Research): suggestion: run 10 quick moderated sessions in the canary cohort and an intercept survey on dismiss asking "Why didn't you try a sample?". also test microcopy with time estimate e.g., "About 5 minutes".

onboard-bot: reminder  run axe smoke and keyboard nav locally before merging.

Asha (Design): copy sets to test (tone + CTAs):
1) Warm: "Try a sample project" CTA: "Open sample" secondary: "Maybe later"
2) Crisp: "Start with a sample" CTA: "Use sample" secondary: "Skip"
3) Minimal: "Try demo" CTA: "Launch" secondary: "Close"
I prefer Warm for first exposure.

June (A11y): also recommend adding SR-only text for time estimate: "Approximately five minutes to complete" and not relying on color to convey urgency or status.

Diego (Frontend): CSS sketch for chip tray:
```css
.sample-chip { position: fixed; right: 16px; bottom: 20px; z-index: 60; }
.sample-tray[aria-expanded="true"] { transform: translateY(0); }
```

Clara (DevEx): feature-flag plan: key = samples_firstrun_variant; internal 100% uses chip; external A/B: 25% gallery, 25% chip, rest control. metric gates: sample_start uplift and dismiss rate < 10%.

records.title: 3109876543-codeblock-escape-and-snippet-lint.json
records.text:
3109876543-codeblock-escape-and-snippet-lint.json

Ana P: Heads up: mkdocs build on staging failed after the last docs PR. Error points at an MDX file with an HTML comment inside a fenced codeblock.
Jared R: can you paste the error?
Ana P: error snippet from CI:
```
ValueError: Unexpected HTML comment in mdx code block at docs/guides/auth.mdx:42
```
I traced it to a codeblock that contains `<!-- TODO: remove this snippet -->` inside triple-backticks.
docs-bot: lint: mdx-codeblock-escape -> detected raw HTML comments inside code blocks. Suggest escaping or using HTML entities.
Nina: interesting — in plain markdown it's fine, but MDX parser treats `<!--` specially even inside fenced blocks depending on parser config. Might be varying between local env and CI docker image.
Jared R: quick fix: wrap the inner comment in an HTML-escaped form like `<!-- TODO -->` or prefix the code fence with ```text so parser doesn't try to parse HTML.
Ana P: I applied an immediate patch that escapes the comment and submitted PR 4312. But we should avoid ad-hoc fixes. We need a pre-commit hook or CI check that flags raw `<!--` inside code fences.
docs-bot: suggestion: add a remark-lint rule `no-html-comment-in-code` to docs-lint config.
Nina: I'll prototype a tiny remark plugin that walks fenced code nodes and searches for `<!--` sequences. It can report and optionally auto-escape. Will add a CLI flag for `--auto-fix`.
Jared R: also noticed some SDK snippets have platform-specific backticks that break syntax highlighting and cause the link checker to miscalculate anchor offsets. Example: a snippet with inline HTML id on a heading inside a codeblock. That moved anchor positions and triggered broken cross-page fragment tests.
Ana P: ugh. Can we standardize snippet formatting? Maybe we add a pre-commit formatter for code fences: enforce language tag, ensure no inline headings or HTML ids inside code fences, and normalize trailing newline.
Nina: sounds good. I'll add tests covering: 1) codeblocks with `<!--` flagged, 2) codeblocks with `# Heading {#id}` flagged, 3) malformed fenced blocks missing language tag.
Jared R: also let's document the recommended snippet style in docs contributors: small checklist and an example snippet template. I'll add `docs/STYLEGUIDE/snippets.md` in the PR.
Ana P: CI change request: add `docs:lint-snippets` job that runs before linkcheck. If it fails, skip linkcheck and mark the PR as needs-fix to avoid noisy Netlify previews.
ops-deploy-bot: job queued: docs:lint-snippets (pending).
Nina: I pushed PR-4313 with the remark rule + tests. PR-4312 is the immediate fix. Please review both; after merging, we can run a one-off job to scan the rest of the repo for offending snippets and open targeted cleanup PRs.
Ana P: thanks. If we get the auto-fix flag in, we can progressively fix historical files in a bulk commit to avoid many small PRs.
Jared R: agreed. Also add a short note in the contribution guide about running `yarn docs:lint` locally.
Ana P: will do. Closing loop: reviewers, please prioritize these two PRs so Netlify can green up for the upcoming release.
docs-bot: reminder: linkcheck will run after lint jobs pass.

records.text:
eng-platform

sami: Quick question — if we set a feature flag default OFF at the org level, can a lower scope (project/route/model) turn it ON by default? wondering about the exact override rules. :thinking:

lee: Specificity wins. Our rule is: model > route > project > org. More specific scopes override less specific ones.

anya: Follow-up — how do canary audiences interact with that? e.g., org default OFF, but model-level canary 10% ON. If a route tries to set 100% ON, which takes precedence?

kevin: Good question. Policy we agreed on in the last sync: a child scope can only expand a parent's enabled percentage up to a hard cap defined by the parent unless the parent explicitly sets `allow_escalation: true`. So in your example, route cannot go to 100% if the model's canary cap is 10% and the parent disallows escalation.

lee: Example config pattern (YAML):
```yaml
org_defaults:
  feature_x:
    enabled: false
    max_child_pct: 0
    allow_escalation: false

project_a:
  feature_x:
    enabled: false
    max_child_pct: 20
    allow_escalation: false

model_v2:
  feature_x:
    enabled: true
    rollout_pct: 10
    allow_escalation: false

route:/generate-text:
  feature_x:
    enabled: true
    rollout_pct: 100  # will be capped to 10 because model_v2 sets rollout_pct=10 and allows no escalation
```

kevin: Implementation note: the evaluation order is: collect effective parent limits walking up scopes, compute min(max_child_pct, parent_rollout_pct, ancestor_caps), then apply the local intent. This prevents accidental full rollouts under a nested canary.

rollout-bot: :robot_face: Canary created: model_v2/feature_x -> 10% (created by kevin at 1891234575)

sami: Thanks — can we also enforce a lint/CI check that rejects PRs which try to set `rollout_pct` > ancestor cap unless `allow_escalation: true` exists in the ancestor? I'll open a small PR with the rule. @kevin can you review when I ping it?

kevin: Yup — will review. Also recommend adding an audit warning in the console when a route-level toggle is blocked by a parent cap (so product sees why it didn't turn on). :+1:

sami: Awesome, thanks all. Keeping this thread as the design note for enforcement behaviour.

Sophie: Quick thread  saved-view preview question for console analytics. If a user saves a view scoped to a route that currently has a pinned model, do we treat the saved view as 'locking' the pin (so restore will force that model) or merely 'suggest' the model in the preview? Need a decision before Friday so we can ship the preview in the rollout.

Jamal: Leaning lock-by-default for route+model saves. In practice people expect saved views to capture the end state. For API I'd add `pinned_models` array to the savedview resource and a `locked` bool in preview. Backcompat: default to false if missing.

Maria Chen: Locking makes sense from a telemetry/QA POV. Also want the preview to show a few small telemetry cues: `sample_rate`, `24h_token_burn`, and an estimated token delta if the model is different. That way teams can see cost impact before applying.

Oliver: UI constraint: we have limited space in the savedview preview card. Suggest a compact row: [ModelChip] [cost delta badge] [info icon]. Info hover opens flyout with sample rate, last 24h burn, and pin provenance. Keeps the main surface clean.

Kevin (PM): Migration risk: this changes semantics for many existing savedviews that were effectively route-only. We should gate behind `console.savedview.v2` and ship a migration banner in the console with opt-in. Also prepare messaging for customers on Dedicated.

Sophie: Agreed on feature flag + migration banner. Jamal, can you keep the public API compat while adding these fields?

Jamal: Example API sketch (keeping as additive fields):

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "scope": "route|model|global",
  "route_id": "string",
  "pinned_models": ["string"],
  "preview": {
    "sample_rate": "number",
    "token_estimate": "number",
    "locked": true
  },
  "metadata": "string"
}
```

Note: the above is just a quick draft; will post a cleaned schema later. Backcompat: servers should ignore unknown fields.

Maria Chen: Please add `provenance` ideally in preview or metadata: who pinned, when, and whether it was autosuggest or user action. That reduces support noise.

Oliver: UI microcopy idea: show provenance as tiny text on hover: "pinned by Maria Chen • 2025-02-14 • suggested by Optimize". Keeps things discoverable without clutter.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: feature flag `savedview-v2` toggled to staging at 2024-09-12T18:22Z :rocket:

Sophie: Action list: Jamal post API schema + migration script; Oliver build ModelChip + flyout; Maria wire telemetry endpoints & include provenance; Kevin draft rollout notes and banner text; Sophie will write RFC summarizing lock default, preview fields, FF, migration flow. Tagging #product for awareness.

Jamal: I'll follow up with a minimal migration snippet showing how to mark existing route-scoped savedviews as unlocked and surface the banner to affected users.

Maria Chen: I'll attach compact mockups to the RFC showing the chip and flyout.

Oliver: I'll prototype the chip component today and DM Sophie with screenshots.

records.title: KPI Entropy & Resilience Planner (Launch Contingency Workbook)
records.text:
KPI Entropy & Resilience Planner (Launch Contingency Workbook)

OVERVIEW:
This workbook is an operational-first KPI tracker that quantifies 'entropy' (unexpected KPI variance) and maps concrete contingency actions to thresholds. Designed to be used during staged rollouts (canary -> slow-roll -> ramp) and 0-72h launch windows.

Quick notes:
- Entropy = weighted stddev across critical KPIs (latency, error rate, cost per token, cache hit). High entropy => risk of cascading failures.
- Use this sheet to drive go/no-go and to automate simple runbook triggers (Slack webhook, autoscale policy).
- Status: draft. Need SRE signoff on automated thresholds (see linked Jira OPS-987).

KPI DEFINITIONS & FORMULA:
- p50_latency_ms: 50th percentile server-side generation time (ms)
- p95_latency_ms: 95th percentile
- error_rate_pct: 5xx + model timeout / total requests
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd: invoice-level approximation (includes model variant coeffs)
- cache_hit_rate_pct: KV/prefix cache effective hit rate
- model_quality_score: eval pass rate on smoke prompt-set (0-100)

Entropy score (working):
Entropy = round( 100 * (0.35*norm(p95,p95_target) + 0.25*norm(error_rate,error_target) + 0.2*norm(cost,cost_target) + 0.2*(1 - cache_hit_rate_norm) ), 1)
where norm(x,target) = min(1, max(0, (x - target) / (target*0.5))) — normalizes deviations up to 50% above target.
Interpretation: 0-20 low risk, 21-50 medium, 51-80 high, 81-100 critical.

KPI TRACKER (snapshot):
| KPI                     | target     | warn_threshold        | crit_threshold        | owner         | fallback_action_short                 | notes |
|-------------------------|------------|-----------------------|-----------------------|---------------|----------------------------------------|-------|
| p50_latency_ms          | 120 ms     | 200 ms                | 350 ms                | SRE Oncall    | increase-replicas -> enable-burst     | p50 drifting after 12:30 UTC
| p95_latency_ms          | 420 ms     | 700 ms                | 1200 ms               | SRE Oncall    | degrade-model-variant -> route-to-ded | observe tail spikes after 1k req/s
| error_rate_pct          | 0.4%       | 1.5%                  | 3.5%                  | Platform Eng  | circuit-open -> reduce-rate-limit     | check external deps
| cost_per_1k_tokens_usd  | $3.20      | $4.75                 | $7.00                 | Product Ops   | switch-quantized -> restrict-traffic  | monitor invoice tag
| cache_hit_rate_pct      | 72%        | 55%                   | 40%                   | Serving RT    | clear-stale-cache/enable-prefetch     | high variance with new prompts
| model_quality_score     | 94%        | 88%                   | 75%                   | Applied ML    | rollback-prompt-set/rollback-weight   | run evals per release
| throughput_rps          | 850 rps    | 650 rps               | 400 rps               | Infra Eng     | scale-up-nodes -> enable-queueing     | autoscaler cooldown 90s
| downstream_errors_pct   | 0.2%       | 1.0%                  | 2.5%                  | Solutions Eng | fallback-to-sync -> degrade-features  | external API flakiness

Derived sample row (calculation): p95=900ms, error=2.2%, cost=$6.10, cache_hit=45% -> entropy ~ 68 (HIGH). Immediate actions: trigger crit playbook, alert stakeholders, run emergency scale/rollforward.

SCENARIO SIMULATIONS (pre-mortem probes):
1) Canary model variant causes 30% p95 increase after 30m
   - trigger: p95 > warn for 10m and entropy > 40
   - impact: 20% SLA degradation for first-party apps, third-party timeouts
   - quick mitigations: weight-shift 90% -> stable model; increase replicas by 25%; enable prefix cache; notify #launch-ops
   - escalation: oncall -> infra lead -> product ops (15min cadence)

2) Traffic surge (organic) doubles RPS in 12 minutes
   - trigger: throughput_rps increase > 60% vs baseline & error_rate rising > warn
   - mitigations: enable burst capacity (if on Dedicated), apply rate-limiter per token, throttle non-critical routes, temporarily disable big-context models
   - comms: open incident doc, post status at 5/15/30/60 min

3) Cost blowout from embeddings during onboarding experiment
   - trigger: cost_per_1k_tokens rolling 30m > crit OR monthly forecast projection > commit tier
   - mitigations: flip to quantized embedding model, pause onboarding job queue, inform finance owner for spend cap

4) Eval-quality regression (model_quality_score drops)
   - trigger: model_quality_score < warn across 3 consecutive hourly evals
   - mitigations: pause rollout, switch to previous model, kick off focused eval, alert product owners and applied-ml team

RUNBOOK SNIPPETS (copyable):
- Slack alert channel: #launch-ops (pinned playbook + incident doc link)
- Immediate checklist on crit threshold:
  1) Acknowledge alert (owner)
  2) Capture snapshot (curl /metrics -> s3) + attach to incident doc
  3) Execute one mitigation (scale/fallback) and monitor 5m windows
  4) Notify stakeholders and set 15-min checkpoints
  5) If entropy remains > 60 after second mitigation -> full scale rollback with 30m ETA

Escalation contact tree:
- first 15m: SRE Oncall (Pager) -> Infra Eng -> Platform Eng
- 15-45m: Product Ops (Riley Alvarez), Applied ML (Maya Singh)
- >45m: CTO on-call ladder

COMMUNICATION TEMPLATE (status updates):
- Subject: [INCIDENT] Launch rollout - {short-desc} - status: {acknowledged/in-mitigation/mitigated}
- Body: current entropy={entropy}, key KPIs: p95={p95}ms, errors={err}% , cost={cost}/1k , action={action taken}, ETA={eta}
- Post to: #launch-ops, incident doc, @product-leads list

POST-INCIDENT ANALYSIS FIELDS (to populate):
- root_cause_summary, timeline_minutes, mitigations_attempted, time_to_stable, residual_impact, suggested_changes (config/code/process), owner_for_followup

AUTOMATION IDEAS (short):
- wire entropy -> alerting rule in OpsMonitor (entropy > 50 AND p95 > warn)
- autopilot: run one safe mitigation (cache warm, weight shift 70%) when entropy 40-60, but require human approval for >60
- daily smoke eval runner to update model_quality_score -> email digest to applied-ml

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs:
- Agree on exact weighting for entropy formula (SRE + Applied ML input). (TODO: OPS-987)
- Decide which thresholds can be auto-actioned vs manual. (owner: Avery Chen)
- Add billing owner to critical cost alerts and set soft spend cap thresholds. (owner: Maya Singh)
- Add synthetic traffic probes for model-quality drift every 30m across canary cohorts. (owner: Jonah Park)

ATTACHMENTS / LINKS (use these in incident doc):
- Confluence: onboarding playbook (linked_artifacts)
- Runbook snippets: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-scripts (linked above)

NOTES TO SELF:
- This sheet should be exported as CSV to feed the launch dashboard during run-of-show.
- Keep the 'owner' column aligned with oncall rotations (sync weekly with ops roster).

ENDWORKSHEET
