records.title: AsterBank
records.text:
AsterBank

requirements_summary:
AsterBank is pursuing Redwood Private for regulated workloads in EU data centers with strict air-gap controls. Primary requirement is offline installation/upgrade using cryptographically signed bundles with deterministic manifests and installer-side verification that fails closed. They explicitly asked how Redwood proves provenance and integrity offline (signing scheme details, trust roots, key rotation, and revocation). Audit logging is a gating item: they expect locally retained install/verify audit events (success + failure reason codes) with a supported export path to their SIEM (they mentioned CEF/JSON with stable schemas and retention guidance). Security team concerns include downgrade/replay attacks via reused media, transport corruption, and time-skew in air-gapped environments causing certificate validity failures. They also asked for documented break-glass procedures (override flag) that are policy-gated and generate prominent audit markers.

Workload notes: intended initial use cases are internal policy/document search + summarization for compliance operations and a restricted customer support assistant (no PII leaving the environment; strong redaction expectations). Preference is consistent model pinning and predictable throughput; they are cost-sensitive but will pay for operational controls and auditability.

Commercial: moving through enterprise procurement. Main contract dependencies map to the offline artifact signing project deliverables: signed bundle GA commitment, key ceremony evidence package, rotation policy with notice, and audit log export specs. They are comparing against self-hosting (vLLM) and cloud private network offerings, but current direction is on-prem due to audit and residency constraints.

next_step:
Procurement/legal: finalize addendum covering offline artifact signing, key rotation notifications, and audit log export specs; schedule customer security sign-off after Redwood provides key ceremony evidence package + sample signed bundle for validation.

blockers:
Offline/air-gapped installation requires signed bundles + installer verification (must be GA and included in contract SOW)
Audit log export requirements (CEF/JSON mapping + retention guidance) need to match their SIEM onboarding checklist
Key custody + rotation policy language: wants documented ceremony, separation of duties, and emergency revocation process
Downgrade/replay protections for offline media transfers (explicitly called out by their AppSec team)
Time source constraints in air-gapped DCs (concern about signature validity windows / 'not yet valid')

activity_timeline:
2025-09-18: Qualified via security-led inbound. Initial notes: 'must run in air-gapped DCs; no outbound network; evidence-heavy procurement.'
2025-10-22: Fireflies security review (offline installs). Topics: supply chain, signing root, audit logs, verification UX, downgrade prevention. Follow-up requested: written signing/key custody policy + example verification output. (Fireflies: 2025-10-22-asterbank-security-review-offline-installs)
2025-11-10: Sent responses to questionnaire on artifact signing + air-gap constraints. (Gmail: aisha_rahman/20251110-customer-security-questions-artifact-signing-and-air-gap)

SBOM path attached. https://scans.redwood.internal/scan/1718502345 :rotating_light:

maya: saw this. thanks scan-bot. is this runtime image currently in prod?

harry: yes, that digest is in the canary pool and one prod node. low traffic but not zero.

maya: ok. immediate containment: can we mark the image as quarantined in registry and start a rollback to previous stable digest? @oncall-sre

leena: what are the exploitability details? is it RCE or local? I see CVSS 8.1 but need more context before telling customers.

samir: looks like remote-ish via crafted payload in deserialization path. exploit requires untrusted input to hit net-lib parsing endpoint — should be medium risk for us, but high for worker-facing ingestion path.

maya: good call. mitigations: 1) quarantine image, 2) block deploys from that pipeline, 3) rebuild image with patched dependency, 4) verify image signature with KMS, 5) ensure audit log entry for all actions.

harry: blocking deploys from pipeline now (ci-policy:deny-on-high). I added a temporary RBAC change to CI service account to prevent new pushes until we flip the flag. CC: @leena for audit requirements.

leena: on audit: create explicit event via `auditctl` and push to long-term retention. Also need to record who triggered quarantine and RBAC override. auditor-bot, can you ingest these events?

auditor-bot: Received request. Please annotate events with keys: {"incident_id":"SC-2025-1718502345","initiator":"harry"}. Ingest scheduled.

samir: quick rebuild plan: update package lock to pin config-parse-utils@0.9.1 (patched), run `make image-build` in staging, run full e2e and image-scan hook, push signed image back to registry. I can take the rebuild if devex gives green light.

maya: samir pls proceed. when you push the rebuild, sign with key `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/build-keys/cryptoKeys/image-signer` and include SBOM. leena, do we need KMS key rotation?

leena: no rotation yet. we should verify that the signing key has not been exposed and that access logs show only CI service account used. If anything funky, rotate. I'll pull KMS access logs and check CMKs.

samir: starting rebuild in staging now. build command: ```bash
./ci/scripts/build_image.sh --tag staging-rebuild-1718502345
```

harry: registry quarantine tag in place, old digest pulled off canary. adding note in incident tracker SC-2025-1718502345.

maya: also notify Legal/Compliance if customer data might have been affected. Samir, keep the unpatched image offline and don't delete the digest until audit sign-off.

samir: got it. preserves old digest locally, won't delete. staging build passed smoke tests, running full scan.

scan-bot: staging image staging-rebuild-1718502345 scanned: no findings for CVE-2025-2786. SBOM updated.

leena: KMS access logs show only CI service account `ci-builder@redwood` used during signing. no anomalous principals. I'll attach log excerpt to the tracker.

maya: good. next steps: 1) schedule canary rollout of signed rebuild, 2) update ops runbook with this CVE note, 3) postmortem and dependency hygiene action items (lockfile audits, transitive monitoring). who owns postmortem?

harry: I'll own postmortem and coordinate with eng-sre and product-security. aiming for draft in 48h.

oncall-sre: canary rollout scheduled in 30m. will watch latency and error rates; rollback on alarms.

auditor-bot: Audit record created: incident_id=SC-2025-1718502345, actions=[quarantine_tag, rbaco_override, rebuild_signed, kms_check], retention=7y.

maya: thanks all. add retrospective item: add a registry webhook to auto-signal when SBOM shows transitive matches for high CVEs.

samir: copying notes to the internal ticket and closing this thread once canary stable.

maya: closing thread here. follow up in #postmortems once harry shares draft.

records.title: devex
records.text:
devex

elaine: hit a weird one in the sampleapp onboarding flow. rerank throws when we call embeddings from Node but python path is fine.
elaine: node stack: TypeError: e.embedding.map is not a function (at scoreCandidates)
ryan: paste the raw SDK responses for a batched call?
elaine: python OK:
```
[{
  "id": "q1",
  "embedding": [0.0001, -0.21, 0.003, ...],
  "model": "open-embed-1536"
}]
```
elaine: node BAD:
```
[{
  "id": "q1",
  "vector": "0.0001,-0.21,0.003,...",
  "model": "open-embed-1536"
}]
```
sam: hm: different field name (`vector` vs `embedding`) and vector is a CSV string when the call is batched. single-item node requests still return numeric arrays under `embedding`.
elaine: exactly. runs fine if I use input: 'one string' but fails with input: ['a','b']
ryan: could the batching helper be joining arrays to save space, then forgetting to parse on the client? we added a small optimization last quarter that serialized arrays for compact transport.
sam: also suspicious: an auth-retry path was recently updated to stitch chunk buffers; if it joins buffers using `buffer.toString()` we could accidentally strip array brackets and end up with CSV content.
elaine: repro (node):
```js
await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'open-embed-1536', input: ['a', 'b'] })
// observed: res[0].vector -> "0.0001,-0.21,0.003,..."
```
ryan: temporary mitigation: normalize shapes in sampleapp after SDK call: detect `vector` or `embeds` strings and convert: `const asNum = s.split(',').map(Number)`; wrap into `{embedding: asNum}` before rerank. we'll add the snippet to onboarding troubleshooting.
sam: i'll add a regression test in node-sdk that asserts numeric arrays are returned for batched calls and audit the retry/concat code path. if it's the batching helper we can revert the compact serialization patch.
ci-bot: CI: embedding-shape.spec.ts failed on sampleapp-node (expected embedding:number[] but got vector:string)
ryan: thanks. prioritize a patch for node-sdk and add an integration that compares node vs python sample outputs on CI to prevent future parity regressions.
elaine: pushed a small fix+note to sampleapp and opened PR redwood/devex#1620 with the workaround. tagging @sam for follow-up. :pray:

records.title: eng-releases
records.text:
eng-releases

maya: proposing a 'slab' fallback strategy for canaries — thinking of grouping model-variant + region as a single fallback unit instead of only model-level or region-level fallbacks. opening short RFC if folks +1 or have objections

ashwin: what exactly is a slab vs the current lane/fallbacks? quick TL;DR pls

maya: slab = {model variant, region, capacity tier}. idea: fallback a slab (route out of that entire chunk) when joint signals indicate it's unhealthy, rather than toggling just the model or just the region. avoids repeated oscillation where model is fine in region A but not B and we flip model and region separately

taylor: worried about A/B experiments. if we pull a slab we might bias tests. do we keep canary sample sticky so experiment integrity remains?

maya: good call. plan is sticky sampling by user cookie/consumer id for experiment window, but allow traffic rebalancing to preserve global RPS. fallback removes the slab from routing table but we keep experiment assignment metadata so cohorts remain balanced across remaining slabs

zheng: what signals trigger slab eviction? errors only? or latency/capacity too? need sensible defaults + backoff

ashwin: propose multi-signal heuristic: 1) error rate 3x baseline sustained for T_window; 2) p95 latency > 2x baseline AND queueing > 200ms; 3) capacity pressure: GPU free < 30% and queue length increasing. combine with :majority vote: at least two signals before eviction

maya: draft config snippet below (for runtime and console UX). open to naming suggestions for 'slab_eviction_policy'.

```yaml
slab_eviction_policy:
  enabled: true
  min_canary_pct: 1
  signals:
    errors:
      multiplier_threshold: 3.0
      window_seconds: 60
    latency:
      p95_multiplier: 2.0
      window_seconds: 60
    capacity:
      gpu_free_pct_threshold: 30
      avg_queue_ms_threshold: 200
  required_signal_count: 2
  cooldown_seconds: 300
  rollback_action: fallback_to_variant: stable
```

release-bot: deploy v0.40.2 started for rollout/experiment-17 — canary=5% in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 :rocket:

ops-bot: alert: us-east-1 slab-3 queue_ms rising to 520ms over last 2m (instances scaling) :eyes:

ashwin: when ops-bot fires, do we immediately mark capacity signal or wait for other signals? we should avoid noisy single-signal evictions during autoscale spikes

maya: plan: capacity signal is considered "soft" — counts as half a vote. combined with one hard signal (errors or latency) reaches required_signal_count. that avoids single-signal action during transient autoscale. also cooldown prevents flipflop

taylor: on the console side, we should show a projected traffic split if a slab is evicted (preflight): current->projected so PMs understand experiment impact. plus Undo button to re-add slab with reason note

ashwin: agree. also add a telemetry tag to every request routed during a rollback window so we can compute bias/regression metrics post-eviction (important for A/B causality)

zheng: what about region-only failure modes (network partition to region)? should we favor regional failover before slab-level if model works elsewhere? e.g., if only region connectivity is bad, don't evict model variants globally

maya: we can encode priority: region-only signals -> region-failover (remove region's slabs for that model); model-only signals -> model-variant fallback; joint signals -> slab eviction. default policy: try narrower scope first, escalate to slab if narrower fixes don't help within escalation_window_seconds

ashwin: propose escalation_window_seconds = 120 and max_escalation_steps = 2. Also record decision graph events to telemetry so we can audit why a slab was evicted

taylor: UI wishlist: 1) per-rollout decision timeline 2) live simulated traffic after each eviction 3) instant replay of routed requests for the cohort 4) a "safety leash" toggle for experiments that disables auto-evict

maya: love that. safety_leash will default ON for all A/B experiments but OFF for infra-only rollouts. need to wire through RBAC so only leads can disable

zheng: one more thing — quotas. if fallback increases pressure on stable pool, should we throttle fallback rate to avoid thrashing? e.g., only allow 1 slab eviction per 60s per region

ashwin: yes, slab eviction rate-limiter is needed. add global and per-region tokens. also prefer fallback to cheaper quantized variants before full stable fallback if model quality rules allow :sparkles:

maya: next steps: I'll spin up a short RFC doc with config proposal + console mocks + telemetry events list. want to land default heuristics and cooldowns before we wire autoscale signals. tagging @taylor @ashwin @zheng for review, will ping eng-telemetry next for event schema

ashwin: +1, please include sample Grafana queries for p95/queue/e2e errors

ops-bot: noted — created incident stub #IR-2024-125 for monitoring playbook updates

records.title: SIG: Encryption controls — KMS/HSM topology and rotation cadence
records.text:
SIG: Encryption controls — KMS/HSM topology and rotation cadence

['From: Andrew Nguyen <andrew@payflux.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: security-team@payflux.com
Date: Tue, 22 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: KMS/HSM and rotation details

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the initial SIG submission. The PayFlux security team reviewed your answers and requested a few clarifications specifically around encryption and key management before we can mark the control as satisfied:

1) High-level topology: Are production data-encryption keys backed by an HSM (Cloud HSM or customer HSM) or only KMS-managed CMKs? If both, which assets use HSM-backed keys vs software/KMS keys?
2) Key material lifecycle: Do you ever export raw key material from the HSM? If not, where is key material generated and stored?
3) Rotation cadence: What is the default rotation schedule for service/tenant keys (days)? Is rotation automated and audited?
4) Envelope encryption details: Confirm algorithms and negotiated TLS versions in-transit, and the envelope scheme used at rest.
5) Audit evidence: Can you provide an excerpt of key-rotation/audit logs for the last 12 months and the HSM certificate chain for FIPS validation?

We appreciate concise answers and any artifacts (architecture diagram, rotation log excerpt, cert chain). If someone technical can be looped in, that would help.

Thanks,
Andrew
Security Engineer
PayFlux

', 'From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Nguyen <andrew@payflux.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Apr 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: KMS/HSM and rotation details

Andrew — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Dev (infra/keys) and Neha (security/compliance) to provide the technical artifacts and concise answers.

Attachments I will upload to the secure drive:
- payflux_SIG_uploaded_kms_architecture.pdf (high-level topology diagram)
- once Dev confirms, we will attach the rotation audit excerpt and the HSM cert chain.

High level summary from a product/security perspective (short):
- In-transit: TLS 1.3 (mutual TLS for internal control channels), strong cipher suites only.
- At-rest: Envelope encryption with AES-256-GCM for data keys; root and master keys are HSM-backed CMKs.
- Key lifecycle: Key material is generated and protected inside HSMs (CloudHSM); we do not export raw key material.
- Rotation: Service CMKs have an automated rotation policy (365 days). Tenant/customer keys can be customer-managed (bring-your-own-key) or Redwood-managed; we support rotation via KMS key rotation and a controlled alias-swap process.

Dev — can you add the technical detail and the log excerpt? Neha — please confirm whether the artifacts meet PayFlux evidence requirements once uploaded.

Best,
Soojin
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

', "From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Andrew Nguyen <andrew@payflux.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Apr 2025 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: KMS/HSM and rotation details — technical details and artifacts attached

Hi all — technical answers and artifacts below. I've attached a small rotation-audit excerpt (key_rotation_audit_excerpt_20250421.csv) and the HSM cert chain (hsm_cert_chain.pem) to the secure drive link Soojin uploaded.

Topology and key placement:
- We use an envelope encryption model across our stack. Data keys (DEKs) are AES-256-GCM, generated per object/prefix and encrypted with a Customer Master Key (CMK).
- CMKs are AWS KMS keys backed by AWS CloudHSM (FIPS 140-2 validated HSM module) in each region. For on-prem/private deployments, we support an equivalent HSM-backed KMIP-compliant appliance or allow customer-supplied HSMs via our Private deployment options.
- Some ephemeral keys used for short-lived caches are generated in-process and wrapped immediately by a CMK; master key material never leaves the HSM.

Key material lifecycle / export policy:
- We NEVER export raw key material from the HSM. All CMKs are created with origin=AWS_KMS (HSM-protected) or via imported key material for BYOK where the customer performed import into their HSM/KMS.
- For BYOK imports we store only the KMS key identifier and usage metadata; the private key material remains under the customer's control in their HSM.

Rotation policy and process:
- Redwood-managed service CMKs: automated rotation set to 365 days. Rotation is implemented by creating a new cryptographic key version in KMS, re-wrapping the DEKs, and atomically swapping aliases to minimize downtime.
- Tenant/customer-managed keys (BYOK): rotation cadence is customer-controlled; Redwood supports an alias-swap procedure and provides tooling to rewrap existing DEKs using the new key version.
- Rotation is logged to our central audit pipeline: KMS/CloudTrail events, CloudHSM audit logs, and application-level rotation events are retained in the audit store. Default retention for rotation logs is 7 years, searchable via our audit interface.
- Key rotation steps (high level):
  1) Schedule rotation window and notify stakeholders.
  2) Create new key version in KMS/CloudHSM and grant necessary key policies.
  3) Re-wrap DEKs in a rolling manner (background re-encryption) to avoid mass downtime.
  4) Swap alias to new CMK version and retire old key version following retention and legal hold processes.

Algorithms and in-transit controls:
- TLS: TLS 1.3 required for all external and internal endpoints. For internal control-plane channels we use mTLS (mutual TLS) with cert pinning between services.
- Envelope encryption: DEKs use AES-256-GCM. DEKs encrypted with RSA/EC-based KMS operations depending on KMS provider; on AWS this is KMS Encrypt/Decrypt (AES-GCM DEKs wrapped by KMS).

Auditability and evidence provided:
- We captured a CSV excerpt of KMS rotation events for the last 12 months (attached: key_rotation_audit_excerpt_20250421.csv). Fields include timestamp, key_id, operation, initiated_by, and event_id.
- HSM certificate chain attached (hsm_cert_chain.pem) showing FIPS-validated module certificate chain for our CloudHSM endpoints.
- Architecture diagram (payflux_SIG_uploaded_kms_architecture.pdf) describes multi-region CMK placement, envelope flow, and optional BYOK paths.

Limitations / notes:
- For customers on Dedicated/Private deployments where they bring their own HSM, Redwood does not have access to the private key material; evidence is limited to key operation logs and signed attestation from the customer's HSM if requested.
- If PayFlux requires a signed attestation from our HSM vendor (NLT attestation or hardware CSP report), we can coordinate via our security team — please confirm the exact artifact.

If you need a sample CloudTrail query or the specific key IDs in your region for test data, tell us which region and we will provide the minimal set.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

", "From: Andrew Nguyen <andrew@payflux.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, security-team@payflux.com
Date: Thu, 24 Apr 2025 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: Encryption controls — received artifacts, one more ask

Soojin / Dev — thanks for the quick, thorough responses and the artifacts. The diagram and the audit excerpt look good at a high level. A couple of small requests to close the control: 

- Can you attach the HSM certificate chain directly in the email (we see the drive link but need a copy in the ticket)? We need it for our FIPS proofing process.
- Please provide either (a) a salted hash of the current CMK key identifiers for our reference or (b) a short mapping of example key aliases we should expect to see in our CloudTrail-based collection (region + alias format). This will help our SIEM mapping.

If you can send those two items I can mark the SIG encryption section as satisfied and move the packet to the legal review.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Andrew
PayFlux Security Team

On Thu, Apr 24, 2025 at 10:12 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Andrew — I'll upload the HSM cert chain into the case and provide the alias mapping (example format) inline below. Expect both by EOD.
>
> Example alias mapping (example only):
> - alias/redwood/prod/us-east-1/master-2024-v3
> - alias/redwood/tenant/payflux/us-east-1/2023-v1
>
> — Soojin
"]

jenn_cs: Heads-up: Acme renewal flagged after pilot. They hit unexpected token spend and occasional p95 spikes. Request: single-page "Pulse Playbook" we can send their engs + a tiny internal ops flipbook. Can we draft and assign? @arun_se @megan_sre

arun_se: I'll draft the customer-facing Pulse Playbook (short). Idea: 3 quick wins + one-line rollback instructions. Keep examples language-agnostic.

megan_sre: Ops flipbook should be minimal: pre-check, quick toggles (route -> lighter model, enable server prefix cache, enable soft token cap), and rollback. Also prepare a Console toggle template.

arun_se: Draft customer one-pager below (VERY short):
- Deterministic client cache — why: avoid re-sending identical context. Action: attach X-RW-Cache key (user + prompt hash) and set TTL 45s. Example header:
```
X-RW-Cache: user:{id}:sha:{sha256(prompt)}
Cache-TTL: 45
```
- Micro-batching at edge — why: reduce per-request overhead. Action: batch short requests with a 30-80ms hold window (batch_max=12). Example config snippet:
```json
{"batch_max":12, "batch_hold_ms":50}
```
- Streaming + truncate fallback — why: streaming improves first-byte; fallback reduces cost if latency spikes. Action: enable streaming with chunk_size=128 and add a truncate_on_timeout policy. Pseudocode:
```
if p95 > 400ms:
  route -> lighter_model
  enable truncate_on_timeout = true
```

arun_se: One-line ops fallback for the customer: "If you hit a spike, request 'Economy Mode' and include 3 request IDs from the last 10 minutes."

megan_sre: Internal flipbook (concise):
1) Pre-check: pull 3 example request IDs + spike window.
2) Canary: create route acme-slim -> llama-7b-128q, start 10% traffic.
3) If urgent: set acme-route -> 100% acme-slim, enable prefix cache, and apply soft token cap 5000/min. Commands:
```bash
redwood routes create acme-slim --model llama-7b-128q --from acme-route --split 10
redwood caches enable --route acme-route --prefix
redwood quotas update --scope customer:acme --tokens-per-minute 5000
```
4) Watch for 5m window: p95, tokens/min, error rate. Rollback: revert route split and disable cache.

metrics-bot: Canary created acme-slim id=canary-331 status=ok

jenn_cs: Great. Owners: Arun = customer email + playbook; Megan = ops flipbook + console toggle; Jenn = client coordinating & invite. Arun, paste a 1-paragraph cover note we can use.

arun_se: Cover note draft: "Hi Acme team — quick plan attached: three immediate engineering steps (deterministic client cache, edge micro-batching, and streaming with a truncate fallback) that are low-effort and often reduce both latency and token spend. If you'd like, we can enable an ops fallback (Economy Mode) while we validate with a 30-minute calibration window. Please share 3 sample request IDs if you want us to pre-check logs before the call. — Arun, CS"

jenn_cs: Sending now and scheduling calibration. Will ping thread with any customer replies. Closing once sent. :white_check_mark:

records.title: Initiative Hub: Operational Radar & Error Budget Passport
records.text:
Initiative Hub: Operational Radar & Error Budget Passport

description:
Background: As Redwood scales Dedicated and Private deployments, teams need a single operational view that tracks per-service error budgets, current SLI health, and automated gating decisions. This initiative will deliver an "Error Budget Passport" concept surfaced in the Console (Operational Radar) that groups SLOs, shows burn rate, links the ledger and runbooks, and exposes automatic gating for rollouts and canaries.

Goals:
- Provide a single-pane Operational Radar in Console that lists teams/services with their active SLOs, current burn rate, time-to-breach, and recommended mitigation actions.
- Surface an Error Budget Passport per service: allocated budgets, recent incidents, owner, associated runbooks, and historical ledger with links to evals.
- Integrate automated gating hooks so Dedicated/Private rollout pipelines can query passport status and apply canary/rollback policies when budgets are breached.
- Expose program-level KPIs for PMs and Eng leads (total # services with breached budgets, mean time to recover, weekly burn rate trend).

SLI/SLO definitions (initial set):
- Request success rate (5xx + inference drop) — SLO target: 99.90% over 30d
- P95 serving latency (end-to-end) — SLO target: 300ms for hosted API, model-family-specific targets for Dedicated
- Embedding correctness/regression (synthetic eval pass rate) — SLO target: 98% across canonical prompts

Acceptance criteria:
1) Console Operational Radar view MVP showing list of services with SLOs and numeric burn rates, filterable by team, region, and model family.
2) Passport detail panel with ledger entries (chronological), linked runbooks, owner, and automated gating flag.
3) API endpoints for querying passport status (/v1/ops/passport/{service}) and a webhook for rollout systems to receive breach events.
4) Two-way linkage to existing SLI ingestion pipeline (ENG-3412) and dashboard templates in Grafana (dash-ops-passport).
5) Regression tests and an e2e canary that exercises gating on a staged Dedicated cluster.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- We will initially limit SLI ingestion to the canonical metrics ingested by the current telemetry pipeline to reduce scope (latency, errors, synthetic evals). Extending to custom SLIs will be a follow-up.
- Automated gating will be opt-in per-service. Conservative defaults will only block broad rollouts; emergency rollbacks require manual confirmation.
- Passport UI uses a compact card layout to avoid Console clutter; expanded detail lives in a dedicated Passport panel.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Ava Martinez (owner)
- Eng leads: Liam Chen (runtime), Priya Kapoor (platform telemetry)
- Design: Marco Liu (UX)
- SRE/Oncall: Elena Ruiz
- Sales/Customer Success: Rodrigo Silva (enterprise customers with Dedicated)

Implementation milestones:
- 2026-02-22: PRD approved and design sprint kickoff (complete)
- 2026-03-05: API schema for passport and breach webhook merged (ENG-3412 dependent)
- 2026-03-18: Console MVP wireframes -> design review (DES-612)
- 2026-03-29: Backend ingestion + ledger persistence implemented
- 2026-04-01: Staged canary and internal beta release

Metrics for success:
- % of critical services with passports created within 4 weeks of release > 70%
- Reduction in surprise SLO breaches during rollouts by 40% for teams that enable gating
- Time-to-detect SLO breaches improved by 25% (via consolidated radar)

Links & artifacts:
- PRD (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RH/pages/InitiativeHub+Error+Budget+Passport
- Design board (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/Operational-Radar-Passport
- API proposal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5412
- Grafana dashboard template: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/ops/passport-template

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: internal alpha for platform + SRE teams, create passports for 10 high-priority services.
- Week 2: invite 3 pilot product teams (hosting, dedicated runtime) and enable opt-in gating.
- Week 4: iterate on UI and auto-scaling interactions based on pilot feedback; prepare broader beta announcement.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Over-automating rollouts could cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: opt-in gating + manual override + gradual defaults.
- Risk: Telemetry gaps may under-report burn rate. Mitigation: require instrumentation checklist before passport creation; surface data confidence level in passport.

Next steps:
- Finalize API schema and webhook contract (owner: Liam)
- Design accessibility pass and small-card/expanded-card polish (owner: Marco)
- Coordinate with Eng telemetry to ensure metric coverage for first 10 services (owner: Priya)

comments:
2026-02-22 - PRD approved in PM sync. Design sprint scheduled for 2/24. (Ava)
2026-02-25 - Design concept reviewed. Recommendation: show time-to-breach prominently and add 'confidence' indicator for SLI data (Marco).
2026-03-02 - Engineering estimates: backend ledger + API 5pt, Console UI 3pt, gating webhook 2pt. Dependency: ENG-3412 (telemetry ingestion). (Liam)
2026-03-06 - Security review intake created; initial assessment low risk for metadata-only access. No KMS changes required. (Elena)
2026-03-09 - UX mock approved pending accessibility fixes; scheduling dev spike for API contract. (Ava)
2026-03-10 - Cross-team sync: Sales asked for 'CSV export' of passports for customer reports — adding as follow-up (PM backlog). (Rodrigo)

jen: Kickoff for CatalystNova POC — they want to validate microburst behavior + SLA before contract. Need a short load plan, cost sketch, and security checklist. Can ops + sec sync? :wave:

maria: Quick plan draft below. Three phases: 1) soak (sustained 5k qps for 1h) 2) microburst spike (20k qps for 10s, repeated 6x) 3) long tail (12h low-rate run). Measure p50/p95/p99, tail token latency, and error budget. Runbook coming.

kevin: +1 on phases. Important notes: warm KV cache before spike, ensure continuous batching enabled, and run at least one warmup iteration with full context lengths. For dedicated runs, pin model shards to avoid cross-host eviction.

maria: Minimal smoke run commands (you can adapt to k6/wrk):
```
# generate mixed short+long prompts
python tools/loadgen.py --mix "short:70,long:30" --qps 5000 --duration 60m --out results/smoke.json
# spike: 20k qps for 10s x6 bursts
python tools/loadgen.py --burst 20000 --burst-duration 10s --bursts 6 --out results/spike.json
```

kevin: Also set warmup flag: `--warmup 20m` so KV/prefix caches stabilize. Metric collection: GPU util, enqueue wait, avg batch size, and per-request model_variant tag. If you see queue length > 50ms consistently, backoff or route to fallback model.

oliver: Pricing/practical: microburst minutes matter. Finance needs an estimate of peak-minute usage to price burst capacity. Jen, confirm if CatalystNova is comfortable with ~2k burst-minutes/month or if they need a hard cap.

jen: They're willing to start with a 2k burst-minutes budget for the POC window but want a per-10k-token cost estimate for that pattern (mix above). Can we generate a quick unit-cost calc from last week's benchmark numbers?

maria: Rough calc from similar runs: with our q4-optimized kernels and batching, microburst unit cost ~ $0.024 per 10k tokens (hosted) vs $0.013 on Dedicated with reserved capacity. I'll run numbers against the exact prompt mix and post updated estimate.

sam: Quick question from CatalystNova: can you replicate our thin-client mix? Most prompts are ~40 tokens, ~70% short replies. Also we use occasional tool calls that add extra round trips.

maria: Yes — include tool-call latency in the end-to-end measurement. Use `--prompt-len 40 --reply-len 60` and add a 2-3x small-request burst to simulate user spikes. Example mix JSON: 
```
{"mix": [{"type":"short","weight":70,"prompt_tokens":40,"response_tokens":60},{"type":"long","weight":30,"prompt_tokens":200,"response_tokens":250}], "tool_calls_pct": 8}
```

sec-bot: Security questionnaire v2 uploaded: https://redwood-inference.internal/sq/789 — check items 3.2 (KMS/HSM) and 4.1 (audit logs retention). Also note: customer requires SOC2 + IP allowlist for the POC.

sam: We prefer customer-managed keys (BYOK) if available. HSM recommended but not mandatory for POC. Also need audit log access for each test run.

kevin: For BYOK/HSM: Private deployment supports HSM and KMS integration. Note: HSM KMS calls add ~8-12ms if done per-request unless we cache derived keys. Recommend key-caching layer at the host for POC to avoid per-request roundtrip. I'll document tradeoffs in the security answers.

maria: Ops recommendation: run POC in Dedicated pool with cache warmed and KMS key-caching enabled. That gives predictable latency and lower unit cost. We'll still run one hosted-run to validate fallback routing.

jen: Next steps: Maria + Kevin to post final runbook + test matrix by Wed EOD. Jen to send cost sketch and contract addendum. Sam — aim for smoke run Thurs 10am PST. If any blocker, flag here.

records.title: introduce-compact-ci-adapter-and-dep-visibility-gateway
records.text:
introduce-compact-ci-adapter-and-dep-visibility-gateway

description:
Motivation: our presubmit and lint/test pipelines have accrued a lot of language-specific runners and duplicated setup steps. This PR extracts a small, language-agnostic CI adapter layer (Go) and a lightweight dependency-visibility gateway that centralizes dev-dependency detection, stale-lock telemetry, and a permissive gate for fastpath merges. Goals: reduce presubmit startup time, provide clearer visibility for dep churn, and make staged release hooks less noisy.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds cmd/ci-adapter: a compact Go binary that normalizes workspace bootstrap across languages, caches toolchain leases, and exposes a small HTTP health/sanity endpoint used by GitHub Actions.
- Introduces tooling/dep-visibility: a minimal service (local-only in CI) that computes a dependency surface summary, flags transitive devdeps, and emits a compact dependency fingerprint to a cache key used by staged CI lanes.
- Replaces language-specific presubmit shell fragments in the main workflows with calls to the ci-adapter; reduces duplicated logic in .github/workflows/presubmit-*.yml.
- Adds a presubmit-fastpath label and automation rule: small changes (docs/infra) can skip heavy integration shards when dep-visibility and unit/linters pass.
- Cleans up legacy Makefile targets used only by CI and moves canonical behavior into the adapter.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation of ci-adapter and dep-visibility modules
- [x] Replace presubmit workflow fragments and update action inputs
- [x] Add telemetry counters (dep-change-rate, presubmit-latency) to internal CI metrics bridge
- [x] Add docs/ci/README.md describing the adapter and fastpath rules
- [x] Add migration note in docs and small rollout plan

Why this is safe: the adapter is opt-in behind workflow updates; the presubmit workflows are staged behind a rollout flag for the first week. Dep-visibility only influences fastpath gating and does not block default presubmit lanes. Release automation is unchanged in this PR (no artifact signing changes).

Rollout plan: merge to main -> opt-in on small team repos -> enable for core services after 1 week of telemetry. We will monitor presubmit-latency and false skips; rollback by re-enabling legacy fragments if needed.

Related: Linear ENG-4821 (presubmit feedback), ENG-4956 (dep surface telemetry).

review_comments:
Aaron Kim: Suggest keeping a short compatibility shim for repos that still invoke make ci locally. Maya: added Makefile targets that forward to the adapter and included migration note.
Lucia Gomez: Can dep-visibility run in parallel with unit tests to avoid adding latency? Maya: yes — the adapter kicks off dep-visibility asynchronously and only waits for its fingerprint when evaluating fastpath rules.
Ravi Shah: Add a feature-flag env var to gate the fastpath behavior during rollout. Maya: added CI_FASTPATH_ENABLED and defaulted to false in workflows; documented rollout steps.

discussion_outcome:
Addressed reviewer feedback: compatibility shim, async dep-visibility, rollout flag added; all reviewers approved

notes_on_testing:
Ran presubmit simulations locally and on ephemeral runners. Observed median presubmit bootstrap time drop from ~14s to ~7s for node/python shards. Telemetry hooks exercised in staging for 48h before merge.

post_merge_tasks:
1) Enable CI_FASTPATH_ENABLED=true for core services on 2024-11-25 once telemetry is stable. 2) Remove legacy Makefile CI targets after two weeks. 3) Monitor presubmit-latency and dep-change-rate dashboards.

ana: Heads-up: multiple reports of SDK differences across runtimes (Node vs Edge) and CJS/TS consumers hitting types issues. Anyone seen this?
sam: Yep. Two problems: how we pick `fetch` (undici vs global) and ESM/CJS export shape + typings.
mike: Need a tiny repro - is it missing API or import error?
ana: User on Cloudflare Workers: `TypeError: fetch is not a function` because our dynamic undici import is getting hoisted by bundlers.

mike: TS: ship `.d.ts`, set `types` in package.json and ensure exports map covers CJS/ESM; add README snippet for `require` vs `import`.
sam: Action items: sam -> runtime helper PR; ana -> exports/types doc; julie -> Workers CI job; mike -> retry/redirect tests.

records.title: new-hires
records.text:
new-hires

noah: Morning — first day, thanks for having me! I'm trying to enroll my personal MBP (M2, macOS 13.6) into MDM but I'm stuck on the 'Enable Disk Encryption' step. Web UI shows 'MDM command failed (403)'. Anyone seen this?

it-support: welcome! :wave: Can you paste the device serial and a screenshot of the error? 403 usually means the MDM couldn't escrow the recovery key (policy or existing FV state).

noah: serial C02ZQ0XXXXXX. Screenshot attached (can't paste here). I ran a couple of commands mentioned in another thread: 
```
$ sudo fdesetup status
FileVault is On.
```
and 
```
$ sudo profiles status -type enrollment
Device is enrolled via MDM: YES
```
But the console still refuses to proceed with key escrow.

emily: hi noah — quick note: if you encrypted the disk previously with a personal iCloud escrow or custom recovery, some MDMs won't override that without a rekey/escrow step. Do you remember if you used your Apple ID to enable FileVault?

noah: I did the FileVault setup when I first bought the laptop — it suggested using my iCloud. Not sure how to check the escrow method.

it-support: ok. Two options: 1) We can guide you through re-escrowing the FV key to company KMS (preferred), or 2) we can provision a temporary admin account and re-enroll the machine clean. Which would you prefer?

noah: prefer not to wipe personal data. Can we do the re-escrow?

it-support: yes. First, run this and paste output: 
```
sudo fdesetup haspersonalrecoverykey
sudo fdesetup list
```
Should be quick. If a personal recovery key is present, the MDM will reject automated escrow until it's rotated.

noah: output: 
```
$ sudo fdesetup haspersonalrecoverykey
true
$ sudo fdesetup list
user: Noah (UUID: XXXXX-XXXX-...) - enabled
```

mdm-bot: Enrollment audit: user=noah serial=C02ZQ0XXXXXX status=FDE_ESCROW_FAILED code=403

it-support: yup — personal key present. We'll need to run the change-recovery command to generate a new escrowable key and then push it to our keyserver. I can remote-guide you. Steps: 1) we'll create a temporary sudo session for you, 2) run `sudo fdesetup changerecovery -personal` to remove the personal escrow and generate a new key, 3) run the MDM escrow command.

emily: small heads up — on macOS 13+ the `changerecovery` flow will prompt for an existing user password. Keep your account password handy.

noah: down to try. what's the temporary sudo session?

it-support: give me a 1-hour window. We'll add your account to a short-lived admin ACL and remove it after escrow completes. Also we'll monitor the enrollment audit. If you want, we can do this over screenshare.

anton: FYI if anything looks off we can also trigger a forced rekey from our MDM portal (it sends a device command) but that will also fail until the personal key is rotated locally. Good call to do changerecovery.

noah: ok ready now — screenshare started in 5.

it-support: perfect. When we run this: 
```
sudo fdesetup changerecovery -personal
```
you'll be asked for your account password and then for a new recovery key. We'll instruct the MDM to collect it and confirm.

(noah shares screen)
it-support: accepted the password, running. ... got the new key. Pushing to MDM now.

mdm-bot: Recovery key escrow received for serial=C02ZQ0XXXXXX user=noah status=SUCCESS

emily: nice! can you confirm the web UI now shows encryption status as 'escrowed'?

noah: the UI now shows "Disk encryption: Escrowed — Managed" and the 403 is gone. THANK YOU 🙏

it-support: glad it worked — we'll remove the temporary admin and close the session. Two follow-ups for you: 1) sign the device attestation in Okta (device trust) if prompted, 2) review the employee laptop policy about personal-device enrollment: https://redwood.internal/it/device-policy (link).

noah: got it. tagging this thread for anyone else who runs into a 403 during FV escrow. super helpful.

it-support: note for records — ticket #IT-4821 created with steps taken. Closing in 24h if no regressions. :white_check_mark:

records.text:
Request: scoped extended log retention for Umbrabank SOC2 evidence

["From: Alice Thomas <alice.thomas@umbrabank.com>
To: michael.grant@redwood.com
Cc: procure@umbrabank.com, security@umbrabank.com
Date: 2026-10-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: scoped extended log retention for audit evidence

Hi Michael,

We're in the midst of our annual SOC 2 readiness run and our auditors have flagged a gap: for a small subset of production tenants we need session-level debug traces retained for 12 months (currently you default to 30 days). The scope is highly limited — only transactions for our payments integration (tenant id prefix UMB-PAY-) and only fields A,B,C (no PII payload).

Can Redwood provide a customer-scoped retention variance for Umbrabank, plus the artifacts auditors will accept (proof of secure storage, access logs, and a proof-of-delete for when the window lapses)? Attached is a short form our legal team uses for retention exceptions.

Specific asks:
- Confirmation that a 12-month scoped retention is technically feasible and which controls would apply
- A list of artifacts you can provide to auditors (hashes, access audit trail, KMS envelope records, deletion timeline)
- Any additional compensating controls you recommend (retention encryption at rest, restricted admin access, quarterly attestation)

We'd appreciate a reply by EOD Tuesday so we can include it in our SOC evidence pack.

Thanks,
Alice Thomas
Sr. Security Manager | Umbrabank
", "From: michael.grant@redwood.com <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Alice Thomas <alice.thomas@umbrabank.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scoped extended log retention for audit evidence

Alice — thanks for the clear ask and the form (received). Short answer: yes, we can support a limited, tenant-scoped extended retention for debug/session traces, but there are a few engineering and compliance steps we need to confirm. Looping in Naomi (Security) and Priyom (Ops) to outline the controls and deliverables; Ben on AE/Sales side for contract/term updates.

Preliminary reply to your bullets:
- Feasibility: We have a feature toggle and per-tenant retention metadata; Ops can route UMB-PAY-* to a longer TTL bucket. We'll need a small infra change to materialize the retention window and ensure KV cache eviction rules are adjusted — no code changes to customer app surface.
- Artifacts we can provide: time-stamped storage manifest (hash per file), KMS envelope metadata (key id and envelope creation time), restricted access audit logs (who/what/when), and a deletion job report (time, objects targeted, verification hashes).
- Compensating controls: we recommend envelope encryption with a customer KMS key if required, role-based access (separate admin role for retention operations), and a quarterly retention attestation signed by Redwood Security.

Naomi: can you confirm the exact list of artifacts we would be comfortable presenting to an external auditor for a 12-month scoped retention? Priyom: what is the expected lead time for enabling this in production and any SLO/latency impact I should flag to the customer?

I'll prep a short evidence checklist and attach our standard retention-exception template for your legal team.

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
", "From: naomi.feldman@redwood.com <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: michael.grant@redwood.com
Cc: alice.thomas@umbrabank.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scoped extended log retention for audit evidence

Alice / team — Thanks for the details. Confirming what we can reasonably attest to for Umbrabank's auditors: 

Deliverables (final list):
- Retention scope document (tenant prefixes, data classes included/excluded) with time-window definition
- Storage manifest: daily digest CSV with object paths, SHA256 hashes, and timestamps for the scoped retention bucket (retained for the 12-month window + 30 days for verification)
- KMS envelope metadata: key ID, envelope creation times, and a reference ID we can correlate to the stored manifests (we do not hand over raw keys)
- Access audit logs: host/service principal, admin user, operation, timestamp, and presigned object accesses (redacted IPs on request)
- Deletion verification: when TTL expires we run a deletion job that produces a verification manifest with post-delete checksums (zero-length markers) and a deletion timestamp; we can provide the job run logs and manifest.

Controls & caveats:
- We will not surface application payloads or PII in the audit artifacts. If Umbrabank requires payload-level retention, we'd need a separate review.
- Encrypted at rest by default; if you require CMK (customer-managed key) we can support via our KMS integration but we need procurement sign-off and a CMK onboarding window (2–3 weeks).
- Access to the retention manifests will be provided via a limited S3 share with time-limited credentials; we recommend the customer provide a list of auditor principals who need access.

I'm attaching a sample manifest and a short diagram that shows where the scoped bucket sits in our topology. Priyom, can you confirm lead time and if this adds measurable cost to the tenant (e.g., storage + retrieval for manifests)?

Naomi Feldman
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-soc2-log-evidence-sample.txt)
", "From: priyom.das@redwood.com <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: michael.grant@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Cc: alice.thomas@umbrabank.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scoped extended log retention for audit evidence

Short operational update:
- Lead time: 7 business days to wire the retention policy, add the tenant routing rule, and enable the daily manifest job in prod (assuming no CMK onboarding). If customer requests CMK, add 10 business days for key registration, policy updates, and KMS testing.
- SLO/latency: negligible impact on request latency; storage increases and manifest generation add a small background I/O load.
- Cost/estimate: incremental storage cost (~$0.02/GB-month) + manifest generation and retrieval costs. I'll produce a quick estimate after vendor confirms expected volume for UMB-PAY-* tenants.
- Security controls: manifests are written to a customer-scoped bucket with restricted ACLs; deletion jobs are audited and require two-step approval for manual deletion outside TTL.

Next steps I recommend we take today:
1) Michael / Ben: provide a short commercial addendum that indicates the scoped retention exception, term (12 months), and any price delta.
2) Umbrabank: confirm the exact tenant prefixes and the auditor principal list for access.
3) Naomi / Ops: finalize the artifact list and deliver a sample manifest to the auditor sandbox.

Priyom Das
Staff Engineer, Production Systems | Redwood Inference
", "From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: alice.thomas@umbrabank.com, michael.grant@redwood.com
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-20T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: scoped extended log retention for audit evidence

Alice — appreciate the quick turnaround from the team here. For contract/commercials: we can cover the scoped 12-month retention under a short addendum to the existing SOW for Umbrabank (no long-term change required). Proposed financials: monthly incremental storage pass-through + a one-time engineering enablement fee of $5,000 to cover Ops onboarding and manifest configuration. I can put a redlined addendum in DocuSign today if you confirm: (a) tenant prefixes (UMB-PAY-*), (b) acceptance that payloads remain excluded, and (c) auditor access list.

Attaching the retention exception template and a simple topology diagram for your legal/audit review. If that works, I'll generate the DocuSign and loop procurement.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
(attachments: umbrabank_retention_request_form.pdf, scoped-retention-diagram.png)"]

records.title: ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing
records.text:
ADR: Declarative Contract Tests and Schema Fencing

Summary

This ADR defines a company-wide standard for declarative contract tests and a complementary "schema fencing" discipline to prevent schema drift between services and the Redwood platform (APIs, telemetry, and model-serving payloads). The goal is to make API and model I/O contracts machine-testable, versioned, and CI-gated, minimizing production surprises and simplifying rollback and compatibility reasoning.

Context and motivation

Recent incidents and near-misses were traced to silent schema changes that allowed malformed or unexpectedly shaped requests/telemetry to flow into the runtime. Ad-hoc unit tests are insufficient for cross-service contract guarantees because:

- Contracts span teams (edge proxies, gateways, runtime, and client SDKs).
- Behavioral compatibility is not captured by type checks alone (e.g., field deprecation with semantic changes).
- Runtime routing fallback and model-variant compatibility require an explicit, testable matrix.

This ADR proposes:

1. A declarative, YAML-first contract-test spec that lives next to service code and in a central conformance repo for cross-service scopes.
2. A "schema fencing" lifecycle that fences allowed shape changes via explicit change proposals, automated conformance checks, and CI gates.
3. A conformance status ledger and telemetry for contract drift and failed-matrix cell SLI.

Scope

Applies to:

- Public and internal HTTP/GRPC REST endpoints (edge, control-plane, telemetry ingestion).
- Model-serving input/output schemas (prompts, structured responses, embeddings metadata).
- Streaming/session protocols where message schemas are negotiated.

Out of scope:

- Internal-only helper functions that are never consumed by other services.
- Ad-hoc developer prototypes until they are promoted to a supported service.

Key concepts

Declarative contract test spec (DCTS):
- A human-friendly YAML format that describes request/response shapes, example inputs, success/failure predicates, and conformance categories (strict, tolerant, deprecated).
- DCTS entries can be unit-run (local), CI-run (service-level), and cross-service-run (integration conformance matrix).

Schema fencing:
- Every change to a DCTS schema field must be accompanied by a Change Proposal (CP) file and an automated compatibility check.
- CPs are accepted automatically if they pass compatibility rules or fail open for manual review if they are breaking.

Conformance matrix and ledger:
- A centrally aggregated matrix that tracks which service versions (and model variants) satisfy which DCTS cells.
- Each matrix cell has a pass/fail history and a conformance SLI aggregated daily.

Rules and compatibility classes

Fields are labeled with one of: required, optional, deprecated, extension. Compatibility rules:

- required -> optional: allowed but requires explicit CP and CI signal.
- optional -> required: breaking change; requires canary/rollout plan and staged opt-in.
- remove deprecated field: allowed only after 3 release cycles and >95% conformance across callers.
- add new field marked extension: always allowed if receivers ignore unknown fields (tolerant mode).

Change proposal workflow (brief)

1. Author creates a CP file in the service repo under docs/contracts/cps/<pr>.yaml describing intent, compatibility class, rollout plan, and rollback criteria.
2. CI runs: unit tests, DCTS local run, contract linters, and cross-service dry-run against the latest conformance snapshot.
3. If auto-check passes (non-breaking or safe extension), merge proceeds. If flagged as potentially breaking, the CP moves to manual review by contract stewards and product owners.
4. After merge, integration conformance jobs run nightly to validate callers and receivers.

Example DCTS snippet (YAML)

# Example: /v1/generate request/response
# Save as service/docs/contracts/dcts/generate.v1.yaml
---
endpoint: POST /v1/generate
scope: public
version: 1.0.0
mode: strict
request: 
  content-type: application/json
  schema: |
    type: object
    properties:
      prompt:
        type: string
      features:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: true
    required: [prompt]
examples:
  - name: simplest
    request: {"prompt": "Summarize the following text..."}
response:
  schema: |
    type: object
    properties:
      id: {type: string}
      output: {type: string}
      tokens_consumed: {type: integer}
    required: [id, output]
predicates:
  - description: output must be non-empty
    jq: ".output | length > 0"
conformance_category: strict

Automation and CI integration

CI responsibilities (service repo):
- Run local DCTS validation (schema validity, example conformance).
- Run contract linter: enforces required metadata fields (owner, risk_level, test_coverage_min).
- Publish DCTS artifact to conformance-bucket/<service>/<version>/dcts.yaml on successful merge.

Cross-repo conformance job (central):
- Nightly job that pulls the published DCTS artifacts and runs pairwise checks across known callers and receivers.
- Failing cells create RFC-style issues in the responsible service repo and update the conformance ledger with failure signals.

Conformance ledger and dashboard

The ledger is a time-series-friendly table with columns described below and exposed in the Redwood Console and an internal dashboard. Store as rows in our metrics DB and index in the conformance service. (Table described in prose below.)

Required columns (ledger row): timestamp, service_a, service_a_version, service_b, service_b_version, endpoint, dcts_version, test_case_id, result (pass|fail), failure_reason, run_id.

Operational SLOs and alerting

- Nightly conformance pass rate for critical public endpoints >= 99.0%. Alert if < 98.0% over a 24-hour rolling window.
- Any new CP that causes a regression in an existing passing matrix cell triggers a P1 review if the affected client is production and >= 10% traffic.

Gating and release policy

- Service merge gating: Non-breaking CPs are mergeable. Breaking CPs require manual approval and a staged rollout with canary conformance verifying client behavior.
- Platform releases (runtime, SDKs): must maintain 100% conformance for official SDK bindings across supported minor versions.

Rollout and rollback playbook (high level)

1. Pre-merge: author runs smoke DCTS locally and creates CP with rollout notes.
2. Merge: DCTS published and cross-repo nightlies scheduled.
3. Canary: route 5% traffic to new service variant for 2 hours while conformance checks run.
4. Monitor: observe ledger and user-facing errors for regressions.
5. If failure SLI breached or critical callers fail, execute rollback to previous version and open an incident review.

Telemetry and observability requirements

Each contract-test run must emit:
- conftest.run_id (UUID)
- conftest.service (service name/version)
- conftest.endpoint
- conftest.test_case_id
- conftest.result (pass|fail)
- conftest.duration_ms

These fields are sent to the conformance-ingest pipeline with low-cardinality sampling for historical debugging. Link failures to trace IDs when available.

Owner and stewardship

- Contract steward role: a cross-functional team (API Platform + SRE + Product) that maintains the conformance harness, linter rules, and central ledger.
- Service owners: must author and maintain DCTS files for each public surface and model variant.

Open questions and tradeoffs

- How strict should default mode be for internal endpoints? Proposal: internal endpoints default to tolerant mode, but any endpoint used by another service must be promoted to strict with a DCTS.
- Cost vs. coverage: nightly full-matrix checks are expensive. We propose prioritized sweeps (critical endpoints every night, others weekly).

Migration plan

1. Pilot: Onboard three services (edge-proxy, runtime-controller, and the embeddings-ingest) to the DCTS and CP workflow over Q2 2026.
2. Expand to all public endpoints and model-serving inputs by Q4 2026.
3. Enforce gate for new public endpoints starting Q1 2027.

Appendix: sample CLI commands and linter config

# Local validation
#   conftest validate service/docs/contracts/dcts/*.yaml

# Publish artifact (CI step)
#   conftest publish --bucket=conformance-bucket --service=$SERVICE --version=$VERSION dcts.yaml

# Central conformance run (dry-run example)
#   conformance-runner --matrix-file=matrix.json --artifacts-dir=artifacts/ --output=ledger.csv

# Linter rules (excerpt)
# required: [owner, risk_level, conformance_category, test_coverage_min]

Notes on documentation style

- Keep DCTS files short and example-driven. Prefer real-world examples over exhaustive machine-generated schemas.
- Use the CP description field to capture rationale and expected client impact.

References

- See canonical request schema and validation playbook: /architecture-and-standards/api-standards/canonical-request-schema-and-validation-playbook-2025
- Variant compatibility ledger: /architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards/variant-compatibility-ledger-and-stewardship-protocol-2026

Approval

Approved by: API Platform leadership, SRE management, and Product for runtime conformance.

maya: pasted one in #incidents earlier but TL;DR: model returned a function-like object but shape mismatched (array vs object) and our code treated it as non-fatal, swallowed it.
leo: ugh. is that from strict-validate=on? I thought canary was running permissive soft-validate.
sasha: canary config is permissive but our coercion layer only logs at DEBUG and sample rate is 0.1. so most bad shapes never show up in SLO dashboards.
irene: the UX problem is users see no error and no retry. They assume model didn't call tool and keep resending prompts.
maya: proposal: make a short-term toggle to escalate coercion logs for canary traffic where fncall appears in model output but schema rejects. Add a line item in rollout checklist.
dan: agree. also we should surface a small counter in the console: "fncall-dropped-by-validator" with tags (route, model-version, canary).
leo: how expensive is bumping sample rate? metrics ingestion and retention cost will spike but for a 24h debug window should be fine.
sasha: ops-bot: note that we may need to increase logging retention if we want to backfill the last 48h. :warning: 
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: increased retention requires approval from finance. pinged @finance for a one-time lift.
irene: longer term: we need a soft-validate mode that returns a structured warning with the response, e.g. keep the toolcall in response but add "validation_warnings": [...]. That way callers can opt-in to degrade gracefully.
leo: can we implement that without big API changes? Maybe a header "X-Schema-Mode: warn" that the SDK can set.
dan: header sounds good for SDK clients, but platform should also allow route-level default. console toggle per-route would help teams who rely on strict semantics.
maya: also add telemetry: count of "toolcall-in-model-output" vs "toolcall-accepted" vs "toolcall-coerced". We need those three to reason about rates.
sasha: dashboard ask: a small panel in per-route metrics showing those counts + sample traces. I'll sketch a mock and drop it in the Roadmap doc.
leo: for immediate mitigation, I'll flip canary coercion logs to INFO and bump sample to 1.0 for 12h. will monitor cost.
irene: please also add an alert: if dropped-toolcall rate >0.5% for 10m then page oncall.
dan: should the alert page ops or eng-platform? page ops first then escalate to eng-platform.
maya: ok action list: (1) leo: bump sample & log level for 12h (2) sasha: dashboard mock + alert panel (3) dan: add console counter + route toggle design (4) irene: spec for X-Schema-Mode warn header and soft-validate payload shape.
leo: starting the log bump now. will post follow-up in this thread when done.
maya: thanks. if anyone sees customer ticket threads linking to this, pls add context and tag me.
leo: done - logs bumped, sample=1.0, retention increased for 48h. watching metrics.
sasha: mock uploaded: https://redwood.internal/designs/fncall-coercion-dashboard - feedback welcome.
irene: I'll draft the header design this afternoon. dan, can you add a short console UX wire for the per-route toggle?
dan: on it, will share a quick Figma frame in a few hours.
maya: great. closing the loop after we gather 12h of telemetry. thanks all :)

people-ops

Nina V (Eng): quick question — planning 10 weeks parental leave for a domestic adoption in Oct. Couple of weird ones: 1) does leave pause my equity vesting schedule? 2) can Redwood's dependent childcare subsidy be applied retroactively if I start it after leave starts?
Omar J (People Ops): congrats! short answers: 1) leave doesn't pause standard vesting schedule automatically. we offer an option to extend your vesting window by the leave length for eligible long leaves — that requires a written election before leave starts. ping me and we'll add it to your form. 2) childcare subsidy can be started during leave but not paid retroactively; you can enroll and it will apply from the next payroll cycle after enrollment.
Leah M (Finance): equity addendum — we can do a vesting extension addendum (LOE) for leaves >= 8 weeks. steps: employee signs LOE, manager confirms leave dates, Finance records in equity ledger. Code note: put "LEAVE-EXT" on the equity note so grants don't auto-expire incorrectly.
Nina V (Eng): good to know. if i elect LOE, does it affect option exercise window on termination?
Leah M (Finance): LOE extends vesting only, not post-termination exercise windows. exercise window rules unchanged unless you negotiate a separate exception with comp. we can loop Legal if you need a contract change.
Nina V (Eng): cool. about the subsidy — i missed the open-enrollment cutoff this month. can i enroll mid-cycle?
Omar J (People Ops): you can enroll outside OE for qualifying life events like adoption. submit the Adoption Enrollment form in benefits portal and upload placement docs. Benefits will enable subsidy on next payroll cycle. subsidy is capped at $600/month and requires receipts.
payroll-bot: Enrollment checklist -> https://intranet.redwood/hr/benefits/adoption-enroll
```
1) Employee files Adoption Enrollment
2) Upload placement docs
3) People Ops confirms
4) Payroll adds SUBSIDY code starting next cycle
```
payroll-bot: subsidy is processed as a reimbursement (non-taxable) if receipts show childcare expense. if you prefer advance stipends, that's taxable and handled via the Emergency Stipend form.
Benefits Team: to clarify 1 adoption is a qualifying life event; subsidy will be active once docs verified. receipts must show childcare provider name, dates, and amount. we can back-date subsidy only if the placement falls within the same calendar month and you filed within 30 days — otherwise no retro pay.
Nina V (Eng): thanks all. Omar, i'll file the parental leave + LOE request today and upload docs. Leah, can you flag Comp so they know LOE is incoming?
Leah M (Finance): flagged Comp. thanks.
Omar J (People Ops): got it. Nina, DM me the final dates and i'll start the LOE paperwork. congrats again! :tada:

records.title: devex
records.text:
devex

marta: Heads up — noticed an odd edge case with the Python SDK streaming API. If an async generator consumer breaks early (e.g. `break` in the loop) while the SDK is in the middle of an auth refresh, the underlying socket stays open and we leak a connection.

marta: Repro steps:
1) start a streaming SSE call with token that expires in ~1s
2) in the client, ensure auth refresh triggers during stream delivery
3) in consumer do `async for chunk in stream: break` on first chunk
Result: socket fd remains open on server and stream task never fully finalizes.

alex: Oof. Any logs or minimal repro?

marta: Paste of minimal snippet:
```py
async def run():
    async for chunk in client.stream("/v1/streams/chat", payload):
        print(chunk)
        break  # early exit
```
I can repro on mac + py3.11 with our sdk 0.12.3.

devex-bot: New error fingerprint created for marta: STREAM_LEAK_DURING_AUTH_REFRESH (auto-collected)

jon: Which transport are you using? aiohttp/ws/tornado?

marta: aiohttp connector, default settings. Also happens on linux ci.

alex: Two hypotheses: 1) generator finalizer not awaiting an internal close coroutine; 2) auth refresh cancels a waiter but leaves socket open. Can you capture a tcpdump or lsof on the worker?

marta: lsof shows the fd stays in ESTABLISHED and Python process still has task referencing _StreamReaderProtocol.

ivan: Possible quick workaround: instead of breaking, call `await stream.aclose()` before break. Does that help?

marta: I tried `await stream.aclose()` in finally block — that closes socket, so it's a usable workaround. But consumers expect `break` to be sufficient.

sam (devex): We should make generator implement `__aexit__` so `async with client.stream(...) as s:` closes reliably, and also add a finalizer that schedules `aclose()` instead of relying on GC. Also add typing hint: returns `AsyncIterator[bytes] | AsyncIterator[str]` so mypy users are aware.

alex: Agreed. Also need to handle an auth-refresh cancellation race: if refresh task cancels waiter, ensure underlying transport is closed in cancellation handler.

devex-bot: Suggest filing a GH issue template.

marta: Filed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/842 — contains logs + minimal repro.

jon: Thanks. Assigning to eng-runtime and devex for joint fix. Is this high-priority? Looks like it affects long-lived streams for a subset of users.

sam (devex): Priority P1 for next patch release — UX impact is real (leaky descriptors in serverless). I'll draft the change: make async generator return a wrapper object with `__anext__`/`__aenter__`/`__aexit__` forwarding and ensure `__aexit__` calls `await aclose()`. Also add unit test that triggers auth refresh.

ivan: Small note for impl: avoid finalizer that does blocking IO on interpreter shutdown; schedule close on loop via `loop.call_soon_threadsafe(asyncio.create_task, stream.aclose())`.

marta: Great. I'll validate the fix on my repro once there's a patch. Thanks everyone :sparkles:

records.title: APAC edge capacity ops scrub — week of May 7, 2028
records.text:
APAC edge capacity ops scrub — week of May 7, 2028

Attendees: Asha Patel (owner), Miguel Ortega, Connor Li, Priya Shah, Lena Voss, on-call: infra-weekend

Purpose: quick scrub to validate APAC edge priming ahead of the expected marketing-driven surge (mobile chat product) targeting SEA on May 12–15. Focus areas: available GPU headroom, prewarming schedule, heterogeneous instance mix, fallback routing, and runbook alignment for preemption risk.

Summary / tl;dr:
- Current committed edge pool for APAC (Tokyo, Singapore, Mumbai): 360 GPUs (equivalent v100-slices). Measured steady baseline utilization = 62% (7-day trailing avg). Planned short-term hedging target = 20% additional headroom (~72 GPUs) to absorb 48–72 hour surge.
- Short warmup experiment (n=3) improved median cold-start latency by 210ms for typical 512-token interactive traffic; cost ~2.8% extra token-cost during prewarm windows. Tradeoff: small cost vs SLO exposure.
- Identified one runbook drift: automated preemptible fallback policy was still set to fall back to a non-quantized variant (higher memory) — causes capacity pressure on certain hosts.
- Action items: immediate policy change to prefer quantized fallback variants, prioritize 40 GPU allocation from regional spare pool, and schedule a deeper priming dry run Wed 2028-05-10 02:00 UTC to validate cross-zone failover.

Observed metrics (as of 2028-05-09 06:00 UTC):
- Committed pool: 360 GPUs (raw) across 3 zones: TYO-1(140), SIN-1(120), BOM-1(100)
- Live instances: 338 GPUs (94% of committed online due to two maintenance hosts in BOM-1)
- 7d util avg: 62%
- 24h tail (p95 token latency, 512 tokens): 1540ms APAC edge aggregate
- Spike forecast probability (next 7 days): 28% (marketing campaign + partner launch)

Risk register items discussed:
1) Preemption cascade on heterogeneous hosts — root cause: some non-dedicated fleets still able to receive preemptible eviction signals; during last surge we saw chained migration delays causing 3–6min window of elevated latency. Mitigation: enforce eviction-migration isolation via taints for edge-prime nodes; scheduled change request INFRA-7382.
2) Runbook drift — older fallback policy (non-quantized) in control plane: causes memory oversubscription during fallback events. Short-term mitigation: override routing policy to tag model-variant=quantized for APAC edge; long-term: conformance test in CI for runtime variant compatibility.
3) Cross-zone priming gap — SIN-1 had only 40% of expected prefix cache hits due to differing traffic mix. Need to align prefix populations and prewarm sequences.

Decisions made:
- Approve temporary 20% capacity hedging for 72 hours starting 2028-05-11 00:00 UTC. Chargeback plan: Hosted-tier surge credit to product team; track cost vs SLO.
- Use quantized fallback variant as primary fallback for APAC edge until INFRA-7390 (runtime A/B) concludes.
- Nightly prewarm window 02:00–04:00 UTC for edge regions to reduce cold-start tail; initial trial for 48 hours only.

Planned ops & schedule:
- 2028-05-09 18:00 UTC: change routing policy to tag model-variant=quantized (Owner: Miguel Ortega, due: 2028-05-09 20:00 UTC)
- 2028-05-10 02:00 UTC: cross-zone dry run — simulate zone outage in SIN-1 and verify failover to TYO-1/BOM-1 (Owner: Connor Li, runbook owner Priya Shah)
- 2028-05-11 00:00 UTC: allocate 72 GPUs from spare pool to APAC edge, distributed TYO+SIN with one-zone limit to avoid single-point capacity drain (Owner: Lena Voss)
- 2028-05-11–2028-05-13: monitor surge; daily sync 08:30 UTC for first 72 hours (Owner: Asha Patel)

Notes on prewarm experiment (brief):
- Method: triggered a controlled prefix population job that stimulates typical user prompt shapes and pins kv-cache for top 25k prefixes. Ran 3 parallel jobs per zone for 30 minutes.
- Outcome: median p95 token latency improvement = -210ms; p99 improved by ~450ms; observed CPU overhead on host < 6% and estimated incremental cost = 2.8% of token spend for the window.
- Observations: warm cache improved small-chat interactions most; for large-batched inference there was negligible benefit. Implication: enable prewarm only for interactive-route tag.

Runbook & automation gaps called out:
- CI test missing: variant compatibility smoke test — should be gated on rollout pipeline (assigned INFRA-7390).
- Monitoring alert thresholds: p95 token latency alert for APAC edge currently at 2.0s — we will reduce to 1.6s for interactive routes during event windows. (Owner: Priya Shah)
- Eviction mitigation: need automated graceful rebalancer to pre-schedule container handoff 10 min before maintenance window (RFC in progress).

Action items (explicit):
- Miguel Ortega: update routing policy to prefer quantized fallback (done target 2028-05-09 20:00 UTC) — linked INFRA-7382
- Connor Li & Priya Shah: run cross-zone dry run 2028-05-10 02:00 UTC and capture latency + error profiles; publish notes to Confluence (due 2028-05-10 10:00 UTC)
- Lena Voss: request allocation 72 GPUs from spare pool and update capacity dashboard; ensure one-zone cap in allocation (due 2028-05-10 04:00 UTC)
- Asha Patel: lead daily surge sync 08:30 UTC 5/11–5/13 and consolidate incident channel plan into the operations binder (due 2028-05-11 07:30 UTC)
- Engineering-sre: add prewarm cost tag to billing pipeline so we can attribute extra spend to the marketing surge (Owner: SRE billing team, tracker: GH #4125)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we expand priming to include high-frequency prefixes for enterprise customers only? (pros: reduces latency for paying tiers; cons: added cost and cache fragmentation)
- What is the exact rollback threshold for the nightly prewarm window? Propose automated rollback if p95 increases by >10% vs baseline measured 24h prior.

Appendix: quick links and references
- INFRA-7382 (Jira): enforce taints & eviction isolation — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-7382
- Cross-zone dry-run playbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/APAC+Edge+Priming+Plan
- Dry-run runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal/pull/4125
- Slack thread: #gpu-ops: https://app.slack.com/client/TXXXXXXXX/C0123456789

Notes to self / scratch (informal):
- If SIN-1 traffic mix stays chatty while TYO uses more long-form, we should consider varying prefix population by zone rather than uniform.
- When surge subsides, evaluate whether we can refund or reassign spare GPUs to EU burst pool (cost ops).

Meeting end 2028-05-09 07:05 UTC.
