records.title: Autoscale Harmonizer and Isolation Patterns — PRD Sketch
records.text:
Autoscale Harmonizer and Isolation Patterns — PRD Sketch

Purpose and context

This is a working PRD sketch proposing the Autoscale Harmonizer: a coordinated, workload-aware autoscaling and isolation subsystem for Dedicated capacity. The harmonizer’s role is to manage multiple scaling lanes (reserved capacity, soft-burst lanes, and opportunistic/backfill), make admission decisions, and enforce tenant isolation and fairness while optimizing cost and latency SLAs.

Why this is needed (problem statement)
- Current Dedicated autoscalers are per-pool and reactive; tenants with spiky usage either over-provision or experience throttles.
- Burst mechanisms exist but are siloed (credits, prewarm queues) and cause noisy neighbor effects or surprise preemptions.
- Ops lacks a single control point that can reason about cross-tenant fairness, model mix, and model-specific latency SLOs.

Goals (what success looks like)
- Provide a centralized decision layer (Harmonizer) that: 1) reduces SLA violations during demand spikes by 30% vs. baseline, 2) reduces average reserved headroom by 15% across fleets, 3) keeps burst-preemption incidents measurable and explainable.
- Implement a tiered burst/escape semantics that are predictable to customers: soft-burst (best-effort), guaranteed-boost (timeboxed reserved), and opportunistic backfill.
- Ensure tenant isolation primitives that prevent model-dominated tenants from starving others — fairness policy pluggable per-org.

Non-goals
- This PRD does not propose a complete replacement of node-level autoscalers or scheduler internals. It focuses on orchestration and admission control above existing mechanisms.

High-level solution overview
- Autoscale Harmonizer: a control-plane service that aggregates telemetry (per-tenant QPS, token distribution by model, KV cache hit rates, per-route latency, backpressure signals) and outputs admissions and lane allocations.
- Lanes (logical capacity categories):
  - Reserved lane: tenant-owned reserved instances (SLA-backed).
  - Soft-burst lane: transient burst capacity drawn from a shared pool, tracked via burst-escrow credits and time-decay rules.
  - Guarded boost lane: short-lived guaranteed capacity (purchased or admin-granted) with timeboxed guarantees.
  - Opportunistic backfill: preemptible capacity used when utilization < threshold.
- Isolation patterns: soft quotas + dynamic weight adjustments, tenant fencing on severe contention, and model-aware shaping (per-model per-tenant weights).

Key components and behaviors
1) Demand estimator (shadow predictor)
- Lightweight ML model + heuristic ensemble that forecasts 1–5m and 15–60m demand windows per-tenant and per-model. Uses request rate, recent latency tail growth, and standing prefix cache metrics.
- Output used to proactively prewarm and also to compute burst-cost tradeoffs.

2) Admission arbiter (Harmonizer core)
- On request spike, arbiter consults: current lane quotas, burst-escrow balance, predicted demand, and cross-tenant fairness state.
- Returns decision: admit into lane X, queue (soft-defer), or reject-with-fallback.
- Supports priorities: e.g., admin-emergency, guaranteed-boost, SLA, standard, best-effort.

3) Burst-escrow credits
- Tenants accrue or purchase credits; credits consumed during soft-burst admissions.
- Credits decay/age to avoid hoarding and to free long-term unused allocations.
- Rules: credits allow soft-burst usage up to a configurable multiplier over baseline QPS for a bounded window.

4) Fairness and weight allocator
- Continuous fairness shim that adjusts tenant weights against lanes when contention detected: proportional-share with dampening to avoid oscillation.
- Optionally apply cost-weighted fairness (tenant willing to pay more gets higher weight) — surfaced as billing/promises.

5) Preemption and graceful degradation
- Opportunistic backfill is preemptible with 30s drain notification.
- Soft-burst may be revoked if a higher-priority tenant requests guaranteed-boost; revocation policy tries to minimize in-flight work by refusing new requests and allowing short tails to finish.
- FallBack policy: automatic downgrade to a smaller model variant or to a cached result when admission is denied; fallback routes configured per-tenant.

6) Observability and explainability
- Audit log per admission decision (why admitted/rejected, credits consumed, fairness adjustment).
- Per-tenant dashboard: burst usage, credit balance, recent preemptions, SLA incidents.
- Operators can replay harmonizer decisions retrospectively for postmortems.

Configuration surface (user-facing)
- Tenant console options: 
  - burst-escrow-enable: bool
  - burst-escrow-cap: numeric (tokens/minute or requests/minute equivalent)
  - guaranteed-boost-window: seconds/minutes (length of guaranteed boosts)
  - priority-class: [guaranteed, standard, best-effort]
  - fallback-policy: [deny, downgrade-model, cached-response, queue-with-timeout]
- Defaults chosen to be conservative; product will expose a simple recommended profile and an advanced tuning panel.

Operational runbook highlights (ops playbook sketch)
- Monitoring: harmonizer-latency, admission-rate-by-lane, credit-burn-rate, fairness-adjustments-per-minute, preemption-counts.
- Alerts: elevated soft-burst preemption > X/minute, harmonizer prediction error > threshold, persistent fairness thrashing (weight oscillation).
- Incident flow: if a tenant reports unexpected throttling, ops can replay decisions, temporally grant emergency credits, or pin a tenant to dedicated reserved nodes.

Metrics and success criteria
- SLOs: reduce P99 latency SLO breaches during bursts by 30% within 3 months of rollout on pilot tenants.
- Efficiency: decrease average idle reserved headroom across participating clusters by 15%.
- Predictability: 95% of admitted burst decisions should be explainable by the audit log with <5 properties.

Rollout plan (phased)
1) Canary: run harmonizer in shadow mode for a set of 3–5 tenant clusters for 4 weeks; compare decisions vs baseline and collect prediction quality.
2) Opt-in beta: surface per-tenant controls; allow customers to enable soft-burst and purchase credits.
3) Gradual enforcement: start enforcing admissions for non-critical clusters with ops guardrails.
4) Full launch: make harmonizer the default for new Dedicated regions; provide migration guidance.

Open questions / risks
- How to price burst credits to align incentives without punishing low-volume customers?
- How aggressive should preemption be for short-lived model tails (text-generation requests often have 1–3s tails)?
- Interaction with existing per-node autoscalers: do we implement an API for scale hints or a hard actuator?
- Security/abuse: can customers game the credit/forecast system by generating synthetic traffic? Need fraud detection signal.

records.title: Per-route/model/customer cost & latency heatmap indexer
records.text:
Per-route/model/customer cost & latency heatmap indexer

description:
Build a backend component that ingests streaming inference telemetry and materializes compact, queryable heatmap indices representing joint cost and latency distributions across three primary dimensions: route, model variant, and customer (tenant). The indexer will produce pre-aggregated tiles for the Console UI and APIs so customers can explore per-route and per-model cost/latency patterns by percentile and sequence-length buckets without scanning raw events.

motivation:
Current Console queries against raw rollups are slow and expensive for multi-dimensional slices (route x model x customer x seq_length). Product needs fast, interactive heatmap views to (1) surface anomalous routes that drive unit-cost regressions, (2) let customers correlate latency vs cost across model variants, and (3) power alerting/quality baselines for rollouts.

goals:
1) Produce a daily and hourly heatmap index for top N routes and on-demand for cold routes. 2) Keep index storage under 5% of existing rollup volume via sparse tiling + compression. 3) Provide query latency <200ms for top routes and <1s for ad-hoc tenant queries. 4) Quantile error <=2% for p50/p95/p99 estimations.

non_goals:
Per-request raw trace retention, full-fidelity token-level traces in the index, or replacing the canonical billing pipeline. This is a complementary fast view layer.

approach_summary:
Streaming ingestion from Kafka -> Flink (stream processor) for online incremental tiles + Beam batch job for backfill and compaction. Use t-digest per tile for quantiles, reservoir sampling for extreme tail preservation, and sparse matrix tiles keyed by (route_id, model_family, tenant_id, seq_bucket, time_bucket). Store tiles in ClickHouse for fast point reads and in S3 as compressed Parquet for longer-term backfill/repairs. Expose an HTTP indexer API for Console to fetch tile slices.

data_model_notes:
Tile key format: route:<route_id>|model:<model_sha_or_family>|tenant:<tenant_id>|time:<YYYY-MM-DDTHH>|seq_bucket:<0-12>. Each tile stores: count, token_count, t-digest(serialized base64), top_k_config_variants(list), cpu_gpu_seconds_estimate, compressed_kv_cache_hit_rate_est. Tiles are sparse and sharded by route hash to balance hot routes.

algorithm_tradeoffs:
We chose t-digest for compact quantile estimation (good for p50/p95/p99) at the expense of exact medians for tiny samples. Reservoir sampling retains tail-outliers but increases state for extremely high-throughput routes; mitigated by adaptive sampling cap per-tenant. Storing both an online ClickHouse hot-store and S3 cold-store makes queries fast but requires compaction jobs to avoid divergence.

infra_impact:
Flink job + ClickHouse retention increase estimated ~3 dedicated streaming workers and a ClickHouse shard increase (2 vnodes). S3 cost for Parquet tiles is expected to be ~1.8% of current telemetry storage. Will require autoscaling rules for spikes and improved schema registry coordination.

api_contracts:
GET /v1/insights/heatmap?route_id={}&model_family={}&tenant_id={}&start={}&end={}&resolution=hour|day returns JSON with grid metadata and base64 t-digest per cell. Accepts optional seq_bucket filter. Auth via existing Console token with tenant-scoped view.

acceptance_criteria:
- Hourly index produced for top-500 routes within 10 minutes of window close.
- Query latency <200ms 95th for top routes in ClickHouse.
- Quantile estimates within 2% of full-scan t-digest baseline for synthetic workloads.
- End-to-end tests covering ingestion->tile materialization->API.
- Console team integration demo completed and UX signoff.
- Monitoring: per-job lag, tile-drop rate, index size delta should be visible in grafana dashboards.

implementation_plan:
1) Prototype t-digest tile emitter in a feature branch and run against 7 days of replay (DEV cluster). 2) Implement Flink streaming operator to maintain per-tile state and emit checkpoints. 3) ClickHouse schema and API server for tile reads. 4) Beam batch compaction job to reconcile S3 and ClickHouse tiles. 5) Add E2E tests and dashboarding. 6) Canary deploy for 50 routes, validate correctness and perf, then expand to top-500.

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Hot routes explode state and slow Flink operator. Mitigation: route sharding + adaptive sampling + separate hot-path path that emits coarse tiles only.
Risk: T-digest divergence after compaction. Mitigation: deterministic merge tests and daily verification job.
Risk: ClickHouse cost. Mitigation: aggressive TTLs for non-top routes and move older tiles to S3.

work_log:
2026-02-22: Spike: ran 7-day replay with a t-digest tile prototype against dev telemetry; observed p95 error ~1.4% for ample samples. Saved prototype results: gs://redwood-dev/heatmap-spike/
2026-02-25: Design review with Console UX. Accepted tile size suggestion of 12 seq_length buckets x 5 percentile bands. Action: add seq_bucket cardinality to tile key. Notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/HEATMAP-INDEXER
2026-03-02: Architecture sync with infra. Decided on ClickHouse hot-store + S3 cold-store, Flink for online; infra to allocate 3 streaming workers initially. PR opened for schema: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-platform/pull/12345
2026-03-06: Implemented reservoir sampling cap per-route (default 10k samples/min). Ran load test; memory stable for top-200 routes. See load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/heatmap-loadtests
2026-03-09: PM feedback: prioritize tenant-scoped heatmaps in initial canary. Updated plan to canary 50 tenant-route pairs first.

comments:
Ravi: Pushed initial Flink operator prototype branch. Need infra to provision ClickHouse test shard before integration tests.
Sofia (Console PM): Important that API supports partial tiles for streaming UI; please include continuation cursors for large tenant queries.
Design (Marco): Suggested a color scale keyed to cost-per-token on the UI; backend will include aggregated cost-per-token metric in tile metadata.
Infra (Leah): Allocated staging ClickHouse + 3 Flink workers for the canary window 2026-03-15 -> 2026-03-22.

next_steps:
Finalize ClickHouse schema PR and get infra approval (owner: Ravi).
Add continuity cursor to index API and write Console client shim (owner: Console SDK).
Implement Beam compaction job for nightly reconciliation (owner: Data Eng).
Run canary for 50 tenant-route pairs starting 2026-03-15 and capture correctness/perf metrics.

notes:
This ticket is focused on the indexer component only; downstream billing reconciliations will reference this index but remain handled by the ledger pipeline. Expect follow-up tickets for per-tenant retention policies and UI guided exploration features.

records.title: customer-success
records.text:
customer-success

Maya Chen: Quick thread — I'm drafting a concise customer-facing enablement checklist for BrightBridge focused on caching, batching, streaming + account-health signals. This will be given to SEs during week-2 handoff and included in the customer enablement email. PTAL @Jonah @Elena @Ravi. Goal: reduce latency/cost while minimizing quality regressions.

Jonah Park: SGTM. A couple of quick defaults I recommend we call out up front: cache_ttl_short=60s for conversational prefixes, cache_ttl_long=24h for embeddings, and prefer idempotent prefix caching only for deterministic prompts. Mention token budget checks.

Elena Ruiz: Adding a tiny sample SDK + streaming example that we can paste into the customer doc:

```js
// Node SDK pseudocode - enable prefix cache + stream
const client = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY});
const stream = client.chat.stream({
  model: 'redwood-enc-2',
  cache: { prefix: true, ttl_seconds: 60 },
  batching: { max_batch_size: 8, max_latency_ms: 50 }
});
stream.on('data', chunk => process.stdout.write(chunk));
```

Elena Ruiz: And a curl SSE example for customers who use server-sent events:

```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-enc-2
```

Ravi Singh: On batching: start with max_batch_size=8 and max_latency_ms=50 for most web workloads. If customer qps > 200, switch to dynamic batching with adaptive backoff. Also include guidance: if p95 latency > 300ms with batching on, revert to single-call low-latency mode and file a perf ticket.

Maya Chen: Renewal-risk and account-health signals we should capture in the runbook: weekly active seats drop >30%, evaluation failure rate increase >5% (compare eval baseline), consistent billing anomalies (>=3x expected), and >2 open P1 incidents in 30 days. When any trigger hits, escalate to AM + Solutions and schedule a health-check call within 48h.

Lottie Marsh: For enablement coordination — recommend a 15-min checklist call with these agenda items: 1) quick architecture review, 2) cache & batch defaults, 3) streaming demo, 4) telemetry + feedback link. I can own scheduling and the call script.

Maya Chen: For feedback capture: include a short form we can send after week 1 with 3 quick metrics (latency satisfaction, quality thumbs up/down, any regressions). Example link placeholder: https://intra.redwood/feedback/brightbridge. Also add an opt-in prompt-sample library so SEs can repro and test.

Elena Ruiz: Telemetry naming convention suggestion: tags like `cs:onboard:cache`, `cs:onboard:batch`, `cs:onboard:stream` and an eval suite named `brightbridge_onboard_v1`. Add a short JSON example for telemetry events to paste into docs:

```json
{"event":"inference_request","tags":["cs:onboard:cache","brightbridge"],"latency_ms":42}
```

Jonah Park: Small note: call out safe-guard for caching with PII — prefix caching must be disabled if any input contains PII markers. Add sample filter rule in the doc.

Maya Chen: Plan: I'll compile this into a one-page enablement checklist + email template and post to Confluence. Jonah — can you finalize the code snippets? Ravi — please add the perf fallback steps. Lottie — will you own the renewal-monitoring thresholds and scheduling?

Lottie Marsh: :thumbsup: Assigning now. I'll also draft the 15-min script and the week-1 feedback form.

deploy-bot: Published page cs-enablement/brightbridge-v1 to Confluence (draft).

Maya Chen: Awesome — thanks everyone. Once Confluence is updated I'll attach the checklist to the customer record and create the monitoring alerts. If anyone wants to add short FAQs for customers (e.g., why streaming vs polling), drop them here and I'll fold them in.

Omar: FYI from today's Globex kickoff — they insist on per-tenant SLA gating + model tethering (ability to force traffic to their certified model) before we can move to pilot. They called it a security and compliance blocker.
Jules: Noted. Sounds like a combo of feature parity + policy surface. Competitor ships "model tether" and per-tenant SLA enforcement. We should map minimal acceptance criteria.
Priya: Sales asks: 1) API to tether a tenant to a model 2) ability to specify SLO thresholds (latency/cost) that trigger routing/alerts 3) daily token-by-tenant CSVs 4) an immutable audit trail for tethering changes.
Nina: Two engineering paths: implement a lightweight "tether" flag on route configs + export hooks, or full per-tenant sandboxing + scheduler. Lightweight path is doable as an alpha.
Omar: Launch criteria for Globex pilot (proposal): a) tenant tether API + console toggle b) SLO rule engine (simple thresholds) c) export of tenant/model/token usage d) p99 latency for tethered requests < 250ms e) audit events persisted and downloadable.
Jules: Perf note — naive per-request lookup and auth-time policy fetch adds ~25-60ms. Mitigations: embed tether info in tenant JWT at auth-time, or compile an in-memory map refreshed on policy change. Spike required.
Priya: Globex wants a signed pilot commitment if we can ship tether + exports within 3 weeks. They accept alpha UX and a documented roadmap to full sandboxing in Q3.
Nina: Proposal for immediate plan: Spike (Jules) 7d to validate p99 with in-memory map vs auth-time attach; Implement tether API (Nina) 1 sprint; Export hook (Priya) 1 sprint; Minimal console toggle (Omar) 1 sprint.
Omar: API sketch for tethering (alpha):
```json
POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/tether
{
  "model": "redwood/gpt-medium-v2",
  "effective_from": "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z",
  "reason": "compliance",
  "created_by": "omar@redwood"
}
```
Response returns tether_id + audit_id.
Jules: Also recommend tagging every request with telemetry: tenant_id, tethered_model (if any), routing_decision, reason_code. That will help product prioritize native features.
Priya: I'll draft Globex pilot letter with the 3-week alpha commitment and a Q3 roadmap milestone for full per-tenant sandboxing. Sales wants explicit rollback windows and an SLA hangar clause.
Nina: Security: need mTLS or signed JWT for any on-prem model endpoints if we add proxying later. For tethering, ensure policy changes are write-audited and require 2FA for prod toggles.
Omar: Owners & dates: Spike (Jules) - 7d, Tether API (Nina) - sprint, Export CSV (Priya) - sprint, Console toggle mock (Omar) - 4d, Pilot letter (Priya) - 3d.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Dedicated pool 'lucid-health-dedicated-1' node gpu-node-17 reporting sustained ECC and correctable memory errors. Affected pool: lucidhealth-dedicated (customer: LucidHealth, VPC). Severity: P2. Page sent to on-call SRE.

alex chen: acked. jumping in. starting triage.

raj singh: thanks alex. pulling task placements. looks like 3 LucidHealth model-serving pods on that node (serving-lg-onnx-01, reranker-02, task-embed-03). One is currently at ~85% GPU mem.

sophie li: passing note — this pool is reserved for LucidHealth (contracted capacity). we need to avoid any data crossing tenants; don't migrate pods to non-dedicated pools. plan should prefer other GPUs in the same dedicated pool.

alex chen: agree. immediate plan: cordon node and drain with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` after ensuring replicas on other GPUs in same pool. I'm going to check if there are valid placement targets.

infra-bot: Autoscaler snapshot: dedicated pool lucidhealth-dedicated has 8 total GPUs across 4 nodes, 2 spare GPUs currently available (pending autoscaler thresholds). No active scaling operations.

mira patel: quick customer impact check: are there request errors now or just degraded perf?

se-lucidhealth: (LucidHealth SE): we see increased errors in our dashboards too. We have live inference traffic for health-check endpoints, some retries are happening. Please advise on impact windows.

alex chen: brief to SE: we're going to cordon and try to drain and relocate pods to other GPUs in your dedicated pool. That may cause short connection drops (<30s) during restart. We'll coordinate more if we need to evict with force.

raj singh: validating replica counts and affinity: two of the three pods have nodeAffinity tied to dedicated pool labels only, so they can land on other nodes in the pool. Good. One pod is hostNetworked (can't be moved) — it's an edge case, might need manual failover within the app.

alex chen: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17` -> node cordoned.

deploy-bot: Rolling drain job scheduled: drift-id 4f7c. Expected pod restarts: 5.

sophie li: notifying account manager to prepare a customer message if we see >5 minutes sustained errors. @se-lucidhealth FYI.

alex chen: doing the drain...

alex chen: drain progress: 2/3 pods terminated and successfully rescheduled on gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-14. hostNetwork pod (serving-lg-onnx-01) is still on gpu-node-17 and did not reschedule due to hostNetwork requirement. It's the one causing the 5xxs.

infra-bot: Node-level memory errors persist. Kernel Xid errors continuing. Hardware vendor recommended creating a hardware ticket and evacuating node.

alex chen: I'm going to mark the node in 'maintenance' and open a hardware replacement ticket with vendor. Meanwhile we'll update routing to fallback to reduce customer error rate.

alex chen: patching routing for LucidHealth: set route for reranker service to fallback model (cfg: reranker-v2-q4) with lower memory profile. Apply now.

deploy-bot: Route update applied for reranker -> reranker-v2-q4.

Some requests may see brief increased latency while we complete failover." Send after we have acceptance?

alex chen: after routing change, 5xx rate down from 4.8% -> 0.9% in 3 minutes. latency P95 improved to ~420ms. looks stable but node errs continue.

raj singh: I'm creating a ticket to hardware vendor: Ticket LU-1905-17 - GPU ECC spike on gpu-node-17. Attaching `dmesg` and nvidia logs. Recommend immediate replacement.

records.text:
slack/architecture/1745670001-delegate-escrow-proxy-rfc-followup.json

Marisa: Quick recap from the lease-swap sims 1: we saw lost-in-flight writes when ownership flipped mid-request. Proposal: proxy escrow + delegate forward. Proxy persists a short-lived escrow and replays to eventual owner instead of synchronous lease handoff. Thoughts?

alex: This should prevent lost writes but adds tail latency and small storage. How do we avoid duplicates?

marisa: Each write gets a signed write_token and shard_seq. Target uses token + seq window for idempotent apply.

devon: Residency: EU-only tenants cannot be forwarded outside region. Escrow must carry residency_policy and proxy must enforce it.

marisa: If no allowed destination, mark escrow QUARANTINED and surface to ops via incident.

sam: Risk: proxy crash during failover could lose escrow. How durable is this?

marisa: Escrow stored locally with sync replication to one standby proxy (replication=2). Metadata index async-shipped to control plane for visibility. TTL short (default 180s).

nina: Metrics to add: escrow_active, escrow_forward_p95, quarantined_count, replay_failures. Also trace IDs per forward.

alex: Client contract? Blocking vs non-blocking behavior?

marisa: Default returns 202 + write_token after escrow commit. Background forwarder applies. Provide sync=true for callers that need strong commit. Client can poll status or subscribe via webhook using write_token.

devon: SLOs: default completion p95 < 30s, alert if >2m, quarantine after 5m. These numbers will drive autoscaling tests.

sam: Ordering across concurrent writes?

marisa: Include shard_seq_range in escrow payload. Target checks for gaps and can request gap-fetch before applying replay.

nina: Audit: log forward attempts (who, when, result) and export to long-term audit store for compliance.

alex: Edge case: forward loop when owner_hint stale. Need handshake and clear retry cap.

marisa: Handshake: forwarder POSTs /handoff with token; target validates signature & ownership. On mismatch return 409 + owner_hint. Backoff + retry_limit=5 then escalate. Example: POST /handoff {"write_token":"wt-ff12","shard":"s-7","seq_span":[9001,9003],"residency":"eu-only"}

ops-bot: [automation] defaults: escrow_replication=2; ttl_secs=180; forward_retry_limit=5; quarantine_retention_days=14.

sam: What if tenant deletes data while write is escrowed?

marisa: Deletes are ops with seq numbers. Replay applies in seq order; tombstone first means replayed write is deduped/skipped.

devon: Rollout plan?

marisa: Feature flag -> dark launch metrics -> small canary for non-sovereign tenants -> expand with legal signoff. Gate each step on escrow backlog and error rate.

nina: I will sketch dashboard tiles for escrow volume, forward latency, and quarantines.

alex: Implementation estimate: 4-6w core + 2w integration + runbook.

marisa: I'll draft a short RFC patch with token spec, escrow contract, sample handshake, and rollout checklist. Prototype in staging for low-risk tenants first. Tagging @alex @devon @sam @nina.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: SEV2 - Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed for customer NimblePay on dedicated cluster dc-us-west-2-7. Alert fingerprints: 5xx-rate>5% over 5m, gateway-524 spikes. Paging SRE oncall.
Alice (oncall): I got the page, looking at dashboards now. Can someone paste the raw alert links?
Ben R. (eng-runtime): logs: https://grafana/reports/alerts/3895001234 - main signal is 5xx from inference-gateway returning 524/502. Backend runtime showing queued_inflight spike and kv-cache eviction rate up 20x.
Alice (oncall): kv evictions? that's usually noisy tenant. Carmen, can you check cluster allocation and pod restarts?
Carmen P. (platform): checking k8s. Node pool nodegroup-dc7 has 3 nodes with high GPU mem and high CPU steal. A few pods in pool-dc7-runtime are OOM/killed in past 12m: pod/runtime-xyz restartCount=6.
Raj (CS): NimblePay says their customers are seeing errors in prod, some long-running batches. They've opened a ticket and want ETA. I told them we're investigating.
Alice (oncall): Ok primary impacts: (1) 5xx from gateway to customer model routes, (2) elevated request latency, (3) some 524 upstream timeouts. Short-term: throttle the noisy tenant if we can, apply circuit breaker on their heavy routes, and add routing fallback for critical NimblePay endpoints to a degraded model variant.
Ben R. (eng-runtime): I can push a tenant throttle via internal CLI. Command:
```
redwoodctl tenant throttle --tenant nimblepay --qps 10 --duration 30m
```
that will shed excessive concurrency from tenant while preserving low-rate requests.
Taylor (rotating-oncall): I can run that now if Alice approves.
Alice (oncall): Do it. Also start a temporary canary route: map nimblepay-critical -> model-x-small (lower mem, faster kernel) for 5% of traffic. Ben, can you add that route?
Ben R. (eng-runtime): Creating route:
```
redwoodctl routes create --tenant nimblepay --route critical-fallback --model model-x-small --pct 5
```
Applying... done. Traffic shift started.
ops-bot: action-log: tenant throttle applied (nimblepay) by Taylor at 3895001305, route critical-fallback created by Ben R. at 3895001320.
Carmen P. (platform): I'm adding capacity: spinning up 2 more nodes in nodegroup-dc7 (G5xlarge equivalent). kubernetes autoscaler is at max for that pool. Running:
```
kubectl scale nodegroup nodegroup-dc7 --replicas=5
```
Request submitted to infra, ETA ~4-6 minutes to new nodes ready.
Alice (oncall): While nodes come up, check KV cache hit rates per tenant. If nimblepay is causing prefix churn, we should increase cache limits for other tenants temporarily.
Ben R. (eng-runtime): Prom query for evictions:
```
sum(rate(runtime_kv_evictions_total[1m])) by (tenant)
```
Output: nimblepay=128/s, tenant-foo=2/s, tenant-bar=1/s. Confirmed nimblepay dominating evictions.
Alice (oncall): That's the noisy neighbor right there. Throttle should cut that. Monitor 5xx-rate and queue depth.
Taylor (rotating-oncall): After throttle, 2m in: 5xx rate dropped from 12% -> 6%, queue depth down 40%. Still above baseline.
Raj (CS): NimblePay acknowledges some routes now succeed, but they report intermittent timeouts for large payloads. They want a rough timeline.
Alice (oncall): Tell them: immediate mitigations applied (throttle, fallback route, extra nodes requested). Expect progressive improvement over 10-20 minutes. We'll follow up with RCA and next steps.
Ben R. (eng-runtime): I also pushed a quick kernel tweak to the runtime to prefer smaller-batch execution for nimblepay routes to reduce memory pressure. Patch:
```
// runtime config snippet
{ "tenant": "nimblepay", "batching": { "mode": "minibatch", "max_batch_size": 8 } }
```
Patch activated at 3895001402.
Alice (oncall): Nice. Any signs of other tenants impacted?
Carmen P. (platform): No collateral evictions increase. New nodes are registering: node-9 and node-10 up, pods scheduled. GPU utilization per node dropping as we redistribute.
ops-bot: cluster-scaler: node-9 ready at 3895001580, node-10 ready at 3895001643.
Taylor (rotating-oncall): 15m after mitigations: 5xx rate stabilized at 2.1% (target <1%), gateway 524 spikes down to baseline. Queue depth back to normal.
Alice (oncall): Great. I'm going to keep this thread open for a bit, but let's move to incident summary once stable. Raj, please confirm customer status and any outstanding requests.
Raj (CS): NimblePay confirms their error rate dropped significantly, still seeing rare timeouts for very large requests. They've asked for a timeframe for permanent fixes.
Ben R. (eng-runtime): Permanent fix options: (A) tenant-side rate limits + batching improvements, (B) tenant isolation via dedicated pool (paid), (C) improved eviction fairness in KV with tenant-weighting. I'll draft proposals.
Carmen P. (platform): For short term, we should add an automated throttle policy when a tenant causes >50x eviction delta in 5m. That would auto-shield others. I filed a ticket: ENG-INC-3895.
Alice (oncall): Can you create postmortem checklist? I'll mark incident as mitigated once we have customer confirm and 30m stability.
Taylor (rotating-oncall): Logging final metrics here: pre-mitigation 5xx=12.4%, queue_depth=420, evictions_total_rate=160/s; post-mitigation 5xx=1.9%, queue_depth=30, evictions=4/s.
Alice (oncall): Marking status: mitigated -> partial (customer degraded but majority traffic healthy). Will transition to follow-up.
ops-bot: incident-status: mitigated at 3895004321 by Alice. Next: postmortem owners: Ben R. (runtime), Carmen P. (platform), Raj (CS) to coordinate customer comms.
Raj (CS): I'll schedule a 1:1 with NimblePay for RCA and remediation options.
Ben R. (eng-runtime): I'll start a runbook PR: automatic tenant throttling + eviction detection. Expected ETA for PR: 3 days.
Carmen P. (platform): I'll add an autoscaler policy change to allow temporary burst capacity without manual intervention; PR ETA 5 days.
Alice (oncall): Thanks team. Closing real-time operations. We'll reconvene for the postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
